At 7:30 p.m. on June 10, 2020, an employee who had worked as a Licensed

On Friday, March 19, 2021, an employee was working at a sawmill. He was the day
shift millwright. He had 21 to 30 years' experience. The facility had two
continuous dry kilns, or CDK machines, for drying sawdust. Moist sawdust
traveled through a rotary fuel feeder into each kiln. This sawdust was rotated
and dried, dumped into a blow line, and transferred to a silo. The sawdust in
the silo was then used as fuel. The two CDKs, CDK 5 and CDK 6, were beside each
other. Each had a rotary valve to rotate the sawdust within. The rotary valve
was behind a door, fastened to the machine with bolts. It occasionally happened
that a rotary valve became jammed with debris, in which case maintenance by an
authorized employee was required. There was one control panel for both CDKs,
located alongside CDK 5. There were two 460/480 volt electrical disconnects, one
mounted above the other on a uni-strut next to CDK 6. One disconnect had a hand
written "5" and a label that read, "VTM6 Rotary Valve 2." The other disconnect
had a handwritten "6" and a label that read, "VTM2 Rotary Valve 1." Before 6:45
a.m., the employee was notified by an alarm of a default in one of the CDKs. He
responded. He determined that rotary valve 2 for CDK 5 was not running. When a
fault occurred, an employee had to reset the fault on the control panel. The
millwright locked out the rotary feeder to clear the debris, but he
inadvertently locked out rotary valve 1 on CDK 6, not rotary valve 2 on CDK 5.
The disconnect for CDK 5 had not been deenergized. The employee removed the
maintenance door to the feeder, to find debris and sawdust blocking the view of
the feeder's fan vanes. The employee reached into the opening with his right
hand to wipe away the debris and get a better view. The tip of his right middle
finger contacted the vanes, which were still rotating. The moving vanes pushed
his finger into a knife. The employee's middle right fingertip was amputated.
The employee was treated without hospitalization.
At 4:00 p.m. on March 22, 2021, Employee #1 was driving a residential garbage

At 9:15 a.m. on February 20, 2021, Employee #1 was working for a roofing

the employee was moved to the ICU due to pneumonia. On February 11, 2021, the

At 2:52 p.m. on June 25, 2021, an employee was using a forklift to move a
wrecked vehicle to a new location within a salvage yard. The employee used the
forklift to pull the vehicle by raising the front with the forklift tines and

At 5:39 p.m. on June 25, 2021, an employee was doing general landscaping

but the employee had died from blunt force trauma to the neck and head caused by
the fall.
At 12:30 p.m. on June 4, 2021, Employee #1 was filling a propane cylinder from a
propane nursing/storage tank. The employee's hand was exposed to liquid propane
released from the pressure relief valve. The exposure caused a frostbite-type
burn due to the extremely low temperature of the liquid propane. The employee
was treated without hospitalization.

15, 2020, the employee was tested for COVID-19 but received a negative test

trees that were being thinned and cut down. The employee became confused and

employee was transported to the hospital, where the employee died of
heat-related illness.
At 11:00 a.m. on June 26, 2021, an employee was operating a tractor mowing grass
in an orchard. When the employee did not arrive home as expected a neighbor went
to look for him and found the employee dead. Heat was suspected of being a

At 8:15 a.m. on June 14, 2021, Employee #1 was trimming dashboard parts using

An employee was working at a medical center when he was exposed to a coworker
that was infected with COVID-19 in a meeting room. The employee was tested for
COVID-19 on December 16, 2020, which returned a positive result. The employee
was hospitalized on December 25, 2020, but successfully recovered from his
infection.
At 11:16 a.m. on December 16, 2020, Employee #1 was performing tree trimming
work while positioned 30 feet above the ground. During the task, Employee #1's
safety belt gave out, causing him to lose attachment to the tree. He fell onto a
branch before continuing to fall to the ground, landing on his back. Emergency
services transported the employee to the hospital, where he was treated for a
mild vertebra fracture and a small intracranial hemorrhage. The employee was
hospitalized.
At 9:00 a.m. on May 26, 2020, an employee working as an automotive technician
for an autobody shop was attempting to vent compressed natural gas tanks
situated on top of a city bus. The employee was preparing to replace potentially
defective pressure relief devices (PRD) as a part of a recall retrofit. The
employee did not ground the bus at its grounding point. The employee also did
not defuel the bus utilizing the defueling instructions on the bus. The employee
attempted to heat up the PRDs using a heat gun to a temperature that would cause
the PRDs to activate and vent the tanks. While performing this task, a sudden
flash fire occurred, burning the employee and destroying the bus, as well as the
two busses parked next to it. The most likely contributing factors to this
accident were, lack of proper grounding, lack of proper procedures for defueling
the bus, and hazardous method employed to pop off potentially defective PRDs to
vent the tanks quickly. The employee sustained 2nd and 3rd degree burns to his
arms and hands and was hospitalized.
At 12:00 p.m. on June 23, 2021, an employee working for a paper products
manufacturer was removing debris from a paste pad. The employee opened the
interlocked doors to access the paste pad. The employee contacted the moving
agitator gear with his right pinky finger. The employee received medical
treatment without hospitalization for a lacerated fingertip which was medically
classified as an amputation.
At 8:00 a.m. on June 28, 2021, an employee and a coworker were using a STIHL RB
600 pressure washer on the exterior of a forty foot molasses tank. The employees
utilized a makeshift basket elevated on the forks of a Komatsu FD25TU-16
Forklift to reach the top of the tank. The employee proceeded to acquire a
defective Werner twelve foot aluminum ladder from inside the facility and
utilize it in the basket to increase his reach. The coworker had left to use the
restroom while the employee climbed the ladder and continued pressure washing
the tank. The employee slipped off the ladder and fell approximately twenty-five
feet landing on a pipe that was laying on the ground. The employee sustained
fatal head and neck trauma and was killed.
At 1:35 p.m. on August 27, 2020, an employee who worked as a Registerd Nurse for

overseeing a patient that was transferred into the facility when she was

Aerosol Transmissible Diseases policies and procedures in place.
At 8:30 a.m. on June 28, 2021, an employee had been watering dirt roads when he

ground and was found unresponsive by coworkers. The employee had suffered a
heart attack and died.
At 3:56 p.m. on May 24, 2021, an employee fell approximately sixteen feet from a
roof. The employee was transported to the hospital for treatment and later died.
An employee worked as a General Laborer for a manufacturer of plastic beverage

machine while the belt was powered on. The employee's hand became caught between

At 11:00 a.m. on June 15, 2021, an employee working as a machine maintenance

Ranger utility truck owned by the cooperative. It had the coop's serial number
2051, VIN 3C7WRNBL3GG275387, and Florida license plate GBR007. The employee had

tree limb and vegetation pulled down and pinned the primary and neutral
conductors across the top of the insulated bucket. At some point, the employee

found with no vital signs. He had been electrocuted. He hadn't opened the S&C
trip saver device downstream. There was no evidence that he had attached any
grounds upstream and downstream before he began cutting the branches with the
fiberglass cable cutters. There was no evidence that he had verified the absence
of voltage on the line prior to working on the line. The employee did not have
on and was not using adequate electrical protective equipment, in the form of
rated rubber gloves.

attention several times. Despite the warning, the employee continued to cut the
trunk. As the trunk fell, the rope struck the employee on his upper left leg.
The employee was lowered from the tree with the assistance of the crew on the
ground. An ambulance was called and the employee was taken to the hospital. The
employee was hospitalized to treat a fractured femur and fibula and soft tissue
damage to his knee.
At 5:25 p.m. on July 5, 2021, an employee set up plastic sheeting to cover an

employee slipped, fell approximately twenty-two feet, and was killed.
At 3:15 p.m. on June 28, 2021, an employee was felling a forty foot palmetto

At 4:30 p.m. on December 4, 2020, an employee was working for a firm that

on the asphalt or railroad track and fell into the drain, where the hot water
was accumulating. He suffered burns to the left side of his body. His foreman
immediately came to his aide and administered first aid. The foreman had the

wounds. The employee suffered second- and third-degree burns to his left side,

performed an amputation of the thumb.
At approximately 2:15 p.m. on December 17, 2020, Employee #1 was cutting a piece

At approximately 1:26 p.m. on April 1, 2021, an employee was  working on top of

At 9:41 a.m. on June 20, 2021, an employee was working as a heavy equipment

At 4:15 p.m. on March 2, 2021, an employee was standing on the roof when the

fractured left leg and was hospitalized.
At 1:00 p.m. on August 14, 2020, an employee working as an electrician for an

employee grabbed hold of a pin from the manhole lid to steady himself. The pin

employee was hospitalized to treat a fractured back and dislocated shoulder.
At 10:15 a.m. on February 23, 2021, Employee #1 was using a band saw to cut

employee was hospitalized for treatment.
At 2:45 p.m. on June 8, 2021, an employee was working for a firm that engaged in

At approximately 12:00 p.m. on November 11, 2020, an employee started

At approximately 7:45 a.m. on February 21, 2020, an employee was scrapping

An employee's last day of work was February 27, 2021, with symptoms appearing on

At approximately 4:00 p.m. on July 15, 2020, an employee was working as an RN

On June 10, 2021, an employee was working for a firm that designed and

At approximately 6:00 a.m. on September 12, 2014, an employee was walking on the

At approximately 9:00 a.m. on May 12, 2021, an employee was working in the

At 10:00 a.m. on June 17, 2021, an employee conducted roofing work walked on the

An employee was conducting sleep studies in an enclosed office space in close

At 10:30 a.m. on May 7, 2021, Employee #1 was assisting a garbage truck as it

At 12:04 p.m. on Friday, June 18, 2021, an employee was working for a firm that

apron and, while using his double-gloved hand to remove the obstruction, his

At 6:45 a.m. on May 28, 2021, Employee #1 was operating a forklift inside a

At 4:30 p.m. on April 22, 2021, at a chicken breading facility, an employee was

An employee was working on communications systems in residential homes

At 9:30 a.m. on June 3, 2021, an employee worked from a scissor lift to secure

At 11:15 a.m. on May 20, 2021, Employee #1 was operating a forwarder across a

An employee was a temporary worker in a three-week training program. The

An employee was a Sales Consultant who worked at a new and used car dealership.

was intrinsically safe. Before placing the vacuum system into operation, the
employer did not verify and record that the system was adequately grounded in
accordance with Article 250 of the National Electric Code. The supervisor did
not conduct a resistance test on the vacuum or boxes.

injuries and was treated without hospitalization.  The machine should have been
off when she was sanitizing the dough wrapper. Additionally, the employee

At 11:00 a.m. on November 5, 2020, an employee, a chief building supervisor, was
taking his break, when he decided to go outside for some fresh air.  He walked

down the first flight of stairs onto the landing. When the employee was walking

extension ladder on the sag span of an 18-ft high communication cable in an

At 8:39 a.m. on June 22, 2020, an employee was setting up a vertical broach

ram to drift downward during the set-up, catching the employee's fingers in
between the cutter pieces. As a result, the employee's fingers were caught in
the pinch point between two cutters.  During set-up, the hydraulic ram was not
mechanically blocked or locked out to prevent inadvertent movement, and the
employee was not provided with extension tools or an alternate means to protect
himself from injury due to such movement. Also, at some point during the
accident, an e-stop was engaged, which caused the machine to lose all power and
trapped the employee's fingers in between the cutters even longer. The employee
could not free himself and had to wave down passing employees to get assistance.
The employee suffered an amputation of two fingers on the left hand.  The
employee was hospitalized.
At 10:30 a.m. on August 26, 2020, an employee was trimming plants at the
facility. The hedge got stuck with the plant. The employee tried to remove the
debris with his finger and at the same time pushed the power button. The
employee suffered a left index finger amputation and was treated without
hospitalization.

At 1:33 p.m. on April 10, 2021 an employee was harvesting strawberries when he

An employee was working for a city police department when she contracted

An employee was working as a police officer in a city police department when she

An employee was working as a police officer in a city police department when she

On March 29, 2021, an employee was felling a large ash tree. During the felling

In early 2021, a 72-year-old woman employee was working at a nursing care or

At 3:00 p.m. on March 8, 2021, Employee # 1 was doing office work. He contracted

using climbing gear. While working, the employee lost his balance and fell from
the tree to the ground. Emergency services were called, and the employee was
transported to the hospital, where he was admitted and treated for multiple
broken bones and a broken back.
At 3:30 p.m. on June 1, 2021, an employee was removing Arrow Panel Traffic Signs
from a roadway when a vehicle hit one of the traffic signs causing traffic sign
to strike the employee. The employee suffered a head injury and was killed.
At 11:00 a.m. on June 1, 2021, an employee and a coworker were attempting to
untangle flag pole lines. The employee was standing on a 14 inch wide flagpole
base approximately 3 feet off the ground when he lost his balance. The employee
fell backward to the ground below and hit his head on the concrete walkway
causing a brain injury and later dies.
An employee was working as a conductor on a public transportation system when he
was exposed to passengers potentially infected with COVID-19. The employee

An employee was a conductor for a public transportation system when he was

On May 5, 2020, five employees who had been providing direct care to patients
were reported hospitalized due to COVID-19 infection after testing positve for
the virus. Employees had reported inadequate training for nurses on how to

breakroom and lack of adherence to CDC infection control guidelines. Adequate
Aerosol Transmissible Diseases policies and procedures were found to not be in
place. The dates, times and further details leading up to exposures are not
indicated in the narrative.
An employee was working as a Registered Nurse who provided patient care at a
hospital. While working, the employee had all PPE available to her including
mask, gloves, gowns, shields, and other. The employee had received safety and
illness training and had been complying with the use of PPE throughout her
shifts. The employee started to have symptoms of COVID-19 on November 13, 2020,
which included fever, and body aches. The employee notified the employer of her
illness and did not go to work. On November 29, 2020, the employee was
hospitalized with COVID-19 until December 1, 2020.
At 2:21 p.m. on December 15, 2020, Employee #1 was carrying a pole brace with
another employee when he slipped on a slurry water mix and fell backwards.
During the fall, the brace pole landed on top of Employee #1, causing a back
injury. The employee was hospitalized for treatment.
At approximately 9:30 a.m. on May 28, 2021, an employee went to retrieve a
monitor from the vehicle.  He was found dead in a stairwell. The employee died
from a heart attack.
At 10:15 a.m. on June 2, 2021, an employee worked to sand and touch up paint
around an elevator shaft door and trim. At some point, the employee fell
approximately thirty-four feet through the opening and was killed.
At 11:00 a.m. on January 10, 2021, an employee was going to get her lunch from
her locker. She lost her balance and fell, resulting in a broken hip. The
employee was hospitalized.
At 7:15 a.m. on May 28, 2021, Employee #1 was cleaning residual food from a drum
former machine. While using his right hand to clean the equipment, his hand was
caught in a pinch point, resulting in amputation of the right middle fingertip.
The employee was treated without hospitalization.
At 5:00 p.m. on May 24, 2021, Employee #1 was engaged in firefighting activities
when he began experiencing symptoms of heat illness. The incident occurred under
conditions of ambient heat combined with radiating heat from the fire. Employee
#1 was hospitalized for treatment of heat exhaustion.
At 12:00 a.m. on April 26, 2021, an employee had a possible heart attack and
coworkers then unsuccessfully attempted Cardio Pulmonary Resuscitation (CPR).
The employee was transported to the hospital, where medical staff pronounced the
employee dead.
On February 2, 2021, an employee who worked for a respiratory equipment rental
company died from COVID-19. The employee tested positive for COVID-19 on
December 31, 2021. The employer appeared to be complying with CDC guidance at
the time the employee tested positive. The investigation was not able to show
that the employee contracted COVID-19 through workplace exposure.
An employee was working in a nursing home when he tested positive for COVID-19
on May 18, 2021. The employee was admitted to the hospital on May 21, 2021 and
died on May 22, 2021.
At 10:14 p.m. on May 3, 2021, an employee working as a machine operator for a

was cutting pieces of channel metal when he reached over a barricade to push a
piece of the metal into the shuttle vise clamp area. As the employee pushed the

fingers between the channel metal and the shuttle vise. The employee received
medical treatment without hospitalization for an approximately 1 inch amputation
of his ring finger and crush injuries to the ring finger and  the other finger.
At 5:02 p.m. on January 21, 2021, Employee #1 and a coworker were performing

collect the material being dropped down the chute and place the material in a

An employee was working as a resident supervisor for a firm that housed people
who had crossed the border from Mexico into the United States. The residents
were housed until suitable housing had been found for them. The employee
contracted COVID-19. Several of the residents tested positive for COVID-19, and
the employer assumed that the employee contracted COVID-19 at work because of
this. The employee tested positive for COVID-19 on April 17, 2021. He was
hospitalized on April 27, 2021. At 5:30 a.m. on May 19, 2021, he died.
An employee was working as a computer programmer for a metal service center and
wholesaler of other metals. A proxy bracelet he wore identified him as having
been within 6 feet (1.8 meters) of a coworker for more than 15 minutes within a
24-hour period of the colleague's having tested positive for COVID-19. Following
that, the employee was quarantined. His last day at work was April 19, 2021.
During his quarantine, the employee experienced difficulty breathing. He was
admitted to the hospital. At 8:00 a.m. on May 15, 2021, he died during his
hospitalization. He had also tested positive for COVID-19, and he died from
complications related to COVID-19.
At 2:30 p.m. on November 25, 2020, an employee from a temporary labor agency was
working at a pasta manufacturing plant located in Yuba City, CA. He was assigned
as the machine operator for a ravioli filling and forming machine, ANKO
HLT-700XL, in the production area of the facility.  The employee observed that
finished pasta products were sticking to the rotating cutter at the discharge
end of the machine. Without deenergizing the machine, he put his hand near the
rotating cutter in an attempt to dislodge the product. The middle and ring
fingertips on his right hand sustained crushing injuries, resulting in muscle
and bone loss. He was taken by ambulance to Adventist Health Rideout Hospital in
Marysville, CA, where he was treated and released. He was referred to an
orthopedic specialist for outpatient surgery.
At 3:40 p.m. on April 10, 2021, Employee #1 was manually feeding wood into a
bench table saw when the saw blade lacerated his finger. The employee was using
his hands to push the material through the saw. The table saw did not have a
guard, and a push stick or push block was used. As a result of the injury, the
employee sustained a fingertip amputation. The employee was transported to the
hospital for admission and treatment.
On January 8, 2021, an employee was working on either a step ladder or similar
A-frame ladder when he fell for unknown reasons. The employee suffered a
concussion and later died.
At 10:00 a.m. on January 28, 2021, Employee #1, employed by a roofing
contractor, was working at the site of a single family residence.  He was
loading tree stumps into a dump truck when he tripped and fell over cinder
blocks.  The employee sustained a fractured leg.  The employee was transported
to the hospital and admitted for treatment of the fracture.
At 2:15 p.m. on May 5, 2021, Employee #1 was working alone to clean a blocked
exhaust duct on an edge banding machine. The machine had been turned off, and
the guard door was lifted to allow access. Employee #1 inserted his right hand
into the machine to clear the duct. While doing so, something cut between his
right index and middle fingers, leaving scrapes on the side of his middle finger
and deeply cutting the base of his index finger at the MCP joint, leaving it
hanging by a layer of skin. Employee #1 applied gauze and went to the emergency
room. Surgery revealed that the finger was no longer viable, and it was
amputated. The employee believes the injury may have been caused by a sharp edge
on the saw motor housing, although it could not be reproduced. Medical records
indicate the injury was caused by a saw, with multiple cuts to the finger.
Employee #1 was hospitalized.
An employee was working for a bus sales company when he attended a sales
conference and contracted COVID-19. The employee reported symptoms and tested
positive for COVID-19 two days after the conference ended. The employee was
admitted to the hospital four days later and died on May 16, 2021, due to
complications of the infection.
At 11:35 p.m. on March 25, 2021, an employee was walking near the loading dock
when a box truck backed into him, pinning him between the truck and the loading
dock. As a result, the employee sustained a dislocated tailbone, a minor
fracture to L5, and bruised intestines.    The employee was hospitalized for
treatment. The incident occurred when the truck reversed and struck the
employee.
At approximately 12:00 p.m. on April 29, 2021, an employee was outside walking
to their car. Unknown what happened perhaps a fall, the employee had an open leg
fracture and bleeding from his head. The employee died from these injuries.

hand. The employee was treated without hospitalization.

buildup of the wire, he started pulling the wire placing his hand beyond the
guard. The employee caught his left-hand fingertips between the wire and the
capstan. The employee received medical treatment without hospitalization for
amputations to his 2nd and 3rd fingers above the top knuckle on the left hand.
At 10:30 p.m. on April 14, 2021, Employee #1 was retrieving fallen parts on a
mold machine. While picking up parts from the top of the machine, Employee #1
accidentally dropped a part into the mold. As the employee attempted to retrieve
the part, the mold closed, pinching the fingertips of the right index, middle,
and ring fingers. Employee #1 sustained fingertip amputations and was
hospitalized for treatment.
At 2:45 p.m. on May 4, 2021, an employee working as a precision woodworker for a

The employee was drilling holes into 1-inch by 2-inch wood for a cabinet frame
assembly. The employee had placed his right hand beyond the improperly guarded
point of operation when the machine cycled. The employee crushed his middle
finger between the pneumatic clamp and the wood piece. The employee received
medical treatment without hospitalization for a partially amputated fingertip
involving only the flesh with no bone loss.
At 5:00 a.m. on March 11, 2021, Employee #1, employed at a food processing
facility, was sanitizing a Bridge Machine Co. meat tenderizer, Model CS-12. A
water hose was used to clean the machine, which was in run mode. When she opened

button, she lost her balance and grabbed the machine to steady herself. Her
left-hand glove became caught in the rotating gear, resulting in the amputation
of her left middle fingertip.  Employee #1 was hospitalized for treatment.

second- and third-degree burns to the legs and torso and was hospitalized. A
second employee, located farther from the vapor's path, sustained minor burns
and was treated and released the same day.
At 2:20 a.m. on April 16, 2021, Employee #1 was waiting for a conveying assembly
line to shut down when he saw a piece of cardboard stuck near a drive roller.
The employee reached to remove the cardboard, and his left middle fingertip was

was treated without hospitalization.

mediation at a local community college, which included 14 participants.
Following the mediation, the employee and a coworker contracted COVID-19. The
employer did not have an effective COVID-19 Prevention Program in place.
At 2:00 p.m. on March 25, 2021, an employee was performing maintenance on a

shattered left femur and hip socket. Emergency services transported the employee

At 11:30 a.m. on April 12, 2021, an employee working as a machine maintenance

Employee #1 was treated without hospitalization.
An employee was working performing maintenance of apartment units and grounds
when he contracted COVID-19. The employee was hospitalized due to his COVID-19
infection and died at the hospital at 10:00 a.m. on April 2, 2021.
At 12:15 on June 23, 2021, an employee working as a laborer for a steel pipe and
tube manufacturer was sitting on the south end of the zinc pot #2 charger
rolling pipe into the zinc pot. The employee would roll about five pieces of
pipe into the pot at a time. The crane picked up a cradle of one-inch standard
pipe out of the dryer to set it down on the zinc pot charging table. The
employee stopped rolling pipe into the zinc pot to allow the crane to set the
cradle of pipe down on the zinc pot charging table. When the crane released the
cable of the lift, an estimated 8 to 20 pieces of pipe that were on top of the
cradle crisscrossed and jumped the four-inch pegs that were designed to prevent
the pipe from sliding directly into the pot. The pipes slid into the north end
of the zinc pot at an angle causing the zinc pressure to build up. The zinc shot
out of the south end of the pipe at the operator station. This end of the pipe,
which was not in the zinc, was pointed at the employee. The employee was sprayed
with molten zinc from the zinc tank via the pipe. The employee was hospitalized
with first degree burns to his chest and abdomen and third degree burns to his
right wrist. The employee stated that as the zinc hit his cotton sateen sleeve,
rolled down the sleeve and under the glove and melted the elastic of the sleeve.
As the elastic melted, the employee's right wrist continued to burn resulting in
the third degree burn. The local hospital diverted the employee to a burn center
for treatment. The employee stated he received skin grafting for the third
degree burn and was off work for one week to monitor for infection. Then, the
employee returned to duty and was on light-duty for two to three weeks.
At 7:30 a.m. on July 19, 2021, Employee #1 was grinding burs on an aluminum
window cutout using a handheld grinder when the plate holding the sanding paper
broke off and punctured his hand. Employee #1 sustained a laceration and
puncture wound. The employee was treated without hospitalization.
At 10:30 a.m. on July 17, 2021, an employee worked on a roof. At some point, the
employee removed a hole cover for an unknown reason and then began to talk on
the phone. The employee then fell approximately fifty feet through the hole and
was killed.
At 8:40 p.m. on July 15, 2021, an employee was serving a customer ice cream when

premature activation of the saw by depressing the guarded foot pedal, which
lowers hold-downs and then the blades. The employee sustained amputations to his
left ring and middle fingers and a partial amputation to his left index finger.
The employee was hospitalized. Lack of experience and inadequate training on the
machine contributed to the incident.
At 10:30 a.m. on March 3, 2021, Employee #1 and #2 stood on a stairway during

At 3:00 a.m. on May 31, 2021, an employee working as a maintenance technician

in the chain and sprocket. The employee was hospitalized to treat an amputated
fingertip.

the finger on July 8, 2021.
At 12:47 p.m. on July 8, 2021, an employee working as a filler at an industrial

At 9:50 a.m. on July 4, 2021, an employee was working for a pharmaceutical

At 8:59 p.m. on May 7, 2021, Employee #1 was performing maintenance on a bread

completing a repair, the employee energized and ran the equipment to validate
the correction. While checking the sprocket's teeth for the chain, the employee
placed his hand under a feeder belt and it was caught between the moving
sprocket and chain. The employee sustained an amputation of the tip of the left
index finger. The employee was working alone and was treated in the emergency
room at Memorial Hospital-Belleville. The employee was treated without
hospitalization.
At 11:00 a.m. on July 30, 2021, an employee worked to install roofing
tiles/shingles around and electrical inlet pipe. At some point, the employee
stood up, made a slight turn to the left, and contacted a live overhead line
(240 Volts). The employee was electrocuted and killed.
At 10:30 a.m. on August 2, 2021, an employee was backing a forklift in a chicken
house with a load of chicken cages on the forks. As the employee was backing,
the chicken cages became dislodged and unbalanced so he stopped, got out of the
forklift, and was attempting to fix the stack of chicken cages. The employee was
standing between the chicken cages and the mast of his forklift when a coworker
backed his forklift into the employee's chicken cages. The employee was crushed
between the chicken cages and the mast of his forklift. The employee suffered a
fractured skull and neck and died from his injuries.
At 8:00 a.m. on July 19, 2021, Employee #1 was operating a Cincinnati 2506 metal
shear to cut sheet metal parts. As he activated the machine, his left hand
slipped under the fixed guard, and his fingers were amputated by the shear.
At 8:30 a.m. on June 7, 2019, an employee was descending a portable extension la
dder when he felt the ladder shift. The employee fell from the ladder and landed
on a concrete surface. The employee was hospitalized to treat a fractured left
leg, which required surgical repair.
At 4:30 a.m. on February 10, 2021, Employee #1, a 26-year-old milking employee,
was walking home after completing an overnight milking shift at a dairy
facility. While walking on the feed alleyway area of a privately owned road,
Employee #1 was struck from behind and run over by a wheel loader. The wheel
loader was operated by a coworker, who had just started their work shift and was
transporting the loader from its overnight storage area in the maintenance shop
to the commodity shed to begin mixing cattle feed. Employee #1 sustained
multiple leg and pelvic fractures as well as internal bleeding and was
transported by ambulance to a local hospital, where he underwent immediate
surgery.  The employee was hospitalized.
An employee was working as a packaging apprentice at a brewery. The employee
went to get tested after a coworker informed him that he tested positive
recently. The employee tested positive for COVID-19 on August 8, 2021. On August
18, 2021, the employee was hospitalized with complications from COVID-19.  At
approximately 3:00 p.m. on August 26, 2021,  the employee died. Information
regarding engineering, administrative and personal protective equipment controls
for COVID-19 are not included in the narrative, but the fatality was not
determined to be OSHA covered.
At 4:00 p.m. on July 31, 2021, Employee #1 was cutting a tree trunk to fell it.
The trunk fell on previously cut branches, causing one branch to spring upward
and the employee's leg to move toward the chainsaw. The employee sustained a
laceration and was hospitalized.
An employee was working for an engineering service when he contracted COVID-19.
The employee was in self-isolation when he died due to COVID-19 complications at
8:00 a.m. on August 4, 2021.
An employee was working as a temporary forklift driver in a warehouse that
primarily stores cases of bottled water for distribution to customers. On July
29, 2021, the employee began experiencing symptoms of COVID-19 in the evening
after work. The employee was on a scheduled vacation from July 30,  through
August 2. The employee did not report to work August 3, and notified the
employer through a coworker that he had tested positive for COVID-19.  The
employer conducted COVID-19 contact tracing and no close contacts were
identified. On August 7, the employee was hospitalized.  He died due to
complications of the infection at 6:00 p.m. on September 2, 2021.
At 11:50 a.m. on August 28, 2021, an employee walked on the top plate of a new
construction building to mount a nine-foot by two-foot girder truss. The
employee leaned against the outer frame, which moved under the employee's
weight, and fell approximately twelve feet. The employee was taken to the
hospital for treatment but died two days later.
An employee worked washing cars at an automatic car wash. The car wash consisted
of an automated "drive through" car wash along with multiple outdoor stations
for manual cleaning and vacuuming of vehicles. The employee worked as a carwash

amputation, avulsion, and fracture to his right thumb. He was treated at Doctors

harmed the employee was the machine die catching the employee's right thumb.

employee received a phone call from a coworker informing her that she had tested
positive for COVID-19. The employees had the same position, therefore they did
not work together on the same production line. The employee got tested for
COVID-19 and received a positive result two days later. The employee quarantined
at home for two weeks before requiring hospitalization on December 21, 2020. The
employee successfully recovered from her infection.
At 10:00 a.m. on February 25, 2021, an employee was standing on the back of a
truck crane loading material into a dumper by using a handheld remote control.
The employee fell from the flatbed of the truck crane. The employee was
hospitalized to treat factures to the ribs, vertebrae and head.
At 6:40 a.m. on April 16, 2021, an employee was working for a farm supply
wholesaler. Specifically, the firm sold fertilizer. The employee was working in
the storage stage, offloading material from a forklift. A powered industrial
truck was driven up to him as he stood near a fixed object. His right ring
finger was caught between a solid surface and the forklift's forks or tines. His
finger was amputated above the knuckle. He was hospitalized.
At 11:30 p.m. on April 22, 2021, an employee worked to change lightbulbs. At
some point, the employee made contact with live electrical wiring and was killed
by electrocution.
At 12:15 p.m. on April 6, 2021, an employee was standing on a ladder in front of
an open elevator shaft attempting to disengage a winch lock. The worker lost his
balance and fell 18 feet to the bottom of the shaft, killing him.
At 8:30 a.m. an employee entered a room to clean it when an individual entered
the room behind her and beat and killed her.
At 6:30 a.m. on January 9, 2021, an employee, a printing press operator, was
troubleshooting a feeder foot/governor foot. The employee came to the feed
section and pressed the stop button for the feeder head.  The employee thought
the feeder foot was potentially getting stuck on the guard for it and was
pointing it out to the Feeder Operator.   When the employee went to point, the
foot performed a cycle, resulting in an amputation injury to the right second
finger.  The employee was treated without hospitalization.
At 6:04 p.m. on April 20, 2021, an employee working for a car manufacturer was
crossing the front sub-frame assembly line while it was in operation. The
employee tripped and lunged forward falling onto the concrete floor face first.
The employee got up on his own and went to the restroom to clean himself up due
to a bloody nose. The lead noticed the employee had not returned to work and
went to the restroom finding the employee unconscious on his back on the
restroom floor. Drugs and alcohol were found in the employee's system. The
employee was transported to the hospital after which he was transferred to a
regional medical center. He was hospitalized with a concussion, a fractured left
temporal bone, a contusion to his frontal lobe and a bilateral fracture to his
nose.
At 6:30 p.m. on November 17, 2020, an employee was moving a steel panel from the
aircraft riveter. As the employee was moving the steel panel, the employee
bumped the switch used to operate the pneumatic clinch gun. The employee's thumb
hospital and admitted for treatment of four crushed and fractured fingers on his
left hand.
At 10:15 a.m. on March 29, 2021, Employee #1 was tracing cable in a ceiling when
he slipped and fell through the tile ceiling. The employee fell approximately
one story to the floor below. The employee complained of back pain, loss of
consciousness, and memory loss. The full extent of the injuries was unknown at
the time. Emergency services were called, and the employee was treated without
hospitalization.
At 7:00 a.m. on March 25, 2021, an employee was driving a garbage truck when
pulled up to a residence to empty a trash can. The employee lowered the trash
truck's arm but was unable to lift the can due to it being frozen to the ground.
The employee exited the truck when the truck began to slide on the ice. The
truck's extended arm knocked over the employee who fell underneath the truck and
was killed.
An employee was working in a school when she began to have symptoms of asthma on
December 13, 2020. The employee continued to work until December 17, and was
tested for COVID-19 which returned positive on December 21. The employee was
piece of glastic, measuring 3.625 inches by 5 inches. Initially, the employee

An employee was working at a general medical or surgical hospital. He worked in
the Environmental Services (EVS) Department of the hospital. Employees in that
department were responsible for general cleanliness of the hospital in their
respective areas. This employee worked in cleaning and sanitation in a
medical/surgical unit. The cleaning included trash and linen removal, dusting,
wiping of surfaces, bathroom cleaning, and mopping of floors. There was one
COVID-19 positive patient on the floor, and the employee entered the room on two
occasions for cleaning. The employee was observed by the floor supervisor
wearing all appropriate PPE before entering the room, including, but not limited

The employee had been medically evaluated, fit tested, and trained for PPE. He
was not vaccinated for COVID-19, and he had signed a declination letter in
January 2021. On March 27, 2021, when he reported for work, he exhibited
symptoms of COVID-19. His employer sent him for testing. This was his last day
of work. That same day, March 27, 2021, the test results came back positive. On
March 29, 2021 he was hospitalized. On April 12, 2021, he died in the hospital.
That same day, OSHA was notified.
On January 21, 2021, an employee working as a mechanical engineering technician
for synthetic rubber manufacturer was drinking an iced tea while waiting for
product to run through a machine. The machine consisted of a drum unloader, twin
packer and extrusion die system. The run was the second trial run being
performed in a pilot plant. Air pockets formed in the supply tube causing the
sheet die extruder to throw molten adhesive across the room when the material
reached the die head. The employee was hospitalized to treat 2nd and 3rd degree
burns to his hands, face, neck and head.
At 6:15 a.m. on December 23, 2020, employees of Zone Safety LLC were
establishing a Temporary Traffic Control Zone on a 35 MPH highway. Employee #1
was controlling traffic using hand signals and a handheld paddle when they were
struck by a moving motor vehicle traveling east to west. The company had
implemented a traffic control plan and had already set up a large orange traffic
warning sign while in the process of placing a second warning sign when the
incident occurred. The on-site supervisor promptly contacted 911, and first
responders arrived to stabilize Employee #1 before transporting him to a local
hospital, where he was hospitalized to treat multiple severe injuries.
At 9:45 a.m. on April 10, 2021, Employee #1 was working to unjam a Niagra power
press (Press SC2-200-60-42, Serial Number 40606) at a manufacturing facility.
The press was interlocked without the die blocks installed. While reaching into
the press, the press settled and came together, crushing the employee's left
hand. The employee sustained an amputation of the left pinky. The employee was
treated without hospitalization.
At 7:00 a.m. on March 3, 2021, an employee working for a soap manufacturer was
observing a potassium hydroxide (KOH) feed during on-the-job training (OJT) for
the saponification feed process. The outlet tubing dislodged from the pump and
sprayed the employee. The employee was hospitalized to treat chemical burns to
his eyes and the skin on his face, neck and chest.
At 4:45 a.m. on April 10, 2021, Employee #1 was moving a material reel with a
forklift at a manufacturing facility. As the employee was pulling the reel out,
it rolled into a crack in the floor, causing it to tip over onto the employee.
The 1,400-pound reel struck and broke the employee's leg. The employee was
transported to the hospital, where he was admitted and treated for the leg
injury.
At 8:00 a.m. on March 1, 2021, Employee #1 was on a roof without any fall
protection. Employee #1 stepped on a weakened portion of the roof and fell 21
feet to the concrete floor. Employee sustained unspecified injuries and was
hospitalized for treatment.
An employee was working in the office of a pipe manufacturer when he contracted
COVID-19 and subsequently required hospitalization for treatment of his
infection at 3:16 p.m. on February 28, 2021.
At 2:30 p.m. on April 6, 2021, an employee was using a stackable window washing
ladder to clean windows on the south side of a house. The ladder was set up on
level ground with self-leveling support pads and extended to a height of 16
feet. At an unknown height, the employee fell an unknown distance, landing on
lava rock and striking the left side of his body. The employee had no memory of
the fall, but the ladder remained standing against the house. After the
incident, the employee walked around the home and informed the resident that the
remaining work would be rescheduled. The resident offered to call an ambulance,
but the employee refused. With the homeowner's assistance, the employee entered
a company vehicle and drove back to the company headquarters, where a cost
estimator met him. The employee was then transported by company vehicle to the
emergency room, where he was hospitalized to treat head contusions, fractures to
the left clavicle, scapula, left wrist, right thumb, ribs, and left toe, as well
as a laceration to the left ear and rock-sized indentations to the head.
At 3:15 a.m. on October 14, 2020, an employee was part of a crew off-loading
containers from an airplane. The employee was struck by a loaded container on
the side of his left foot. The employee was wearing composite toe boots but
suffered crushing injuries to the left foot.  The employee was hospitalized.
At 12:45 p.m. on October 20, 2020, an employee was working as a construction
laborer for a firm that constructed commercial and institutional buildings. His
firm was performing exterior carpentry during the alteration or rehabilitation
of a single-story commercial building. The employee was removing ceiling
rafters. He was working from an elevated work platform, moving a scissor lift
around a roof beam. He got too close to the beam and was pinned between the beam
and the railing of the platform.  The employee had suffered contusions to his
back and chest. The employee was taken to the hospital, where he was admitted
for observation overnight. He was hospitalized.
At 11:30 a.m. on October 26, 2020, Employee #1, a framer at a residential
construction project, was working on the second floor of the structure,
approximately 10 feet above ground level. While standing near the edge of the
floor, Employee #1 slipped, causing his right foot to become caught in a wood
framing block. The employee was left hanging upside down, placing significant
pressure on his foot. He sustained a fractured right foot and was hospitalized
for treatment.
At 4:15 p.m. on April 7, 2021, Employee #1 was running a piece of wood through a
jointer when the fence slipped. While bracing against the fence, his hand was
exposed to the jointer blade, resulting in a partial amputation of a finger. The
employee was treated without hospitalization.
At 1:10 p.m. on October 6, 2020, an employee was engaged in performing a dig out
of grapes on a 5,000 liter fiberglass variable capacity tank, with the use of a
sanitary plastic rake and a half ton plastic macro bin. As the employee was
raking the grapes out of the bottom front door of the tank, the lid slipped from
the top of the tank and struck the employee on her back while she was bent over
raking out the tank. At that time, the employee was transported to the hospital,
treated and released within two hours that same day. A few days later, the
employee was subsequently admitted to the hospital, where she was treated for
three fractures in her back.
At 9:00 a.m. on April 8, 2021, an employee was operating a golf cart when he
turned into the oncoming path of a SUV. The employee was ejected from the golf
cart in the collision and died as a result of his injuries.
At 11:45 a.m. on November 27, 2020, the milking operation of the farm's herd had

carousel to move the cows through the parlor. Cows entered and exited the
carousel on their own, with parlor employees performing cleaning of the animals'
udders and affixing the milking apparatus to each animal. After milking, the
being renovated.  The employee fell, a fall height of 32 feet.  The employee was

An employee was working as a maintenance technician and also lived in the
housing community. The employee was going on a trip so he took a pre-trip
COVID-19 test that was positive. The employee was in quarantine when he was

condition worsened, and he subsequently died from his infection on October 19,
On March 3, 2021, an employee was performing a training drill known as the

box with obstacles while wearing their SCBAs. During the drill the employee
became distressed and was having difficulty navigating the obstacles forcing him
to exit the obstacle. He remained motionless before coworkers began attending to
him when they realized that he was unconscious. The employee had suffered a
heart attack and later died at the hospital.
At 12:25 p.m. on January 12, 2021, Employee #1, employed by a waste management
company, was riding on the rear driver side step of a trash truck with his left
leg on the step and right leg on the edge of the hopper. After the last pickup,
the driver accelerated, causing the truck to jerk. As a result, the employee's
right leg entered the hopper, and the hopper blade rapidly came down on the
employee's leg. The employee sustained a compound fracture with a laceration
that required surgery. Emergency services transported the employee to the
hospital, where he was admitted and treated for his injuries.
At 11:00 a.m. on September 16, 2020, an employee was working on a variety pack
assembly line repackaging product for a soft drink manufacturer. The variety
pack assembly line consist of four stations, each representing a different
flavor to be packaged in a variety pack case. The employee was working at the
fourth and last station that was originally located directly in front of the
free roller section of the conveyor. Due to COVID-19 safety precautions, plastic
safety dividers were implemented into the operation making it difficult to work
from the original position. The employee was relocated to the other side of the
divider towards the end of the free rollers. While working from the new
position, the employee reached to grab a case with his left hand while holding
himself up with his right hand on the side of the conveyor. The employee's right
hand slipped from the side of the conveyor and went between a free roller and
the belt driven rollers causing his right hand to become caught in between the
belt and the rollers. The conveyor was missing a roller which allowed for a gap
large enough for his hand fall through and be caught in between. The employee
was transported and admitted to a local hospital, where he underwent surgery for
a fractured right hand and replacement of skin on that hand.
At 12:30 p.m. on September 28, 2020, an employee was working on bottom and his
partner on top. The operator at the top had left his position and only the
operator at the bottom was operating the equipment. The employee thought the top
operator had turned off the equipment and that they were getting ready to clean
stuck product debris out of the hopper and auger. The machine was not off.  When
the bottom employee placed his hand in the machine, he was caught and stuck on
his glove at the auger, causing injury to the right index finger. The employer
called 911, and the employee was transported by Riggs Ambulance to Emanuel
Medical Center, Turlock. The employee was admitted on September 29, 2020; the
employee had surgery and was discharged on September 30, 2020. They were unable
to reattach the amputated fingertip and used skin grafting to suture up the
wound. The finger was amputated at the dip joint.
At 7:30 a.m. on March 4, 2021, an employee working as a machine operator for a
recycling facility was cutting copper tubing into 2-foot sections. The employee
placed his left hand too close to the alligator shear jaws. The employee
amputated his middle and ring fingertips and was hospitalized.
On March 10, 2020, and March 11, 2020,  an employee called in sick with
gastrointestinal symptoms. On March 18, 2020, the employee called in sick again
and was unable to speak. The employee had reportedly been in close contact with
Coworker #1 (Telecare Nurse) who also became hospitalized with COVID-19.   The
employee told Coworker #2 (Nurse Manager) that she and Coworker #1 spent time
walking together during breaks at work. The employee remained on  sick leave
from March 19, 2020 to March 22, 2020.  On March 23, 2020, the employee was
hospitalized and was tested for COVID-19.  The employee was placed on a
ventilator on March 24, 2020.  On March 25, 2020, the COVID-19 test results were
confirmed positive and the employee was transferred to a different hospital,
where she was admitted to the Medical Intensive Care Unit (MICU) and died on
April 5, 2020, from COVID-19 related illness.
At 9:00 a.m. on February 18, 2021, an employee died after contracting the
coronavirus.
Two employees were working in a hospital when they were exposed to patients and
coworkers infected with COVID-19. The employees contracted COVID-19 and
subsequently required hospitalization for treatment of their infections.
At approximately 10:00 A.M. on March 11, 2021, an employee, working for a
specialty trade contractor, was beginning work to replace a storm water
drainpipe. The employee was using a ladder to enter a manhole and measure the
pipe that was going to be replaced. While climbing down into the manhole, the
employee fell from the ladder. The employee was hospitalized and treated for a
compression fracture in his back.
At 8:00 a.m. on March 6, 2021, Employee #1, employed by a warehouse company, was
operating a forklift when the fuel was running low. The employee proceeded to
change the propane cylinder. After replacing the cylinder, the employee noticed
the smell of the odorant added to propane and stopped the forklift to check the
situation. The employee then tightened the coupler connecting the cylinder to
the forklift by hand. Hours later, the employee began experiencing pain in both
hands but continued working until the shift ended. The employee did not inform a
supervisor about the incident and went to the hospital after work. The employee
was diagnosed with 2nd degree burns to both hands, including the fingers.  The
employee was hospitalized for treatment.
At approximately 9:00 a.m. on July 29, 2020, Employee #1 and a coworker, working
for a general building contractor at a condominium complex, were preparing the
worksite for painting. The employees were using 6-foot step ladders placed on a
15-foot balcony to tighten wood screws that secured the balcony railing above
them. The forward-facing balcony railing became loose due to rotten wood,
causing Employee #1 to lose his balance and fall approximately 19 feet to the
ground. The employee suffered a broken upper left leg and a hairline fracture to
the neck and was hospitalized for treatment. The incident was reported to DOSH
at 11:15 a.m. the same day, and DOSH arrived on-site on August 28, 2020. At the
time of the accident, both employees were unsupervised as their supervisor had
wearing a high-visibility vest or steel-toe boots, which might have prevented or
minimized the injury. Emergency services transported Employee #1 to the
hospital, where he was admitted and treated for a serious injury to their right
foot.
At 2:00 p.m. on October 2, 2020, an employee working as a construction laborer
for a demolition contractor was torch cutting metal pipes in a ceiling. The
employee was working from an 8-foot A-Frame ladder when section of the pipes
swung and fell to the ground knocking over the ladder. The employee fell to the
ground and hit his head. The employee was hospitalized to treat head injuries,
including a concussion.
An employee was working as a produce sales clerk when he was exposed to
customers and coworkers potentially infected with COVID-19. The employee
contracted COVID-19 and subsequently required hospitalization for treatment of
his infection at 2:00 p.m. on February 11, 2021.
At 2:00 p.m. on January 26, 2021, Employee #1, employed by a remodeling company,
was engaged in a waterproofing project at a multifamily residential building.
He was carrying a bucket of hot tar when he tripped and fell, and hot tar
splashed over his left hand burn.  The employee was transported to the hospital
and admitted for treatment of burns.
At 9:00 a.m. on November 4, 2020, Employee #1, employed by a vehicle lift
installation and servicing contractor, was working at a vehicle maintenance
facility. The employee had raised the carriage on a Rotary SP020 automotive lift
and was in the process of connecting a hydraulic hose to the bottom of a
cylinder/ram inside the column while a coworker secured cables running through
the overhead section. While connecting the hose, the carriage became disengaged
from the locking latch and fell onto Employee #1's forearms, crushing them.
Employee #1 sustained fractures to both forearms and was transported to the
hospital for admission and treatment. The employer was cited for failing to
secure the carriage, which contributed to the accident.
At 2:30 p.m. on February 8, 2020, Employee #1 was working for a framing
contractor.  Employee #1 was cutting fascia board (wood) with a portable
circular saw. The left finger of Employee #1 contacted the rotating saw blade.
Employee #1 suffered a partial amputation of his finger.  Employee #1 received
medical attention but was not hospitalized.
At 1:00 p.m. on March 23, 2021, Employee #1 was cutting lumber using a table
facility. He lit the torch and adjusted it to a proper gas rate and gas mixture.
In order to test these adjustments, he proceeded to conduct a test cut on the
metal. A 9-inch by 4-inch square cut-off from the tube detached and fell to the
floor. As it fell, the red hot metal bounced off the concrete and landed on the
gas hoses connecting the oxygen and acetylene tanks to the torch. The hot metal
burned through both hoses and ignited the now escaping gasses. The flame spread
in every direction from the severed hoses which were now whipping. The flame
engulfed the back of the employee's clothing and simultaneously the flames came
into contact with a nearby 55-gallon drum that had contained a small amount of
waste oil. The waste oil ignited and caused a boiling liquid expanding vapor
explosion (BLEVE). The employee was transported to the hospital before being
transported to a medical center, where he was admitted. The employee was placed
into an induced coma and underwent several skin grafts and other treatments for
severe burns to his upper body. On July 29, 2021, the employee was discharged
after 87 days of hospitalization. On August 24, 2021, the employee was admitted
to a university medical center due to complications and is currently unable to
verbally communicate.
At 1:47 p.m. on April 10, 2021, Employee #1, a tree trimmer, was hired to remove
two eucalyptus trees in the backyard of a residential property. After completing
the removal of one tree, the employee began cutting branches on the second tree.
While using a chainsaw, the employee accidentally cut the rope securing him to
the tree, causing him to fall approximately 30 feet onto a sloped hill. The
employee then rolled down the embankment, sustaining multiple fractures to his
back and ribs. The employee was hospitalized for treatment.
At 12:00 noon on April 28, 2021, an employee was operating a school bus with no
children on board when a deer ran into the road way between two vehicles. One
vehicle swerved out of the way, forcing the bus off road.  The employee died due
to her injuries.
At 8:30 a.m. on December 28, 2020, Employee #1 was assisting the gang saw
operator by unloading wood from the saw at a wood processing facility. After
noticing a piece of wood jammed in the gang saw, Employee #1 informed the saw
operator, who proceeded to walk back to the control panel to initiate a lockout
procedure for the machine. While the machine was turned off, Employee #1 opened
the guard for the sizer portion of the gang saw and reached in to remove the
jammed wood. Unbeknownst to Employee #1, the sizer teeth and saw blades were
still spinning, resulting in lacerations and contusions to his hand. Employee #1
was hospitalized and required hand surgery.
At 6:40 a.m. on May 3, 2021, an employee working for a compressor manufacturer
was operating a Rod Excello. The employee caught her right hand third finger in
a clamp on the equipment during operation. The employee was hospitalized for
treatment of a fingertip amputation.
At 4:45 p.m. on April 28, 2021, an employee was approaching a truck tire that
had just been inflated when the tire ruptured. The sudden release of air
pressure caused the employee to be forced to the concrete floor. The employee
sustained lacerations to the back of the head and internal injuries to the chest
due to the impact of the sudden air pressure release and the fall onto the
concrete floor.  The employee was hospitalized for treatment.
At 9:00 a.m. on January 28, 2021, an employee was adjusting the tailgate of a

was scraping product from the bed, the truck began rolling backward. Employee #1
attempted to return to the cab of the truck to put on the parking break, but the
truck tipped to the side, pinning and crushing Employee #1 beneath him. Employee
#1 later died after being care-flighted to the hospital.
At 4:23 p.m. on September 21, 2020, an employee was working for a logging firm.
He was a timber cutter or logger. The narrative said he was talking on the phone
when something hit him on the head, but it was more likely that he was talking
to other workers at the site on a two-way radio. Possibly he was struck by some
sort of vegetation. It was unclear what he was doing prior to the incident, as
the employee was not able to remember anything. There were no witnesses. The
employee suffered head trauma. He was hospitalized. The employer was aware of
the incident and its seriousness on September 21, 2020, but it did not report
the incident to the Division until three days later, on September 24, 2020.
At 6:00 p.m. on January 12, 2021, Employee #1, employed by a roofing contractor,

structure.  At the end of his work shift, as he was cleaning up debris, he
disconnected his fall protection to walk from his work area across the roof to a
ladder.  As he was crossing the roof, the employee fell and struck the bottom of

services transported the employee to the hospital, where he was admitted for
treatment of multiple injuries, including fractures to an arm, wrist, and ribs,
and fluid that required draining from his head.
At 9:00 a.m. on October 29, 2020, an employee working for a hardware store was

customer service drop zone.  The employee had his fingers interlaced through the
top cage of the order picker when he hit an I-beam on the ceiling. The employee
fractured two fingers and was hospitalized.
An employee was working as a school resource officer in a city school system

At approximately 4:15 a.m. on December 17, 2020, an employee was shoving snow

At 7:15 a.m. on March 12, 2021, Employee #1, an elderly home health care sitter,

The client also engaged in unknown activities resulting in Employee #1

At 8:00 a.m. on March 22, 2021, Employee #1 was observing a boring operation

force to the chest and was killed by suffocation.
At 1:00 a.m. on March 18, 2021, an employee was using a standup forklift to move

At noon on March 18, 2021, Employee #1 was found unresponsive on the ground

In early 2021, an employee was working for a nursery, garden center, or farm

At 3:15 p.m. on March 8, 2021, an employee was clearing trees and brush to

At 8:30 a.m. on March 19, 2021, an employee worked to remove old roofing

At approximately 9:39 p.m. on August 13, 2020, an employee was replacing

At 8:00 a.m.  on October 22, 2020, Employee #1, employed by a building equipment
company, was moving shelving components attached to a masonry wall inside a

Employee #1 was killed.
An employee who had been working on the repackaging line at a vitamins and
dietary supplements manufacturing site. On January 8, 2021, an employee was

At 8:30 a.m. on March 9, 2021, an employee was handing out lunch bags to
students, when she fell over the lunch bag container.  The employee was
hospitalized for a fractured hip.
