refill it with clean water. While refilling the bucket, it slipped and fell onto
the employee's foot. The employee's foot became infected and she was
hospitalized to treat an amputation of her fourth toe.
At 11:00 a.m. on December 3, 2020, Employee # 1 was working on a 4:12 sloped
roof of a one-story residential home. Employee # 1 was working alone to install
underlayment sealing tape onto the plywood of the roof, located underneath a
nearby skylight. Employee # 1 suddenly slipped, tumbled down to the eave of the
roof, and fell approximately eight feet to the ground below. Employee # 1
suffered a fractured right ankle injury from the impact onto the ground. He was
hospitalized.
At 9:45 a.m. on May 15, 2021, an employee working as a mechanic for a delivery
service was removing a transmission from a delivery vehicle. The employee failed
to strap the transmission to the lift. The transmission became unstable and
caught the employee's finger between the transmission and the floor. The
employee received medical treatment without hospitalization for a crushed and
partially amputated fingertip.
At 9:00 a.m. on May 18, 2021, an employee working as a heavy equipment mechanic
for a construction materials wholesale business was climbing the ladder of a
crane truck. The employee was carrying a bucket of tools when he lost his
balance just as he was placing the tools on top of the work station. The
employee fell to the floor below. He was hospitalized to treat a fractured skull
and a right ankle sprain.
At 3:00 a.m. on June 3, 2021, an employee exited the work truck to assist the
crew leader with a road sign. A passing motor vehicle entered the lane closure,
struck and killed the employee.
At 5:00 p.m. on May 26, 2021, an employee was manually taking a sample of
"paste" from a mixer for an impurity test. The employee reached through an
opening on the back side of the mixer and was struck by the mixer blade. The
incident resulted in total amputation of the right hand middle finger and
partial amputation of the right hand ring finger. The employee was hospitalized
for treatment.
At 5:00 p.m. on January 4, 2021, an employee who had been working as a
Registered Nurse at a regional medical center was hospitalized with a COVID-19
infection. The employee had been providing direct patient care to suspected and
positive COVID-19 patients when she was likely exposed to the virus. The
employer did not have an adequate respiratory protection program in place.
At 2:00 a.m. on May 18, 2021, an employee working for a soap and detergent
manufacturer was attempting to adjust the transfer plate on a conveyor. The
employee caught his left thumb between chain and sprocket. The employee received
medical treatment without hospitalization for an amputation to his thumb.
At 2:30 p.m. on June 1, 2021, an employee kneeled in front of a truck to fasten
a chain to the front in preparation to pull it out of mud. At the same time, a
coworker operated a backhoe to back up to the truck and swung the bucket towards
the truck, striking the employee and pinning the employee between the truck and
the bucket. The employee received upper body trauma and was killed.
At 10:45 a.m. on June 3, 2021, Employee #1 was operating a metal press when his
left finger was caught, resulting in amputation of the left fingertip. The
employee was hospitalized for treatment.
At 4:30 a.m. on June 3, 2021, Employee #1 was operating a powered industrial
truck (P.I.T.) to remove trash. While reversing to approach an elevator, the
employee accidentally pressed the accelerator, causing the vehicle to crash
or near the paint booth when a fire ignited, resulting in burns. The incident
prompted immediate response and investigation into fire safety protocols and
equipment usage in the vicinity of flammable materials. The employee was
hospitalized.
At approximately 10:30 a.m. on May 25, 2021, an employee was operating a manual
Bridgeport Milling Machine. The employee's right hand came in contact with the
point of operation because the guard was not deep enough.  His hand was caught
in the mill bit. The employee amputated the right ring and pinkie fingers and
was hospitalized for these injuries.
At approximately 9:05 a.m. on March 13, 2021, Employee #1 was operating a mini 9
deburring machine with a wet dust collector attached to deburr steel parts being
fabricated. Earlier, aluminum had been processed through both machines, causing
a buildup in the dust collector. While deburring the steel, sparks were
generated, leading to a flash fire. The employee sustained third-degree burns to
the back of his head, neck, back, and right arm.  The employee was hospitalized
for treatment.
At approximately 5:45 p.m. on April 4, 2021, Employee #1 was operating a
standing forklift while backing up when the employee stepped off the forklift
before it had come to a complete stop. As a result, the employee's left foot was
caught between the forklift and racking. The injury caused a fractured left foot
and ankle. The employee was hospitalized for treatment.
At 1:00 p.m. on June 14, 2021, Employee #1 was using an air wand to blow out hot
sand from the upper nozzle in the gate area on the cold-side (bottom) of a
ladle. The sand was at a temperature of approximately 2,000 degrees Fahrenheit.
When the employee blew the hot sand with the air wand, some sand blew back onto
the employee and entered small gaps in the personal protective equipment (PPE).
The employee sustained second and third-degree burns on the right hand,
extending from the bottom of the hand to about midway up the forearm. Burns on
the top of the wrist required a skin graft. The employee also suffered
second-degree burns on the right side of the face around the temple and cheek
area, outside the frames of the safety glasses. The employee was hospitalized
for treatment.
At 12:30 p.m. on June 14, 2021, Employee #1 was bending metal parts on the LVD
#181 press brake. After completing the first bend, the employee repositioned the
part for a second bend and held onto it as the machine engaged. During the
bending operation, the employee's right thumb was pinched between the part and
the front side of the press brake, resulting in a partial fingertip amputation.
The metal part was approximately 1.5 inches wide, and additional safeguarding
methods, such as using a tool to maintain hand clearance from the point of
operation, were not in place at the time. The incident occurred indoors and was
not weather-related. The employee was treated without hospitalization.
At 10:50 a.m. on June 21, 2021, an employee installed lighting and at some point
made contact with an energized wire, electrocuted and killed.
An employee was working in a hospital when she was exposed to patients and
coworkers infected with COVID-19. The employee contracted COVID-19 and
subsequently required hospitalization for treatment of her infection at 9:45
a.m.  on July 21, 2020.
At 9:00 a.m. on June 22, 2021, an employee was preparing to deliver a load of
topsoil. While unloading the material, the truck tipped over. The employee
sustained six broken ribs, a punctured lung, facial lacerations, and multiple
bruises. The employee was hospitalized for treatment.
At 1:50 p.m. on June 18, 2021, an employee was finishing her shift in a
watermelon field.  She began to feel nauseous, and was vomiting.  She sustained
a heat-related illness and was hospitalized.
At 6:45 p.m. on June 12, 2021, Employee #1 was clearing a jam on a milk filling
machine/caser. His hand was caught between the gripper head and the Teflon
cutting edge. Energy sources were not isolated during the jam clearing process.
The employee sustained lacerations to the back of his right hand and index
finger and was hospitalized for treatment.
At 1:45 p.m. on January 22, 2021, Employee #1 working as a machine operator for
a sheet metal manufacturer was cutting metal to length. The employee was
troubleshooting the process that applies film to the metal prior to metal being
mechanically fed into the point of operation. The process involved manually
removing air bubbles from the material being applied to the metal. The employee
was performing this task while the machine was energized. The employee was
pulled into the mechanical feed mechanism that moved the material into the point
of operation. The employee was hospitalized to treat a severe laceration to his
right hand.
At 12:30 p.m. on June 21, 2021, an employee assisted with the installation of a
crushing injuries to his hand and arm.
At 2:30 p.m. on May 15, 2021, an employee working for a flat glass manufacturer
was cleaning dust build-up off machine behind the hopper. The employee climbed
over the guard rails to clean an area between silos and platforms. He stepped on
a weak spot and fell through the floor to the concrete floor below. The employee
was hospitalized to treat broken ribs and a dislocated and fractured shoulder.
At 12:00 p.m. on January 7, 2021, Employee #1 was walking on the edges of a
Timpte semi trailer, using a rake to level dried material (blood). As the
employee felt the trailer move slightly, he attempted to return to the platform
ladder to investigate. Before reaching the ladder, the trailer's landing gear
suffered a catastrophic collapse, causing the employee to fall approximately 10
feet to the concrete floor. The employee lost consciousness upon impact and was
later diagnosed with a herniated disc at L5 and S1, along with paresthesia in
the lower extremities and right hand. The employee was hospitalized for
treatment.
At 8:15 a.m. on March 12, 2021, Employee #1 was operating a tractor with a
shredder to shred citrus plant debris. Upon noticing smoke coming from the
activation of the lever. The employee received medical treatment without
hospitalization for amputations to his index and middle fingers.
At approximately 10:15 a.m. on July 29, 2020, an employee was assisting in the
instillation of 72 ft of 3-in stainless steel riser pipes on the 8th floor of a
newly constructed residential high-rise construction site in excess of 60
stories. While brushing away construction debris that had gathered on the pipe
surface, the suspended load dropped suddenly pinning the employee's hand between
the two sections of pipe.  The cause of the sudden drop of the load could not be
conclusively determined. The employee sustained crushing injuries to his fingers
that resulted in the surgical amputation of 1 or more fingers.  He was treated
and hospitalized at Long Beach Medical Center. At 10:37 a.m. on September 22,
2020, DOSH was notified from a complaint from a member of the public, the
employer did not meet the reporting requirement. At approximately 12:03 p.m. on
October 15, 2020, DOSH arrived on-site and issued serious accident related
citations for T8CCR �1511(b). The employer failed to effectively survey the
conditions associated with having an employee working in a position whereby his
hands are underneath a suspended load of approximately 72 ft of 3-in stainless
steel riser pipe weighing up to 1,000 lbs., and to determine the kind of
safeguards necessary to execute the work in a safe manner.
At 10:30 a.m. on April 27, 2021, two employees from the County of San Diego,
Department of Parks and Recreation, were working at Damon Lane County Park in El
Cajon, CA, to remove a fallen eucalyptus tree. Employee #1 had been instructed
to remain near their truck, approximately 60 feet away from the tree.  A
coworker was using a chainsaw to clear vegetation and small branches around the
tree.  While performing this work, the fallen tree rotated at its base, causing
its top to move approximately three feet. Employee #1 was struck by vegetation
and branches from the shifting tree and was found lying on their back, covered
in debris. Emergency services were called, and paramedics arrived at
approximately 11:00 a.m. Employee #1 sustained a scalp laceration, a T5
compression fracture, and an L3 endplate compression fracture. He underwent
surgery to repair the scalp laceration and was admitted to Scripps Mercy
Hospital in San Diego from April 27, 2021, to April 29, 2021.
At approximately 2:15 P.M. on March 3, 2021, an employee, working for a
construction contractor, was aligning pin holes to attach equipment to an
excavator. The employee attempted to align pin holes internally with the left
middle finger. The equipment arm dropped and pinched the employee's finger. The
employee was hospitalized and treated for amputation of the left middle
fingertip between the fingernail and first knuckle.
At 5:35 p.m. on June 6, 2021, Employee #1, employed as an associate for
GoBrands, Inc. DBA Go Puff, was off the clock at the worksite located in San
Francisco, CA. The employee was involved in a verbal altercation with a
coworker, who struck Employee #1 with a car. Employee #1 sustained bilateral leg
fractures from the incident. Emergency services responded, and the employee was
hospitalized.  No accident-related citations were issued.
At approximately 2:30 a.m. on Friday, October 9, 2020, an employee was working
for a temporary staffing agency. The firm was known for providing technical
workers, but that was not the only field for which they provided workers. This
employee had been sent to work at a firm that manufactured foam packaging using
recycled materials. In this incident, he was working as a sorter in the firm's
sorting and recycling department. He operated heavy equipment. He was operating
a Raymond stand-up forklift. The forklift was carrying a baler load. He was at a
crossroads where two aisles intersected. He yielded to another employee crossing
his path. He said in his statement that he allowed the employee to pass, move
his forklift forward, and then, without warning, blacked out. The forklift he
was operating crashed, and the employee's left foot struck against a metal work
uniform cabinet. His left foot was pinned between this metal work uniform
cabinet and the side of the Raymond stand-up forklift. His left foot was pinned.
It was bruised and swollen. The employee was hospitalized. The incident was
reported to the Cal/OSHA Long Beach district office at 9:57 a.m. that same day.
At 11:30 a.m. on Monday, November 2, 2020, the Division held an opening
conference with the employer. The inspection of the manufacturing firm was
covered in inspection number 1500600.
At 10:30 a.m. on June 3, 2020, an employee was engaged in relocating a large
structural steel frame at the direction of the shop foreman.  The employee was
working with a pendant controller and had rotated the frame on its short end and
placed it on a work rest. The employee then relocated the chains to a position
below the structure's center of gravity and attempted to lift it while standing
in the structure's fall zone. The structure shifted towards him quicker than he
could react, and it struck his shoulder.  The employee sustained serious
injuries to his left shoulder that required multiple surgeries.  The employee
was admitted and treated at Harbor UCLA Medical Center. The investigation
revealed that the employer failed to ensure that the load was well secured and
properly balanced in the lifting device before it was lifted more than a few
inches.
An employee was working as a cardiovascular nurse at a heart surgical hospital
providing care to post-surgery patients. The employee contracted COVID-19 and
was hospitalized on September 17, 2020, for 16 days with breathing complications
due to COVID 19.
On June 7, 2021 an employee at a lumber mill was caught between the roller and
belt of a CBI Grinding Machine used to make mulch. The employee was crushed and
killed as a result of his injuries.
An employee was working for a temporary staffing agency when he contracted
COVID-19 and required hospitalization for treatment on July 4, 2020.
At 12:00 p.m. on May 21, 2021, an employee working for a hotel was scraping
paint off a ceiling in preparation for painting. The employee swept up the paint
chips and leaned between the top and mid rail of the scaffold cross bracing to
toss the broom down to a coworker. The mid rail gave way and the employee fell
to the floor. The employee was hospitalized to treat a broken wrist and internal
abdominal injuries.
At 10:00 p.m. on May 28, 2021, Employee #1 was returning from lunch and
attempted to remove a piece of garment that had been pulled into conveyor
rollers. Her hand was caught and pulled between the rollers, resulting in
amputation of a fingertip. She was hospitalized for treatment.
At 11:00 a.m. on June 8, 2021, Employee #1 washed the inside of a tanker to
clear chemical residue from the inside of the tanker. At some point, Employee #1
lost consciousness and was found by Employee #2, who attempted to rescue
Employee #1 from the tanker. A coworker heard Employee #2 in distress and called
for emergency medical assistance. Employee #1 was killed and Employee #2 was
hospitalized due to exposure to hydrogen sulfide.
At 2:30 p.m. on May 12, 2021, an employee worked to fell a red oak tree. At some
point, a five-inch diameter branch sheared off and fell approximately
thirty-five feet onto the employee's head. The employee received a crush injury
to the skull and was killed.
At 11:15 a.m. on May 28, 2021, Employee #1 was clearing a jam of stuck blister
packs on a blister picker machine when the machine returned downward. His right
middle finger was caught between moving parts, resulting in a partial
amputation. He was hospitalized for treatment.
At 1:35 a.m. on June 8, 2021, an employee worked to install metal roofing
panels. At some point, the employee stepped backwards, fell through a roof
opening and was killed.
At 3:15 a.m. on June 2, 2021, Employee #1 was finishing grinding a urethane roll
when his right hand was struck by the grinding wheel. The employee sustained
trauma to his right ring and middle fingers, resulting in amputation up to the
first knuckle of the ring finger and up to the second knuckle of the middle
finger. The employee was hospitalized for treatment.
At 4:36 a.m. on March 28, 2021, Employee #1 was tasked with moving bread trays
through a conveyor system for a baking company. While working on Line 4 with
three other coworkers, the employee attempted to correct a misaligned tray,
caught by the moving rollers. The employee, who was wearing protective gloves,
sustained a broken right wrist and a finger amputation. He was transported to
Magnolia Regional Medical Center, where he was admitted for overnight treatment.
At 2:13 a.m. on August 3, 2021, Employee #1 was removing a piece of plastic from
an injection mold machine when another employee closed the outer door. The mold
struck and crushed his left arm. He was hospitalized for treatment.
At 10:00 a.m. on July 27, 2021, an employee was standing on the 4th floor while
an electric winch operator on the 2nd floor was preparing to hoist a 300-lb
steel tubing section from the 1st floor to the 3rd floor of an elevator shaft.
The employee was guiding the tubing when his right hand became pinned between
the hoisting line and the snatch block. The employee sustained amputations to
the index and middle fingers, which are surgically reattached.  The  employee
was hospitalized for treatment.
An employee was working as a Custodian for a City public transportation agency.
The employee's duties were to swipe/wax floors and vacuum/clean carpets.  The
employee worked as part of a team with 4 coworkers and they work at night. The
employee stated he refused to share rides with coworkers. On July 4, 2021, the
employee was off work and didn't meet with anyone. On July 5, 2021, the employee
worked at the Metro East site. On July 6, 2021, the employee worked on the Woods
division site and reported he encountered an unmasked coworker in the restroom
(employer records do not show that the employee worked at the woods division
site). On July 7, 2021, the employee reported he was starting to experience
symptoms. On July 16, 2021, the employee tested positive and was hospitalized
for three days. The employee was not vaccinated.  The employee informed his
employer the same day and was advised to call the company hotline which he did.
The employer notified the employee's worksite on July 18, 2021. The employee
stated that management is not enforcing the indoor face covering policy and that
the COVID-19 training provided did not provide enough information for him to
understand the subject matter. The employer did provide face coverings but the
employee chose to use his own reusable one. The employee had access to hand
washing facilities but reported he observed coworkers not washing their hands.
The employee's source of exposure could not be traced. The employer provided
tools to protect employees from COVID-19. The employer did not document the
COVID-19 hazards for Custodial Staff.
On July 5, 2021, two employees working as bus drivers working for a public
transportation agency were reported hospitalized with COVID-19. Employee #1 last
worked on June 25, 2021. He started to experience symptoms on June 25, 2021, one
week after his spouse tested positive. His spouse did not develop symptoms. He
was sent by ambulance to the emergency room where he tested positive and was
hospitalized from July 5, 2021, to August 20, 2021. Employee #1 notified his
employer on July 7, 2021, and started rehabilitation on August 20, 2021.
Employee #1 was not vaccinated prior to contracting COVID-19 and reported he
does not recall most of the details. Employee #1 believes he contracted COVID-19
from his spouse and doesn't recall receiving COVID-19 training. Employee #2 last
worked on July 16, 2021. She began to experience symptoms on July 19, 2021,
tested positive on July 20, 2021, and was hospitalized for 5 days around July
26, 2021. Employee #2 was not vaccinated and there are no barriers in the
driver's seat to separate driver and passengers. Employee #2 reported no contact
with coworkers during her job duties. The employer provided wipes, gloves and
masks and the employee has access to hand washing facilities along her route.
Employee #2 stated that she did not receive COVID-19 training and doesn't recall
any rules to keep bus windows open during operations or open the doors at the
end of the lines. Employee #2's source of exposure is unknown. The employer did
provide tools to protect employees from COVID-19. The employer did not document
the COVID-19 hazards for bus drivers or document training for drivers.
At 6:40 p.m. on July 31, 2021, Employee #1 was putting paper into a feed roller
when the left pinky became caught in the rollers. While attempting to free the
left hand with the right hand, the right hand also became caught. The employee
sustained amputations to both hands and was hospitalized.
At 10:30 a.m. on May 2, 2021, Employee #1 was retrieving carpet rolls from a
shelf approximately nine feet above the ground while standing on a platform
elevated by a forklift. During this task, two brackets supporting the platform
broke off, causing the platform to tilt to one side. Employee #1 lost footing
and fell to the concrete floor. The employee sustained a fractured left leg and
a head concussion. The employee was hospitalized for treatment.
At 10:30 a.m. on August 3, 2021, Employee #1 was performing maintenance on a
generator when he fell from a 10-foot ladder, striking a concrete floor. He
sustained a fractured skull, pelvis, ribs, vertebrae, and a possible broken arm,
and was hospitalized for treatment.
At 7:05 a.m. on July 27, 2021, Employee #1 was making adjustments to a freight
elevator when the elevator failed. Employee #1 fell into the elevator shaft and
sustained fractured ribs. The employee was hospitalized.
At 11:00 a.m. on August 3, 2021, Employee #1 was approximately 35 feet up a pine
tree cutting limbs when he fell to the ground. He sustained multiple blunt force
trauma injuries and was hospitalized for treatment.
At 3:00 p.m. on July 30, 2021, an employee working as a laborer for a farm
products storage facility was working with two coworkers preparing to install an
additional section to a sweep auger. The employee was using the unload drag
conveyor to remove the grain from a steel corn bin before installation of the
section.  The employee was distracted before trying to grab a tool that was
getting pulled into the drag. The employee fell causing his foot to slip into
the unguarded sump drag chain in the moving drag conveyor. The employee was
hospitalized to treat a mangled left foot and heel. Coworkers called 911 and
first responders determined he needed to be flown to a nearby medical center. At
the time the narrative was submitted, the employee remained at the hospital,
where he was being treated and observed. On August 2, 2021, the employee was
scheduled to have surgery to amputate his foot.
At 11:15 a.m. on June 20, 2021, Employee #1 was cleaning the manure at the tail
end of a conveyor system in the conveyor adjustment room. He had pressed the
emergency stop button and reached through an access hole in the side of the
conveyor to clean between the roller and the belt. The conveyor restarted, and
his arm was pulled between the roller and the belt, resulting in the amputation
of his right arm. The employee was hospitalized for treatment.
At 6:00 p.m. on July 28, 2021, Employee #1 was installing the last actuator to
open the clamshell roof of the Nacelle. While stepping across the gear box and
turning his body 180 degrees, the employee's left hand contacted the exterior of
a LED light fixture. Employee #1 received a 230-volt electrical shock, resulting
in a dislocated and fractured left shoulder. Emergency services transported the
employee for treatment. Employee #1 was hospitalized.
At 1:45 a.m. on July 27, 2021, Employee #1 was working as a bander operator at a
stacker machine, receiving stacked lumber. When a forklift stopped, the lumber
packs slid forward, striking the bander operator and pinning him between two
packs of lumber. Employee #1 sustained fractured hips and was hospitalized.
An employee and coworkers were working for a new car dealership and were
transferring used cars between car dealerships when they exposed each other to
COVID-19. The employee contracted COVID-19 and was hospitalized on July 27,
2021, for treatment.
An employee was working in a county sheriff's office when she was exposed to
members of the public and coworkers potentially infected with COVID-19. The
employee first started exhibiting COVID-19 symptoms on January 14, 2021, was
tested on January 16, 2021, and received a positive test result the next day.
The employee was hospitalized for treatment of her infection at 9:05 p.m. on
January 22, 2021.
At 3:30 p.m. on July 18, 2021, Employee #1 was standing by the cash register at
a commercial establishment when he attempted to light a cigarette, causing a gas
explosion. The employee sustained third-degree burns to the face and hands and
second-degree burns to the chest and stomach. Employee #1 was hospitalized for
treatment.
At 2:10 p.m. on February 11, 2021, Employee #1 was working for a tile and
terrazzo contractor.  Employee #1 was prepping the floor using an angle grinder
to cut the door jam.  The grinder inadvertently struck his left hand causing a
laceration on the index and ring finger. Employee #1 was hospitalized.
At 04:45 a.m. on August 04, 2021, an employee was walking through the Bakery
department. The floor care contractor was stripping flooring near the bakery
when the employee walked through the area and slipped and fell. The employee was
contact with COVID-19 patients. Employee #2 tested positive on August 12, 2020,
was hospitalized on August 20, 2020. Employee #3 last worked on December 9,
2020, symptoms began December 10, 2020, tested positive on December 13, 2020,
and was admitted to the hospital on December 19, 2020. The employer did not have
Adequate Aerosol Transmissible Diseases policies and procedures in place.
At 3:30 p.m. on May 30, 2021, an employee working as a painter for a poultry
processor was trying to unjam a heart de-fatter machine. The employee was using
an improvised hook that had a loop at the end. The machine was running while the
ambulance to Riverside Medical Center in Kankakee, Illinois, where he was
admitted and hospitalized for treatment.
At approximately 3:15 p.m. on June 24, 2021, an employee was operating a
horizontal press. The employee entered the press area to retrieve a part when
the die set began to close, striking the employee's left hand. As a result, the
employee sustained an amputation to the left index finger. The employee was
treated for the injury but was not hospitalized.
At 9:00 a.m. on July 23, 2021, an employee and a coworker opened a controlled
atmosphere warehouse to clear off condensation on a window, check the inside
temperature, and collect a sample of apples. The employee reached for the
apples, gasped, and collapsed into a narrow opening between the apple crates.
The coworker attempted to rescue the employee but could not move him due to the
restricted space. The coworker ceased initial rescue efforts and ran to get help
and call emergency services. Employee died due to asphyxiation in the low oxygen
environment.
At 11:35 a.m. on June 15, 2021, an employee working as an assembler for an
industrial equipment wholesalers was attempting to turn, by hand, aluminum
trusses hanging from a boom on a powered industrial truck (PIV). Coworker #1,
who was operating the PIV misunderstood what Coworker #2, the spotter, said and
moved forward instead of moving the trusses up. The employee's foot was run over
but the PIV tire as a result. The employee was hospitalized to treat a
separation of the heel from his leg and severed nerves, all within the skin.
Employee #1 worked as a Senior Test Technician for an electronics company. The
employee's last day of work was December 23, 2020. On December 30, 2020, the
employee tested positive for COVID-19 and notified his employer. On January 7,
20201, the employee was admitted to the hospital due to his infection. On
January 25, 2021, the employee died at the hospital due to COVID-19. The date,
time and other details leading up to exposure are not indicated in the
narrative. Information regarding engineering, administrative and personal
protective equipment controls for COVID-19 are not included in the narrative.
Employee #1 worked in an office setting at a computer station, servicing
customers. Employee #2 was hospitalized on July 20, 2021, due to Covid-19
related symptoms. Employee #2 worked in an office setting within acceptable
social distances from other employees answering phones.  On July 5,  2021,
Employee #1 tested positive with Covid-19. and was hospitalized due to Covid-19.
Employee #1 later died from COVID-19. On July 10, 2021, Employee #2 showed
symptoms of Covid-19. On July 15, 2021, Employee #2 tested positive for
Covid-19. On July 20, 2021, Employee #2 was hospitalized for Covid-19 related
symptoms and later died from complications from the virus.
At 8:30 p.m. on June 12, 2021, Employee #1, working for a cleanup crew at a
poultry processing establishment, climbed down into a sunken ice bath chiller
approximately 12 feet wide using a ladder. After the cleaning process, the
ladder was no longer available, so the employee attempted to climb out by
ascending the suspended gates that move the carcasses along. The gates swung
when the employee's body weight caused one to open, creating a pinch point. The
employee placed his left pinky finger into this pinch point. When the gate swung
back, it closed on the gloved finger, causing a laceration and removal of the
nail and some flesh. The employee was treated without hospitalization.
On December 29, 2020, Employee #1 and a coworker, employed by a construction
contractor, were replacing old posts and fencing using a tractor and a power
take off (PTO) post-hole digger.  Employee #1's clothing became caught in the
PTO shaft.  Employee #1 was pulled into the rotating draft shaft and killed.
On July 22, 2021, an employee was found unresponsive in a restaurant. He had
been left at the facility the night before to close and coworkers found him the
next day dead of unknown causes.
On July 15, 2021, an employee performing underwater diving operations at a
electrical generating station inspecting pipes and clearing debris from a pump
basin. Coworkers for the power company reported to the dive crew that the
stoplog gates "should be in place" but they were unsure. The employee verified
that LOTO was performed on the two pumps in the immediate work area and the
employee entered the water to check for the presence of stoplogs and water flow.
The employee mistakenly verified that stoplogs were down and that there was no
water flow or current present (which was incorrect). The employee then continued
his work and returned to the water to make a last check of the area. During this
final check, the employee's umbilical was caught in a current caused by a pump
in an adjacent bay that was still in operation. The current pulled the umbilical
into the pump, which in turn, pulled the employee into the pump, killing him.
At 8:20 a.m. on July 16, 2021, Employee #1 was picking up a skid from a
workstation when a stand-up powered industrial truck operator started to back
up. At the same time, a sit-down powered industrial truck operator was
attempting to go around the stand-up truck. The interaction caused the employee
to be impaled on the upper back of the thigh by a powered industrial truck fork.
The employee was hospitalized.
At 4:45 p.m. on July 20, 2021, an employee had just finished his shift operating
a nip roller machine which required him to observe the trusses for defects and
retracted while Employee #1 was holding it at the base and pinched his left ring
finger. Employee #1 suffered a partial amputation and was hospitalized.
At 5:45 p.m. on August 4, 2021, an employee was assembling a three-seat sofa on
the north side of Cell 58. He had just stapled components into place when, while
holding the staple gun in his non-dominant left hand, he inadvertently triggered
it. The staple gun unexpectedly contacted his forehead, discharging a 16-gauge,
galvanized chisel point staple that fully penetrated his forehead. The employee
was hospitalized for treatment of the head injury.
At 6:30 a.m. on Thursday, March 18, 2021, an employee was working for a firm
that manufactured sheet metal work for the aerospace industry. He was directly
employed by the firm. He was working in the wood shop or woodwork shop. He was
operating a Delta table saw, with serial number 89D18957, to cut wood. The blade
was unguarded. The employee was holding a piece of wood with his hand, and his
thumb came into contact with the running blade. The employee's thumb was
amputated. The narrative did not specify whether the amputation occurred at the
time or was done surgically. The narrative did not say whether it was his right
thumb or his left thumb that was amputated. The employee was hospitalized. The
employer reported the incident at 12:38 p.m. that same day, in compliance with
342(a). DOSH arrived at the site on April 24, 2021.
At 9:30 a.m. on November 11, 2020, Employee #1, while moving a dishwasher on the
back of a truck, took a wrong step backward and fell off the truck onto the
ground. The employee sustained multiple injuries, including head and collarbone
injuries. Emergency services transported the employee to the hospital for
admission and treatment.
At 10:00 a.m. on July 22, 2021, Employee #1 was power-washing an automotive
repair pit at a vehicle maintenance facility. While working, the employee fell
onto the concrete floor or adjacent structure beneath his feet. He sustained
severe head trauma and was transported to a local hospital, where he was
admitted for treatment.
At 1:50 p.m. on August 5, 2021, an employee working for a manufacturer of
precision turned products was operating an overhead crane. The employee was
moving bundles of bar stock. He began stacking the bundles on top of each other
when the stack collapsed and fell on his foot. The employee was hospitalized to
treat a crushed foot.
An employee was working as a licensed practical nurse at a general medical or
surgical hospital. She worked as a safety companion. She contracted COVID-19 on
about July 26, 2021. She was found unresponsive at home on August 4, 2021. She
was brought to the emergency room at the hospital. She was pronounced dead.
At 1:25 p.m. on June 11, 2021, Employee #1 was operating an industrial reach
truck loaded with wrapped boxes on a pallet. While traveling through an aisle in
anticipation of storing the pallet on a racking system shelf, the pallet struck
a rack column. The impact caused the materials on the pallet to fall and strike
the employee. She sustained a fractured left leg and a fracture to the left side
of her hip. The employee was hospitalized for treatment.
At 7:00 a.m. on June 2, 2021, Employee #1 was exiting the back of a freight
truck by stepping down onto the bumper. While moving his right foot from the
freight bed to the bumper, he lost his footing and fell to the concrete ground.
The fall resulted in an unspecified injury caused by impact with the concrete
surface. Employee #1 was hospitalized for treatment.
On April 12, 2021, an employee working as a machinery maintenance technician for
a manufacturer of specialty lumber was attempting to determine why a machine was
not working. The employee placed his hand in a Mann-Russell Electronic Generator
when he contacted a hot lead. The machine was energized and not locked out. The
employee was hospitalized to treat injuries to his back, arm and torso from the
resulting electrical shock.
At 1:30 p.m. on August 4, 2021, an employee was operating a re-roll machine when
his arm became caught in a rotating shaft. This incident resulted in multiple
fractures to his arm. The employee was hospitalized for treatment of these
injuries.
At 7:30 a.m. on February 10, 2021, Employee #1 was working for a structural
medical or surgical hospital. He became infected with COVID-19. He developed a
respiratory disease.  At 5:00 p.m. on November 6, 2020, he died.
At 4:00 p.m. on June 30, 2020, Employee #1 was in the cone basket of a vehicle
picking up traffic cones at the end of the work shift. A coworker was operating
the vehicle erratically which caused Employee #1 and the coworker to get into a
dispute. When Employee #1 got out of the cone basket and onto the bed of the
truck, the coworker stopped the vehicle and grabbed Employee #1 pulling him to
the ground causing Employee #1 to suffer anterior compartment syndrome and a leg
fracture. Employee #1 was hospitalized for 19 days.
At 7:20 a.m. on November 17, 2020, Employee #1, employed by a steel erection
company, was working at a multi-employer construction project, a new storage
facility.  He was helping load a bundle of stainless steel decking intended for
a hallway.  The load of decking was being lifted by forklift onto steel beams.
As Employee #1 stood near and held onto a beam, the load of decking on the
forklift started to shift and slide off the forks.  Employee #1 moved toward the
forklift.  The falling load struck Employee #1 in the head and pinned him to the
ground.  Employee #1 sustained blunt force traumatic crushing injuries and was
killed.
At 8:12 a.m. on November 13, 2020, Employee #1 and a coworker, employed by an
HVAC company, were repairing a steam piping system leak in the mechanical room
of a medical care campus building.  The employees did not utilize a lockout
and/or tagout device.  Following the repair, as the steam line was being
re-energized, a threaded drip cap at the bottom of the vertical steam pipe riser
apparently failed.  The room immediately filled with pressurized steam.  The
interior door was in the closed position, and the employees were unable to exit
the room.  Employee #1 was killed.
An employee was working as a nursing aide, orderly, or attendant at an assisted
living facility for the elderly. She began to have flu-like symptoms on October
25, 2020. She left work at 9:00 a.m. on October 28, 2020, because she was
coughing so badly that she could not work. She stated that she tested positive
for COVID-19 on October 31, 2020, and that she was admitted to the hospital on
November 1, 2020, for COVID-19. She remained in the hospital until she was
released, on March 15, 2021. The Division was notified on November 12, 2020, by
a representative of the employer. The Division opened an investigation on
November 18, 2020.
On October 21, 2020, Employee #1, employed by a siding company, was installing
downspouts on a commercial building.  He was working from the roof when he came
into contact with a power line and received an electric shock.  The shock caused
him to fall from the roof to the concrete surface.  Employee #1 was transported
to the hospital, where on October 22, 2020 he died from multiple blunt force
traumatic injuries.
At 12:00 a.m. on June 25, 2020, an employee fell from an elevated location and
was killed.
At 1:53 p.m. on November 18, 2020, an employee was killed while traveling on a
mechanic tug.  The employee made a sharp left turn and drove the tug into a
support beam.  The employee was struck in the chest and wedged between the
support beam and the tug's seat support structure.  An hour later the employee
was discovered and pronounced dead at the scene.
At 10:00 a.m. on October 21, 2020,  Employee # 1 was found by a coworker face
down with the torso inside a trash compactor.    Employee #1  was doing normal
routine checks the morning of the accident. There was no eye witness of the
accident and no video was available. According to the Medical Examiner's Office,
the manner of death was multiple blunts injuries of the torso caused by getting
crushed by the trash compactor.
At 9:00 a.m. on November 16, 2020, an employee was pruning rose bushes on the
shoulder of a residential street.  The employee was struck and killed by a
passing motorist.
At 3:00 p.m. on November 11, 2020, an employee was operating a forklift when he
observed that conveyor rollers were not turning. The employee exited the
forklift and began to apply WD-40 lubricant to the conveyor roller bearings.
While using his left gloved hand to rotate the rollers to loosen them, a cube of
bricks advanced on the conveyor and pinched his left ring finger between a cube
of bricks and the roller. The employee sustained a left ring fingertip
amputation. The employee was treated without hospitalization.
At 10:30 a.m. on November 11, 2020, an employee was standing above a hot water
heater, attempting to access the heating element from an elevated work area.
The employee fell to the concrete ground and sustained unspecified injuries to
his hips, legs, and body system.  The employee was hospitalized for treatment.
At 1:00 p.m. on July 17, 2020, an employee was performing his normal work duties
as a wet formation operator for battery manufacturing when he  began to exhibit
signs and symptoms of heat exhaustion. The employee moved to a cooler area of
the facility to recover, but his symptoms continued to worsen. A coworker called
911, and the employee was hospitalized to treat a heat-related illness.
At 12:00 p.m. on August 31, 2020, an employee working as a mason for a masonry
contractor was walking across scaffold planks. The planks collapsed causing the
employee to fall to the ground below. The employee was hospitalized to treat a
fractured ankle.
An employee was working as an auxiliary police officer for a major metropolitan
police department. He was 65 years old. He contracted COVID-19. At 9:00 a.m. on
April 2, 2020, he died from complications related to the COVID-19 coronavirus.
At 4:15 a.m. on November 11, 2020, an employee was sanitizing a batter machine,
while the machine was running. The employee placed his finger in a pump,
contacting a blade. The employee's finger was amputated, and he was
hospitalized.
At 3:30 a.m. on November 14, 2020, Employee #1 was working as a maintenance
mechanic at the employer's metal can production facility.  Employee #1 was
tightening a conveyor belt on press line 2, when his right arm became entangled
in the rotating shaft that drove the conveyor.  Employee #1 had removed a
machine guard to access the conveyor belt and had not locked out the equipment
prior to performing the belt tightening work that was in close proximity to the
rotating shaft. Employee #1 was hospitalized to treat multiple arm fractures and
ladder to climb to an elevated work area. While climbing, the hoist broke,
causing the employee to fall to the ground. Emergency services transported
Employee #1 to the hospital, where he was admitted and treated for a fractured
left femur.
At 5:45 p.m. on December 6, 2020, Employees #1 and #2 and coworkers, employed by
a roofing and siding company, were working at the construction site of a new
two-story residence.  Employees #1 and #2 were repositioning a pump jack
scaffold from the back of the house to another location.  According to a
coworker who witnessed the event, the two employees were in the process of
laying down parallel to the house a 36-foot Alum-A-Pole, part of the scaffold
system, when they appeared to lose control of the pole as a gust of wind came
around the house's corner.  The pole toppled onto energized overhead power lines
8 to 10 feet away, and electrical current flowed through the pole to the
employees.  Employee #1 was electrocuted.  Employee #2 was transported to the
hospital for treatment of electric shock injuries.
At 2:00 p.m. on November 29, 2024, an employee working as a laborer for a marine
cargo handler was sitting on a roll of paper listening to music while wearing
earbuds. A flagger directed the employee to move. The employee moved in the
wrong direction and into the path of a crane carrying a 5,000-pound roll of
paper. The load struck the employee in his left ankle. The employee was
hospitalized to treat a fractured ankle.
At 7:15 a.m. on August 14, 2020, an employee and coworker were handing out masks
to other workers when a nearby Gator (small utility vehicle) backed into the
employee. The employee received blunt force trauma to unspecified body parts and
was killed.
At 9:30 a.m. on December 1, 2020, an employee working for a plastics
manufacturer was using an air hose to clean the Line #9 Brown Thermoformer
machine while it was still running. The employee caught her hand in the conveyer
chain. The employee was hospitalized to treat partially amputated fingers on her
right hand.
At approximately 7:00 p.m. on December 6, 2020, Employee #1 and Employee #2
worked on a pipe/valve repair project in the Pipe Shop. They were working
alongside each other. A coworker was diagnosed with COVID-19 on or about
November 24, 2020, with the first symptoms occurring on or about November 18,
2020. Based on the contact tracing of another employee that tested postitive for
COVID-19, the employee was sent home to quarantine on or about November 20,
2020. Employee #1 died on December 6, 2020 and Employee #2 died on  December 10,
2020, due to potential COVID-19 related complications.
At 9:30 a.m. on September 30, 2020, an employee was working for a polyurethane
products manufacturer operating a Fecken-Kirfel Hole Bore Machine in the large
peeler area. The employee was positioned on the southside of the machine and
needed to move to the northside. There were materials stored around the machine
including, but not limited to, boxes and silicone. The materials blocked the
employee from going around the machine, so he stepped across the machine. While
stepping across the machine, the employee realized that he could not fit and he
became stuck between the 20-foot long by3-foot diameter foam roll and the
agricultural cooperative was climbing a ladder on the front of a grain trailer.
The employee lost his balance and fell from the ladder to the gravel driveway
below. The employee was hospitalized to treat multiple injuries including a
concussion and lacerations, fractures and contusions to his head, ribs, chest
and back.
At 4:40 p.m. on March 5, 2021, six employees were working to isolate a leaking
gas line by squeezing off lines feeding the damaged section. During the process,
the gas leak found an ignition source, causing an explosion and fire. Employees
standing near the sidewalk and in the bell hole sustained second- and
third-degree burns. Emergency services transported the employees to the
hospital.  Three employees were hospitalized, and three others were treated
without hospitalization.
An employee was working for a ranch and rodeo employer and was on leave when he
tested positive for COVID-19 and required hospitalization for treatment of his
infection at 1:56 p.m. on October 21, 2020.
An employee worked as a Physician for a general medical and surgical hospital.
The employee's last day of work was November 9, 2020. The employee had treated a
COVID-19 positive patient prior to becoming ill himself. The employee began to
exhibit COVID-19 related symptoms on November 9, 2020, but tested negative on
November 10, 2020. The employee retested on November 16, 2020, and received a
positive test result. On November 17, 2020, the employee was hospitalized for
treatment and was released on November 21, 2020. The employer did not have
Adequate Aerosol Transmissible Diseases policies and procedures in place.
At 1:15 p.m. on March 5, 2021, Employee #1 worked alone at the base of an
elevator shaft, retrieving a cell phone for a tenant. Employee #1 was caught in
between the elevator's moving hoist ropes and sheave. Employee #1 was killed.
An employee was working as a corrections officer when he was exposed to inmates
and coworkers infected with COVID-19. The employee tested positive for COVID-19
on November 27, 2020, and was admitted to the hospital December 6, 2020. The
employee died on December 20, 2020, due to COVID-19 complications.
An employee was working as an anesthesia technician in the operating room of a
children's hospital when he contracted COVID-19. The employee began feeling ill
on November 17, 2020 and was admitted to the hospital on November 19, 2020. The
employee died on December 21, 2020, due COVID-19 complications.
In early 2021, an employee was working as a nurse practitioner at an assisted
living facility for the elderly. She prepared and delivered medications. Her
last day of work was January 27, 2021. She began exhibiting symptoms of COVID-19
two days later, on the 29th. She tested positive on the 30th, before being
hospitalized. At 3:00 p.m. on February 10, 2021, she died.
At 7:30 p.m. on March 1, 2021, an employee worked to install framing rafters on
a roof. At some point, the employee fell approximately ten feet and killed by
blunt force injury to the head.
Employees worked in a skilled nursing facility that had an outbreak of COVID-19
including 11 employees and 7 clients starting at the beginning of July, 2020.
Fourteen employees tested positive for COVID-19 in the month of July, 2020.  Two
employees were hospitalized for treatment of COVID-19.  Employee #1, the
assistant director of nursing, performed administrative and clerical duties and
did not provide care to the residents but did provide fit testing to the nursing
staff. Employee #1 was transported from home and hospitalized on the evening of
July 19, 2020. Employee #2, a licensed practical nurse who provided care to
residents in the facility and was married to a spouse who is a nurse providing
treatment.
An employee was working as a social worker at a general medical or surgical
hospital. As a social worker, she performed interventions. She visited
individuals who had been referred to her and who were experiencing mental health
crises at their homes or other places in the community. The employee traveled to
different communities around Queens County, NY. She contracted COVID-19. On
December 28, 2020, she tested positive for COVID-19 and was hospitalized.  On
January 21, 2021, she died.
At 3:40 p.m. on January 12, 2021, an employee assisted a coworker operating an
excavator with felling trees and cutting them into smaller sections. The
excavator operator completed felling a tree and began to work on a second one
when the operator realized that the first tree landed on top of the employee.
The employee was killed by unspecified injuries as a result of being stuck by a
tree limb.
At 1:00 p.m. on January 20, 2021, an employee was getting off the roof when he
lost his footing and caused the ladder to slip. The employee subsequently fell
off the ladder (19-foot fall) and sustained a fracture to his left leg.  The
employee was hospitalized.
At 4:00 p.m. on January 26, 2021, an employee worked to place a tarp over
freshly poured concrete while standing on an elevated, snowy work platform. The
employee fell approximately seven feet from the platform and was killed due to a
severe head injury.
An employee was working as a physical therapist at an outpatient care center. He
contracted COVID-19. He was hospitalized.  At 2:30 p.m. on January 21, 2021, he
died from complications of COVID-19 while in the hospital.
An employee was working in the kitchen of a skilled nursing facility when she
was exposed to patients and coworkers infected with COVID-19. The employee
contracted COVID-19 and subsequently died from her infection at 8:00 a.m. on
December 20, 2020.
At 10:00 a.m. on January 19, 2021, an employee was standing on a 10 foot ladder
stand brushing snow off a truck roof. The employee fell and struck his head on
the floor, killing him.
At 8:00 a.m. on September 9, 2020, an employee was smoothing a steel workpiece
with sandpaper on the Haas CNC lathe. The employee's glove was caught on a burr
on the steel workpiece. The employee fractured the right index finger and
dislocated a knuckle.  The employee was treated without hospitalization.
An employee was working as a volunteer fire police captain for a volunteer fire
department. For some unknown reason, one that was not work-related, he was
exposed to severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2). He
contracted COVID-19.  On January 23, 2021, he died as a result.
At 4:24 p.m. on August 10, 2020, an employee was attempting to drive a Crown
RC3000 Series Stand-Up Powered Industrial Truck (PIT) onto a flatbed tow truck.
As the employee drove the three wheeled PIT up the ramp, the hard smooth tires
began began to lose traction on the diamond plate bed deck and the began to roll
backward down the ramp. The PIT veered to the left and tipped partially off the
truck bed. The employee  jumped from the PIT and when as he jumped, he pinned
his left foot between the PIT and a metal guard pole that was cemented near the
warehouse roll up door. The employee crushed his toes requiring hospitalization
and later amputation of his 3rd and 5th toes.
At 9:45 a.m. on January 23, 2021, an employee was felling a tree when the
employee was struck by a falling tree. The employee suffered blunt force trauma
to his torso, killing him.
At 2:15 p.m. on January 7, 2021, Employee #1 was performing setup operations on
a mechanical power press. While attempting to remove a part from the press, the
supervisor cycled the machine as Employee #1's hand was inside the die area. The
incident resulted in the crushing of three fingers: the middle, ring, and tip of
the small finger on the employee's right hand. Due to the extent of the
injuries, medical amputation of the affected fingers was required. Employee #1
was transported to the hospital, admitted, and treated for the injuries.
At 8:45 a.m. on November 10, 2020, an employee was sweeping grain into a floor
auger inside a grain bin. The employee stepped in an unguarded opening on the
floor leading to the floor auger. The employee's right leg was amputated above
the knee.  The employee was hospitalized.
An employee was working as a health aide at a nursing care or skilled nursing
facility. It was a retirement community. She worked as an activities
coordinator. For some unstated reason, she contracted COVID-19.  At 10:00 a.m.
on January 6, 2021, she died.
At 11:00 a.m. on July 27, 2020, an employee and a coworker (supervisor) were
moving a vehicle utilizing a back hoe (PIT) and and a chain hoist to lift the
vehicle with the front bucket of the back hoe. The employee was attempting to
unhook the sling from underneath the front bumper of the vehicle and but the
hooks were stuck onto the bumper. The employee hand signalled his coworker who
was operating the back hoe to lower the bucket. The coworker interpreted the
hand signal as to lift the bucket and consequently pinched the employee's index
finger between the sling and the hook. The employee amputated his finger and
required hospitalization.
An employee had been working for a supermarket chain. On December 9, 2020, the
employee reported experiencing COVID-19 related symptoms to the company nurse.
The employee's symptoms included fever, chills, severe headache, body aches,
coughing, and difficulty breathing or shortness of breath. On December 17, 2020,
the employee went to the hospital. On that same day, the employee was tested for
COVID-19 and received a positive test result. In the hospital the employee was
diagnosed with congestive heart failure and pneumonia due to his COVID-19
infection and was administered oxygen. On December 28, 2020, employee was
discharged from the hospital. The employee had been off work from December 7,
2020 to February 25, 2021. The employee reported he is still experiencing
employee.  The employee was crushed by the semi-truck and was killed.
At 1:15 p.m. on January 5, 2021, Employee #1, was observing a valve when the
valve was opened, causing the pump to fail and spray acid. The acid caused
chemical burns to the employee's back and neck. Emergency services were called,
and Employee #1 was transported to the hospital, where he was admitted and
treated for the burns.
At 12:40 p.m. on December 28, 2020, an employee was cutting trees in an almond
orchard using a STIHL MS 271 chainsaw (Serial No. 511319280). During the cutting
process, the chainsaw became caught on a branch. In an attempt to pull the
branch out of the chainsaw, the employee's glove became entangled in the chain,
resulting in a laceration to the employee's right hand. The employee received 18
stitches for the injury. The employee was hospitalized for treatment. This
incident highlights the risks associated with using chainsaws and the need for
proper safety precautions to prevent entanglement and lacerations.
At 2:00 p.m. on August 21, 2020, an employee was working as a maintenance
technician for a city preschool department. The employee was walking out of
building onto a dirt parking lot when he stepped on a nail lacerating his foot.
The employee went home that day without reporting the injury to his employer.
The next day the employee went to emergency room. The employee was seen by
medical personnel, treated and released. On September 2, 2020, the employee
noticed his foot had become infected. The employee was admitted to hospital with
toe infection requiring his toe be amputated.
At 10:30 a.m. on January 8, 2021, Employee #1, employed in electrical work, was
preparing to hang a guidewire. The employee went to cover a phase that was
energized but mistakenly covered the neutral phase, which was not energized.
While attempting to hang the guidewire, Employee #1 thought he was making
contact with the deenergized neutral but instead made contact with an energized
electrical line that was not covered. The employee sustained an electrical shock
and electrical burns to the left hand and right forearm, which led to subsequent
transradial arm amputations. Emergency services transported the employee to the
hospital for admission and treatment.
At 3:45 p.m. on July 17, 2020, an employee was moving freight containers on a
deck when the employee was struck in the groin by a container. The employee
suffered a bruise and internal bleeding and was hospitalized.
At 4:00 p.m. on January 11, 2021, Employee #1 from Police Department #1
responded to a vehicle crash when one of the drivers involved in the crash
opened fire on him with an AK-47 killing him instantly. The driver then car
jacked a vehicle and took off toward the airport. Employee #2 from and Employee
#3, both from Police Department #2, pursued the driver until he stopped and shot
Employee #2, killing him. Employee #3 was injured in the leg and hospitalized.
As the driver attempted to flee in the car a second time, he struck Employee #4
from Police Department #1 with the car, killing him.  See also investigation
summary ID 132467.
An employee worked as a Maintenance Worker for a sports gym and swimming
facility. On December 10, 2020, the employee was feeling ill, did not go to work
and got tested. On December 11, 2020, he received a positive test result. At
4:00 p.m. on December 15, 2020, the employee had difficulty breathing and went
to the hospital, where he was admitted.  He was discharged on December 18, 2020.
On December 27, 2020, he returned to work. On December 11, 2020, the employer
tested the remaining staff who received their results that day. Coworker #1,
also a Maintenance Worker, confirmed he was positive for COVID-19 but was
asymptomatic. The remaining employees were retested one week later, and all were
negative. Coworker #1 is the older brother of the employee, and they reside
together in a 2 bedroom, 1 bathroom apartment along with 3 other family members
including the employee's wife and their parents. All of them tested positive for
COVID-19 after the employee was diagnosed. The employee and Coworker #1 also
carpool to work together. On December 13, 2020, the girlfriend of Coworker #2, a
bookkeeper who is the employee's daughter, tested positive for COVID-19. On
December 15, 2020, Coworker #3 developed symptoms, was tested and confirmed
positive for COVID-19 that same day. Coworker #3 lived with the girlfriend of
Coworker #2. Both employees stated they wear face coverings every day and they
do not eat together at work. They also stated that they were provided COVID-19
safety training by the employer, and they usually work on their own at the job
site. Since Employee #2 is asymptomatic, they do not know if Employee #1
infected Employee #2 or vice versa. Neither of them knew who was infected first
and how they were infected. The source of the initial infection could not be
determined, but the other infections appear to be community-acquired. The
employer did not have an effective COVID-19 Prevention Program in place.
At approximately 12:00 p.m. on January 1, 2021, an employee contracted the
COVID-19 and later died from complications from the virus.
At 2:00 p.m. on October 9, 2020, an employee was working for a firm that made
cardboard boxes for various consumer products. He was a machine operator. He was
working in the finishing department. He was setting up a model number L2BDC
Flexo-Folder-Gluer machine, with serial number 15400. The machine was not
deenergized. The employee placed his right hand between two unguarded in-rolling
rollers to make an adjustment to the folder portion of the machine. The machine
started moving, and the employee's hand was crushed between the rollers. The
employee was hospitalized. The firm's s managers knew that employees set up the
equipment prior to each job. The managers stated that the equipment being used
was quite old and that only trained employees operated the machinery. One
manager stated that he was not sure why the employee went into the area that he
did. Nonetheless, he stated the machine was not locked out and the employees
were at the end of the set-up process. This manager had a third-party vendor
come in and place guards with a chain and lock all around the equipment to
prevent employees from being able to reach into the machinery. The manager also
stated that it was company policy to lock out equipment when employees were
performing any type of servicing or maintenance. The company provided lockout
training to employees as affected employees but did not enforce that employees
lock out the equipment out during the set-up process.
At 3:15 p.m. on November 4, 2020, Employee #1, operating a press brake machine,
was performing routine tasks when his fingers became caught in a pinch point.
The employee was immediately injured, and emergency services were called. The
employee was transported to the hospital, where he was admitted for treatment
for the amputation of the fingers.
At 10:45 a.m. on January 6, 2021, Employee #1 responded to a request for
assistance from a coworker, who was attempting to rewind a steel coil. Employee
#1 had been training the coworker on press operations. While the coworker was
working the controls to rewind the coil, the steel began "bunching up" because
all of the hold-downs, which maintain tension on the coil, were released.
Without sufficient tension, the rewind occurred faster than normal, causing the
coil to become crooked. Employee #1 began assisting the coworker in
straightening the coil at the mandrel but failed to lock out the equipment.
While positioned between the coil and the coil blade, Employee #1 manually
adjusted the coil. As Employee #1 was holding the loose coil winds in place, he

At 11:25 p.m. on February 21, 2021, an employee was in the process of stripping
the outer layer of stranded aluminum cable using a stripping machine. The

housing unit that guards the point of operation. The employee reached between

At 3:30 p.m. on Friday, March 19, 2021, an employee was working for a millwork
firm. She was in the flooring area, operating a Cross Cut Solutions model number
CS14ML pop-up saw, with serial 0504-08, saw number 6 at the facility, to cut
pieces of flooring. She was using her right hand to remove defective pieces of
wood flooring from a feed conveyor, place the pieces under the saw, make a cut
in the center of the defect, and place the pieces on the outfeed conveyor with
her left hand. The employee was holding a piece of wood with her right hand,
when the blade contacted the wood. The contact resulted in a loud popping noise,
and the wood jumped. This jump caused the piece of wood to be pulled under the
guard into the blade, along with the employee's right hand. The employee
suffered the total amputation of her index and middle fingers, a partial
amputation and a fracture of her ring finger, and a laceration of her thumb. She
was hospitalized. Her ring finger was reattached during surgery. The employee
stated that her right foot was positioned on the foot pedal. She believed that
when the wood jumped, it startled her into pressing the foot pedal again. That
caused the saw blade to rise and strike her hand. In the flooring area of the
site and possibly other areas, the firm had six Cross Cut Solutions pop-up saws.
The model numbers and facility numbers for all six saws were: saw number 1,
model number CS14MLH, serial number 160203; saw number 2, model number CS14MLH,
serial number 151214; saw number 3, model number CS14ML, serial number 120102;
saw number 4, model number CS14ML, serial number 120105; saw number 5, model
number CS14ML, serial number 120101; and saw number 6, model number CS14ML,
serial number 0504-08. All six saws were operated by foot pedal. All had been in
place for over 20 years. Employees operating saws on the day of the inspection
stated in interviews they had at some time unintentionally struck the foot pedal
and activated the saw inadvertently.
At 8:30 a.m. on April 7, 2021, an employee was using a hand tool to remove
screws from the main distribution electrical panel while disconnecting the four
OTT conductors. During this task, the employee came into contact with electrical
current, resulting in electrical shocks and burns. The employee was treated for
the injuries and was hospitalized for further care. This incident highlights the
critical importance of following lockout/tagout procedures and ensuring proper
deenergization of electrical systems before conducting maintenance work.
At 7:30 a.m. on November 20, 2020, an employee was de-icing air valves at a chop
saw from an I-beam.  The employee fell from an elevated location below the chop
saw. The employee was hospitalized to treat an open frontal skull fracture,
fractures of the left distal radius and ulna, and loss of vision in his right
eye.

outcome.

At 11:30 a.m. on April 1, 2021, an employee who was contracted to perform
temporary work at a steel fabrication shop was asked by a coworker to help them
move a heavy steel frame with other coworkers.  While lifting the steel frame,
the employee's third digit finger on his right hand became caught between
between two tubular steel pieces.  The employee's middle finger on his right

transported to a surgery center and released the same day.

Hanrich Corporation dba Tasty Plus Foods. The employee approached a dough

while it was in operation. Her right hand was caught between the rollers,

supervisor, who was in another room, responded to the employee's calls for help
and assisted her. The employee was hospitalized at Los Angeles County USC
Medical Center for treatment.  The accident was reported by telephone on
November 23, 2020, at 4:40 p.m., and Cal/OSHA initiated an accident
investigation at 11:20 a.m. on November 24, 2020. The employer complied with the
reporting requirements outlined in T8CCR 342.
At 9:45 a.m. on April 22, 2021, an employee worked to install an asphalt ridge
cap. The employee fell approximately thirteen feet and was killed.

An employee was on vacation for approximately one week and returned to normal
duties in the Meat Department for  one day.  The employee contracted COVID-19

At 11:08 a.m. on February 13, 2021, an employee was working with a coworker
conducting gardening operations at a residence. The employee had been loading
yard waste into a dump trailer when he collapsed to the ground. He was later
found by a passerby and the coworker in front of the residence. The homeowner
called 911 and performed CPR. The fire department arrived and continued CPR and
an ambulance transported the employee to the hospital, where he later died.
At 8:45 a.m. on March 16, 2021, Employee #1, a laborer employed by an
agricultural company, was servicing a 1982 Ford Field Cultivator at the
employer's shop and yard. The employee and a supervisor were preparing to lower
the cultivator's wings for maintenance when the left wing unexpectedly fell. The
supervisor had pulled the pin securing the wing, expecting the hydraulic system
to hold it in place. However, the hydraulics failed, causing the wing to
collapse. Employee #1 attempted to move away but was struck by the falling wing.
The employee sustained serious internal injuries, including a perforated
stomach, fractured ribs, a concussion, and a head laceration, and was
hospitalized for nearly a month and a half. The employer had not implemented
precautionary measures to prevent hydraulic failure after the equipment had been
idle over the winter. No accident-related citations were issued.
At 8:23 a.m. on October 28, 2020, an employee working as an automobile mechanic
for a repair shop was preparing to work on a customer pickup truck that had a
malfunctioning AC unit. The employee was positioned under the dashboard on
floorboard of truck when he reached up to turn the ignition. The truck began to
roll crushing the employee between driver door and vehicle lift. The employee
was hospitalized to treat a lacerated lower leg and a fractured right pelvis.
At 7:30 p.m. on August 20, 2020, an employee who had been working as a cook in
the kitchen of a senior living facility was hospitalized with COVID-19. On
August 18, 2020, the employer tested the entire kitchen staff for COVID-19. Five
out of the fifteen workers, including the employee, were positive for COVID-19.
At the time, the employer required face coverings in the workplace, but it was
not rigorously enforced in the kitchen area. In addition, the kitchen area was
an enclosed space with minimal ventilation. The employer did not have an
effective COVID-19 Prevention Program in place.
At 9:42 a.m. on October 20, 2020, an employee was walking on the pier. The

At 6:15 p.m. on April 13, 2021, an employee worked on a roof, fell approximately

At 10:30 a.m. on April 6, 2021, an employee entered the Dapec area to
investigate a clicking sound. During the inspection, he failed to lock out the
Dapec line before entering the area between the rehang and grading section,
where the drum and thigh blade were located. The employee did not notify his

laceration to his upper right arm and was hospitalized for treatment.
An employee was working as a police officer for a large city police department
when he was infected with COVID-19. On November 27, 2020, the employee was
transported to a regional medical center for the treatment for COVID-19 and he

At 3:00 p.m. on April 12, 2021, an employee working as a machine operator for a
structural steel manufacturer was adjusting steel strips in a bandsaw. The
employee activated the hydraulic clamp to hold the material in place. He did not
remove his hand and caught his right thumb tip in the machine. The employee
received medical treatment without hospitalization for an amputated thumb tip.
At approximately 12:00 p.m. on February 23, 2021, Employee #1 was cleaning dust
from the roaster drum. While cleaning, the employee slipped, and in an attempt
to prevent a fall, placed his right hand to support himself. His hand landed on
the pinch point between the metal wheels and the roaster drum. The employee
sustained compound fractures to his middle finger and severe crushing injuries
to his right-hand ring finger. The employee was hospitalized and treated for the
fractures and crushing injuries. This incident emphasizes the importance of
maintaining awareness of pinch points during cleaning tasks and using
appropriate fall protection measures when working in potentially hazardous
areas.
At 12:30 p.m. on April 10, 2021, an employee was directing traffic to allow a
garbage truck to back up when an automobile came around the stopped truck and
struck the employee dragging him 50 feet. The employee died from injuries to his
head and upper body.
At approximately 12:00 a.m. on July 29, 2020, an employee was operating an ATV
for farm ground maintenance when it rolled over, pinning the employee beneath.
The approximate elapsed time to extraction was 45 minutes, but died at the
scene.
At 9:45 a.m. on April 10, 2021, Employee #1 was leaving the area after
installing the keeper when the employee stepped on a looper block. The
employee's foot became caught between the looper mechanical stop and the
mechanical block. The injury resulted in a partial amputation of the employee's
left foot. The employee was transported to the hospital for admission and
treatment.
At 9:30 a.m. on April 14, 2021, an employee was on a scissor lift to remove
racks. As the scissor lift operator backed the lift to the rack, the employee
was caught between the rack and lift. The employee received trauma to the chest
and was killed.
At 1:14 p.m. on April 7, 2021, Employee #1 was operating a Stamco rivet press
(Serial No. 2521) at a metal culvert manufacturing facility. While assembling a
12-inch culvert pipe, Employee #1 was feeding a rivet beneath the press punch
when the machine cycled, crushing his left index finger. The rivet press, a
full-revolution press operated by a foot pedal, was equipped with a mechanical
safety sensor intended to detect hands or fingers in the punch area. However, at
the time of the incident, the sensor was not functioning properly and did not
detect the employee's finger. Additionally, the sensor probe design allowed the
employee to reach into the punch area by reaching over it. Employee #1 sustained
crushing injuries that resulted in a partial surgical amputation of his left
index finger. The employee was treated without hospitalization.
An employee worked in an unspecified capacity for a machine shop. The employee
had close personal contact with a coworker who had been experiencing COVID-19
related symptoms and who later tested positive for COVID-19. The employee was
tested on November 17, 2020, and was asymptomatic at the time he was tested. The
employee's test results came back positive on November 18, 2020. The employee
went home to quarantine. During the quarantine, the employee did not develop
symptoms. The employer tested six additional coworkers during this time. Since
the employee had a kidney transplant earlier in the year, he was instructed to
report to the hospital to have his oxygen levels checked. At that time, he was
admitted into the hospital. The employee died on December 13, 2020, due to
COVID-19 related complications.
An employee was working for a paper manufacturer. He was a safety and health

moved the pallet jack forward out of the bay, then reversed it suddenly. As a

The employee was hospitalized to treat a fractured lower right leg.
At 7:30 a.m. on March 16, 2021, Employee #1 was attempting to clear a wood jam
in a machine. The operator had turned off the saw, but the blades were still
spinning when the employee reached in to remove the obstruction. The employee

injury. Employee #1 was hospitalized for treatment.
At 9:00 p.m. on January 20, 2021, two maintenance employees were performing a
filter change on a purple K pump due to lower than usual suction identified
throughout the day on the first shift. After replacing the filter, they began
re-installing the butterfly valve, which fits between the pipe flanges. Due to
limited clearance, the maintenance workers used a pry bar in an attempt to
create more space to allow the butterfly valve to move into place more fluidly.
The employee was pushing the valve back into place but pushed the valve too far.
The employee reached on the top of the valve to pull it back, while the coworker
continued to use the pry bar to create space. During the process, the pry bar
slipped, and the employee's fingers became caught between the valve and the top
flange. The employee initially suffered a crush injury to his right ring finger
and was treated without hospitalization.  Later, a decision was made by a
hydraulic excavator.  Employee #1 was waiting and planning the next spoil pile
to be removed with the excavator.  While the excavator operator was rotating his
tracks to move up the road, Employee # 1 was struck by the left side track, and
his left foot was crushed.  Employee #1 was hospitalized for treatment of a
brain hemorrhage, crushing injuries to the left foot, and a degloving (avulsion)
of the skin on the left foot.
At 4:15 p.m. on March 15, 2021, Employee #1 and Employee #2 were repairing a
hole in the spent oil tank when the tank exploded. Employee #1 was killed and
Employee #2 was hospitalized with 3rd degree burns and blunt force trauma
injuries.
An employee was working as a school resource officer in a city school system
when he was exposed to students and coworkers infected with COVID-19. The
employee contracted COVID-19 and subsequently died from his infection at 9:00

At approximately 4:10 p.m. on March 15, 2021, an employee, working for a framing

flooring. The employee was getting ready to shut down the machine and looked
away from the switch. The board made contact with the rotating blade of the
table saw and pulled the left hand of the employee into the exposed blade. The
employee was hospitalized and treated for amputation of 4 fingers to the left
hand.
At approximately 12:30 a.m. on March 14, 2021, Employee #1 was attempting to
load wire into the feed rollers of a straighten and cut machine. While manually
holding the wire in place, the feed rollers closed on her left middle finger.
The feed rollers were inadequately guarded at the time of the incident. As a
