and was hospitalized for treatment.
At 11:30 a.m. on March 10, 2021, an employee was repairing the tines of a dozer
rake and used a spot weld to hold the piece of equipment in an upright position.
The spot weld broke and the rake fell over, crushing and killing the employee.
At 5:15 a.m. on March 13, 2021, an employee attempted to load a two thousand,
one hundred and twenty-two pound crate of commercial glass onto a flat trailer.
At some point, the crate fell back on top of the employee who received multiple,
blunt force trauma injuries to the entire body. The employee was killed by the
crushing injuries.
At 1:00 p.m. on March 16, 2021,  an employee attempted to move slabs of quartz,
each measuring approximately 65 inches by 128 inches. The employee was crushed
vertically between two of the slabs and sustained injuries to the abdomen and
chest before dying.
At 10:30 a.m. on March 2, 2021, an employee was preparing to help spin a boat so
that fiberglass could be sprayed onto the other half of the boat hull. As the
mold over-spun, the employee's left pointer finger became caught between the
frame and the mold. The employee yanked his hand out, resulting in an amputation
to the first joint of his left pointer finger. The employee was treated without
hospitalization. The injury was caused by the mold being positioned too close to
the frame during the process.
At 6:00 a.m. on February 12, 2021, an employee working as a molding machine
operator for a milk producer was operating a blowmold machine producing plastic
milk jugs. The employee was using a hand tool to roll the mold. The employee
reached into the machine and caught her jacket on the corner of the unguarded
mold frame. The employee extended her hand forward in order to dislodge her
jacket from the mold. At this point, she caught four fingers in the closing mold
for 6 to 8 seconds. The employee was hospitalized to treat four amputated
fingers.

torch when a flashback condition occurred with the torch equipment. This
malfunction caused both the propane and oxygen tanks to explode, resulting in

At 11:45 a.m. on September 25, 2020, an employee was deboning a carcass.  The

At 9:15 a.m. on June 18, 2020, Employee #1 was working for a residential general

Employee #1 was cutting a piece of wood when his hand contacted the blade.
Employee #1 sustained a laceration and was treated and released from Harbor UCLA
Medical Center.
At 12:15 p.m. on October 19, 2020, an employee working as a quality assurance
inspector for a machine shop was walking next to a forklift that was

load during transport when the load shifted. The employee caught his hand
between the fork and the load. The employee amputated his right index fingertip
and was hospitalized.
At 9:00 a.m. on November 30, 2020, an employee working as a health aide for a
home health service was bathing a client. The employee slipped on the floor
while returning the shower hose. The employee was hospitalized to treat
transverse fracture to her back due to impact with the floor.
At 12:10 p.m. on February 2, 2021, an employee experienced a same-level fall
after tripping over an empty pallet and falling into a metal railing, striking
his left shoulder and right leg. On March 2, 2021, the employee had surgery on a
ruptured quadricep, directly related to the injuries sustained from his fall. He

At 2:40 p.m. on December 8, 2020, Employee #1 was descending a set of stairs in

At 8:30 a.m. on March 8, 2021, an employee was removing a guard to change the
lead screw on Tapper 6. The machine was not locked out, and the operator came
back to the machine and accidentally activated the machine while the employee's
hands were in the machine. The employee's left ring finger was caught in a belt

hospitalization.
At approximately 12:30 PM on March 12, 2025, an employee, working for a
transportation agency, was training on equipment. Employee #1 was being trained
by a coworker on how to reset/repair a Crash Attenuator.  Employee #1 and the
coworker were preparing to reset/repair a collapsed TAU II Crash Attenuator by
using an International 3-ton dump truck, connected by an approximately 6-foot
alloy steel chain with hooks on each end, to pull the collapsed Crash Attenuator
out for the reset.  The chain was first hooked to the nose of the Crash
Attenuator by running the chain over the front top horizontal frame member. The
top horizontal Crash Attenuator frame member is a steel U-channel ran openside
down.  Employee #1 and the coworker engaged the chain hook on the back underside
of the steel U-channel.  They then hooked the other end of the chain to the
front of the dump truck. The coworker left Employee #1 by the nose of the Crash
Attenuator and got into the cab of the dump truck.  Employee #1 had on leather
work gloves. Employee #1 gave the coworker the ok to back up.  Employee #1 saw
there was slack in the chain and took hold of the chain with the left hand to
was ejected resulting in critical injuries. He was able to call a coworker who
called 911 and initiated a search for the employee.  The employee was airlifted
to the hospital, but became unresponsive on the way and died.
At 2:00 p.m. on March 30, 2021, Employee #1, employed by a road construction
company, was working with coworkers on a road construction clean up crew.  They
were in the road and gathering the last pieces of traffic control equipment.  No
traffic control equipment remained to warn drivers away from the lane where they
were working.  A semi-truck drove over a hill and struck Employee #1.  Employee
#1 sustained blunt force traumatic injuries and was killed.
At 1:25 a.m. on March 19, 2021, an employee was standing at counter when an
individual entered store and shot the employee, killing him.
In January 2021, an employee was working as a farm worker supervisor at a crop
the power lines. Upon arriving at the job site, the employee and coworkers

At approximately 2:30 p.m. on July 8, 2021, an employee was repairing a water
line of the furnace arm during a scheduled shut down.  The employee reported

At approximately 11:00 a.m. on June 16, 2021, an employee was laying down a

The employee suffered a fractured fibula, head and possible internal injuries.
At approximately 6:00 a.m. on September 12, 2014, an employee was directing the
Medical-Surgical 3C Unit. The employee had a migraine headache and fever. The

At approximately 3:00 p.m. on June 24, 2021, an employee was attempting to carry
a 45-pound solar panel up an extension ladder to complete the final installation
above the front door of a residence. Other employees were unavailable to assist.
The employee carried the panel in his right hand while ascending the ladder. The

Although they did not report injury from the fall itself, the solar panel landed
on his left leg, resulting in fractures. The employee was hospitalized for
treatment.

At 12:00 noon on July 13, 2021, an employee was mowing grass next to a drainage
ditch when the tractor's tire got stuck in a hole. A coworker was contacted to
help him get the tractor freed. The employees hooked a chain to the tractor and
as they were pulling it another wheel fell into a hole causing the chain to come
free and the tractor to start to tip. The employee tried to jump free of the
tractor but was struck by the rollover protection system and roof of the tractor
as it rolled over onto him. The employee died from his injuries.
At approximately 6:00 a.m. on September 12, 2014, an employee was standing on
the inside of the bay No. 1 east exit opening (raised overhead shop door),
slightly off its center towards the driver's side of the oncoming vehicle. The

had dismounted from the tractor.
At 3:30 p.m. on February 15th, 2022, Employee #1 who was working at a
manufacturing company, pushed the wrong button that advanced the tail stock
spindle instead of clamping it. Her finger got caught in the spindle that
resulted in a puncture wound. Employee #1 was treated without hospitalization.
At 5:24 p.m. on February 16, 2022, an employee was filling trays with onions to
send through the Maxwell Chase MCT-ITS Tray Sealer. The employee went to load
more trays into the tray sealer, and they realized the machine was running out
of plastic film and was jammed. The employee reached underneath the guard at the
exit of the tray sealer to remove a strip of jammed film. The machine was not
powered down at this point and the sealing plate inside the machine came down
while the employee's hand was inside. The sealing plate contacted the thumb and
first finger of her left hand, partially amputating them. The employee was
hospitalized for treatment.
At 6:15 a.m. on October 26, 2021, two employees were starting-up an asphalt
plant for the morning shift. While conducting start-up procedures and
inspections, the employees discovered the ignitors to the west-side liquid
propane gas (LP-Gas) vaporizers were not staying lit and began troubleshooting.
The vaporizers are fed LP-Gas through steel piping connected to a storage tank
100 feet away, with pilot flames used to ignite the vaporizers that heat the
dryer drum and liquid asphalt storage tanks. The employees locked out the
electrical breaker switch for the affected vaporizer unit and turned the in-line
valve to the closed position to block LP-Gas flow. The employees did not turn
off the east-side LP-Gas vaporizer's pilot flame. Employee #1 opened the drip
leg valve on the side of the vaporizer cabinet and burner pressure tap to
relieve pressure and drain remaining LP-Gas. The employees decided to replace
folding ladder to place a box on a shelf above. The employee climbed to step
just below the top of the ladder.  While attempting to place the box on top of
the shelf, the ladder suddenly twisted under the employee.  Employee #1 fell to
the floor and died from head injuries.
At 10:45 a.m. on November 9, 2021, an employee was constructing the foundation
for an in-ground pool.  The employee attempted to stop a run away pick up truck,
when he was struck by and dragged by the vehicle.  He was killed due to blunt
force trauma to the head and torso.
At 7:44 a.m. on February 2, 2022, an employee was bringing animals into the
clinic, speaking with customers, and prior to the incident had been speaking
with the clinic manager. The employee was speaking with the clinic manager, when
she stated that she felt light-headed. The clinic manager went to retrieve food
for the employee. Upon the clinic manager's return, s/he observed the employee
slouched over and unresponsive in the lobby. The employee was found unresponsive
at the jobsite and transported to the hospital, where she was pronounced dead.
There were no jobsite hazards that the employee was exposed to.
At 2:00 p.m. on March 26, 2022, Employee #1, an assistant store manager, was
leaving the retail store to go to the clearance store, so that she could check
on the employees at the clearance store.  Using her Drive Walker, Employee #1
went out the front door of the retail store, then sat down on the Drive Walker
seat and started to push herself backwards down a slight grade down to the
clearance store.  As Employee #1 was going down the grade, she picked up speed
but was dragging her feet and using the hand brakes on the Drive Walker to slow
down.  As she was navigating to go around a support column, her wheel/wheels got
caught in a crack in the public sidewalk that stopped the walker and caused her
to flip over the walker, striking her head on the concrete.  Employee #1 was
killed.
At 1:15 p.m. on March 30, 2022, an employee was preparing for final refuse
collection rounds of the university campus, when he suffered a medical event
leading to his death.  The medical event was acute coronary insufficiency.
At 1:30 a.m. on March 17, 2022, an employee was moving an aerial lift, when it
tipped over. The employee was thrown from the lift. The employee suffered broken
bones and internal injuries. The employee was killed from falling from the lift.
At 1:00 p.m. on January 2, 2022, an employee was standing on top of a ship
behind a guardrail-type system and bent over to look inside a pit on a ship that
was being unloaded by a crane. The crane operator was lowering his clamshell
bucket into the pit to retrieve ash and struck the employee. The employee was
decapitated (head & arm).
At 12:00 p.m. on December 14, 2021, an employee worked to repair the ridge cap
of a pole barn. As the employee stepped over the ridge cap to unscrew bolts, the
employee slipped on ice and fell approximately nineteen feet. The employee was
taken to the hospital and admitted to treat fractures to both ankles.
At 7:30 p.m. on March 28, 2022, an employee was going down a flight of steps in
a residential group home, when he fell to the bottom of the steps onto concrete.
The employee was killed due to a head injury.
At 12:00 p.m. on March 28, 2022, an employee was trimming tree limbs in the
backyard of a private residential home. The employee came into contact with an
energized powerline and was electrocuted.
At 9:30 a.m. on December 16, 2021, an employee was preparing chemical solutions
in spray bottles for the day's round of cleaning a hotel. The employee mixed
chlorine bleach with ammonia to fill a bottle and it generated an ammonium
chloride release. The employee was exposed to the resultant toxic vapors and
experienced difficulty breathing and severe coughing, requiring medical
treatment without hospitalization.
At 12:00 p.m. on February 2, 2022, an employee was operating a self-propelled
stock picker. The employee stepped off of the stock picker onto shelving that
was approximately 16 feet high to retrieve a toilet. The employee was not
wearing any fall protection while on the shelving and fell off of the shelving
to ground level, which was approximately a 16 foot fall. The employee had
serious head injuries that lead to a fatality several days after the incident.
At 1:00 p.m. on March 30, 2022, an employee was attempting to open swing-style
trailer doors of a tractor trailer loaded with truck tires, prior to moving the
trailer into position at a loading dock. When the employee opened the trailer
doors, multiple tires fell from the trailer and knocked the employee to the
ground. The employee was killed due to severe spinal injuries.
At 8:38 a.m. on March 24, 2022, Employee #1, a vector ecologist, experienced a
personal medical condition leading to her death and was transported to Pomona
Valley Hospital Medical Center by the paramedics.
At 11:10 a.m. on March 31, 2022, Employee #1 entered the excavation to retrieve
hand tools. A coworker was operating earth moving equipment to backfill the
excavation. When Employee #1 entered the excavation, the coworker backfilled
soils over the employee in the excavation. Employee #1 was buried,  suffered
multiple injuries, and died.
On March 16, 2022, an employee was utilizing an extension ladder to take down
Christmas decorations outside of the main entry of the facility, when he fell
from the ladder. The employee later died from his injuries on March 29, 2022.
At 12:45 p.m. on April 1, 2022, the local marina's pier division had a crew of
three employees working to install a pier, boat/jet ski lifts, and a swim raft
at a residential property on Lauderdale Lakes. They were using a Kann crane
barge powered by a 115 horsepower Mercury outboard motor and an Amco Verba crane
Model V806NF4S on the deck of the barge.  They were also using a separate flat
deck barge to work from, as needed.  Multiple sections of the pier had been
installed, along with a boat lift, and a couple of jet ski lifts. The final step
was to install a swim pier, which had been lifted onto the crane barge to
prepare it for installation.  Employee #1 and Employee #2 were on the crane
barge, when Employee #1 turned the key to start the outboard motor of the crane
metal enclosed electrical cabinet to take a reading on the fuses when he caused
an arc flash/blast. The employee was not wearing proper personal protective
equipment, using proper electrical tools and had not received proper training in
the high voltage electrical work. The employee was hospitalized to treat
electrical shock and burns to his chest, arms, hands and fingers.
At 3:15 p.m. on September 39, 2020, an employee was working as a machinist for a
tubular commercial airplane and aerospace parts manufacturer. The employee was
working on the W/C 8071 10-foot draw bench attempting to remove a stuck part
when the machine moved and caught his hand. The employee had contacted a
coworker (his supervisor) to report that there was a problem with the machine.
The coworker asked the employee to run a part through to see what the problem
was.  While drawing a tube through the machine, the stub mandrel broke. The
employee placed his hand between the die holder and gripper trying to remove the
puller.  The employee mistakenly pushed the forward button crushing his hand.
The employee was not a trained repair technician for this equipment. The
employee was hospitalized and required amputation of the crushed hand.
At 8:40 a.m. on July 15, 2021, an employee was clearing a clog in a dust
collector while operating a trim saw. The employee shut down and locked out the
machine but was not aware of the spin-down time for the hog blade (12" x 3", 20
lbs). Believing the blade had stopped spinning, the employee reached in to
remove trimmings and the back of his hand made contact with the still-spinning
blade. The employee sustained a severed extensor tendon and a partially severed
flexor tendon on the right index finger. The employee was hospitalized.
At 8:00 a.m. on July 7, 2021, an employee was participating in a 1.5-mile run as
part of a new hire physical ability test. Within the last 50 meters of the run,
the employee collapsed. The employee self-reported insufficient hydration and
nutrition prior to the test. Emergency responders treated the employee with
extensive fluid administration, and the employee was diagnosed with
rhabdomyolysis. The employee was hospitalized for treatment.
At 5:30 p.m. on August 21, 2021, an employee went to the work site to conduct
weed eating operations. After about ten minutes, the employee went to their
truck and passed out. The employee was discovered killed by a heart attack.
At 10:00 p.m. on July 12, 2021, an employee working as a millwright for a marine
cargo facility was welding a mild steel deflector onto a rail car dumper. The
employee unhooked his lanyard to reach a welding rod when he received an
electrical shock. The shock caused the employee to fall to the aluminum plank
and steel floor below. The employee was hospitalized to treat a fractured wrist
and pelvis.
An employee worked as a medical assistant at the pediatric outpatient clinic.
The employee last worked on July 23, 2021.  The employee reported COVID-19
symptoms in the early part of the workday on July 23, 2021.  The employee tested
positive for COVID-19 on July 23, 2021.  The employee was admitted to an
intensive care unit on July 31, 2021.  The employee died at the hospital on
August 17, 2021.
At 11:45 a.m. on April 26, 2021, an employee was working as a farm laborer for a
She was apparently asymptomatic at the time. The test results were positive for
COVID-19. She was placed on quarantine at home. On August 25, 2021, she was
hospitalized. On September 6, 2021, she died. Her daughter reported the death to
the employer on September 8, 2021. The employer believed that the employee had
contracted the disease at work.
At 9:30 a.m. on September 8, 2021, an employee was performing tree work when he
contacted an overhead electrical line and was killed. The employee was moving an
aerial lift when he contacted the 13 killivolt line and was electrocuted.
At 11:15 p.m. on August 27, 2021, an employee was working as a molding machine
operator for an iron foundry. The employee was breaking up pieces of metal slag
in tubs located underneath the "Charlie" or C casting machine in a pit filled
with water. After being broken up inside the tubs, a Harrington Model ERP050L
Hoist would lift the slag out of the pit and them move it to the other side of
the "Delta" or D Casting machine. At this point, the tub was to be switched to
another crane before being moved outside for cleaning. The employee was using
the hoist to lift one of the tubs out of the pit when he reached out to adjust
the tub. As he did this, he brought the hoist pendant control to his abdomen
with his off hand. The employee then depressed the East movement button on the
pendant and at that time he felt an electrical shock and immediately collapsed
onto the ground. The employee began to experience chest pain and numbness in his
arm due to the shock, but he did not lose consciousness. Coworkers responded and
provided first aid until the ambulance staffed by the local fire department
arrived at the scene. The ambulance transported the employee to the local
hospital, where he was kept overnight for evaluation.
At approximately 8:30 A.M. on March 12, 2021, a subcontractor, working for a
plumbing contractor, was installing 20 foot long PVC pipes at a mixed use
building. Pipes were delivered to the job site in bundles. These bundles were
hoisted/moved from ground level to the second story of the parking structure. An
all-terrain PIT was used to lift the bundled PVC pipes. The 2nd level was
protected along the edges by guardrails. This area was not a designated material
loading/hoisting area. The employee was standing on the guarded side of the
guardrails as the PVC pipe load was being hoisted when the load became unstable
and started to fall off the forks. The employee climbed over the guardrails
without using fall protection to secure the load and prevent it from falling.
The load continued to move which caused the employee to lose balance and fall
approximately 12 feet. The employee was hospitalized and treated for a left
broken heel bone, fracture of the 6th vertebrae, left rib fracture, and epidural
hematoma.
An employee was working in a skilled nursing facility when she was exposed to
residents and coworkers infected with COVID-19. The employee contracted COVID-19
and subsequently required hospitalization for treatment of her infection at 2:30
a.m. on June 1, 2020.
At 9:30 a.m. on April 6, 2021, Employee #1, a garbage collector, was loading
garbage into the rear of a rear-loading garbage truck as part of the client
route. A coworker, the driver of the garbage truck, checked his mirrors and
assumed Employee #1 was out of the way. The coworker then reversed the garbage
truck into the client driveway, striking and running over Employee #1. Employee
#1 sustained severe injuries, including eight fractured ribs, a collapsed lung,
a lacerated liver, a fractured ankle, a fractured knee, spinal fractures, and a
large gash on the right lower leg. Employee #1 was life-flighted to the hospital
for admission and emergency medical treatment.
At 8:30 a.m. on March 5, 2021, an employee of American Builders & Contractor
Supply Co., Inc. operated a Moffett truck-mounted forklift to unload materials
from a flatbed truck at a residential construction site in Napa, CA. The
forklift was positioned on an uneven, sloped road covered with loose gravel and
rocks. After unloading several pallets, the employee attempted to lift a 1,600
lb. pallet of Polyglass Polystick XFR rolls. As the employee retracted the mast
and backed out, the forklift became unstable and tipped over, causing the
employee's hand to be crushed against the rollover protection system (ROP). The
employee was transported to Queen of the Valley Hospital, then transferred for
surgery, where partial finger amputation occurred.
An employee performed regular duties as an admitting financial counselor. On
August 4, 2021, the employee was in close contact with a COVID-19 positive
coworker at a meeting. The employer performed contact tracing upon learning the
coworker was COVID-19 positive and discovered that the coworker had been in
close contact with the employee for more than 15 minutes when they sat at the
same table during a meeting. At the time of the meeting, the coworker did not
know she was COVID-19 positive. On August 14, 2021, the employee began exhibit
symptoms and was diagnosed with COVID-19 on August 16, 2021. At 3:36 p.m. on
August 22, 2021, the employee was hospitalized due to COVID-19 complications,
including but not limited to difficulty breathing. Information regarding
engineering, administrative and personal protective equipment controls for
COVID-19 are not included in the narrative.
At 10:00 a.m. on September 7, 2021, an employee was unloading cargo, when he was
struck in the face by a hook and chain.  The employee was killed.
At 11:45 p.m. on March 30, 2021, an employee burned his fingers and back with
melted plastic.  The employee was treated without hospitalization.
An employee was working as an air traffic controller at a federal air traffic
control facility. A coworker at the facility had contracted COVID-19. At
approximately 5:30 p.m. on or about July 30, 2021, while the employer was
conducting contact tracing, the employee reported to his supervisor and to the
regional flight surgeon that he had had contact with the COVID-19-positive
coworker on Thursday, July 22, 2021. At the time, the employee was asymptomatic.
He was directed to quarantine for fourteen days. On August 4, 2021, he was taken
to a hospital. He died there at 10:14 a.m. on September 2, 2021. His death was
thought to be associated with COVID-19. The county forensic service did not
generate a medical examiner's report.
An employee was working at his desk in a correctional facility when he felt pain
inserted his left hand into the equipment while it was running. The employee was
hospitalized to treat an amputation to his index fingertip.
An employee tested positive on August 8, 2021, and the employee was hospitalized
at 9:00 a.m. on August 17, 2021.  The employee was exposed to COVID-19 when
attending a meeting.
At 2:53 p.m. on August 17, 2021, an employee was driving a tractor-trailer when
he stopped at an intersection with his headlights and flashers on. The employee
was standing outside of the cab when he was struck and killed by an automobile
traveling in the opposite direction.
An employee was a nurse practitioner (NP) and was providing care services to
hospital patients, including those in the COVID-19 ward. The employee tested
positive for COVID-19 on August 18, 2021, and was hospitalized with
COVID-related pneumonia on the same day.
An employee was working as a laboratory scientist.  The employee last worked on
August 20, 2021, and received Covid-19 positive results on August 25, 2021, but
was not hospitalized. At 3:00 p.m. on August 26, 2021, emergency services
transported the employee to the hospital, and she died from complications from
COVID-19 on the same day.
At 12:15 a.m. on May 22, 2021, an employee was working as a laborer for a
company that provides support services to oil and gas operations. The employee
was working on a crew that was tasked with pressure washing only the exterior of
two tanks. The employee had finished power washing the exterior of one of the
tanks. The crew put down their equipment and broke for lunch. As the employee
was walking towards the truck dragging the water hose, he walked by the tank
battery. At that point, a fire occurred and ignited the tank causing an
explosion. The employee was hospitalized to treat 2nd and 3rd degree burns to
45% of his body including his back, head, upper legs, shoulders, upper arms and
neck.
At 3:30 p.m. on August 27, 2021, an employee was looking for the location of the
parking brake release handle in preparation to drive a bus route for the school.
The employee was found under the bus, pinned by the back left wheels. It is
suspected that the employee got out of the bus in order to see the release lever
for the parking brake and when it was located she pulled it not realizing that
the bus was in drive. The bus lurched forward knocking the employee to the
ground and the bus ran over her. When the back left wheel came in contact with
the employee, it stopped turning and dragged her several feet. The employee died
due to multiple blunt force trauma injuries and asphyxiation.
At 9:00 a.m. on May 28, 2021, Employee #1 was re-installing a rotary valve after
it had been cleaned. While the valve was suspended by a hydraulic lift, his hand
was sucked into the rotary valve, and his fingers made contact with the valve
fins. He sustained amputations to four fingertips on his right hand and was
hospitalized for treatment.
At 3:00 p.m. on June 14, 2021, an employee was operating a forklift moving
product totes from a process building to a storage shed when he woke up on the
ground. A coworker who spoke to the employee said the employee had left the
forklift to check a tote number after placing the forklift in neutral and
setting the parking brake. The employee told the coworker he may have tripped or
missed a step and fell to the ground hitting the left side of his body on the
concrete. The employee had sought medical care three separate times for his
injuries. On June 27, 2021, the employee died from cardiac arrest.
At 9:00 p.m. on May 28, 2021, Employee #1 was operating a Serac 2 milk container
stacker/palletizer, which involved supervising the process and placing cardboard
between rows of milk containers. During palletizing, some containers fell into
the stacker. While the equipment was still in operation, the employee climbed
onto the exit side conveyor and entered the elevator section of the machine to
retrieve the containers. As the palletizing cycle completed, the machine
descended from the upper portion, striking the employee with moving parts. He
sustained a wrist fracture and was hospitalized for treatment.
At 8:30 a.m. on August 20, 2021, an employee worked to clean the outdoor work
site raking debris. While working, the employee began to gasp for air, collapsed
and was killed by a probable heart attack possibly brought on by heat and over
exertion.
At 4:30 p.m. on August 26, 2021, an employee worked to install a flat rubber
roof system on a building. At the end of the workday, the employee descended to
the ground and later found on the ground unresponsive. The employee was killed
by hyperthermia from outdoor exposure to high heat, sun, and humidity.
At approximately 5:00 a.m. on August 22, 2021, an employee was working as a
truck driver and was driving his truck state to state. The employee informed his
employer he was not feeling well and contracted COVID-19.  The employee died
from complications from COVID-19.
At 12:27 p.m. on February 24, 2021, Employee #1 was working for a plumbing/HVAC
contractor. The worksite is a Warehouse Distribution Center.  Employee was
installing new duct work in the facility.  Employee #1 was working from a
scissor lift that was being lifted by a forklift.  The scissor lift fell from
the elevated forks causing Employee #1 to strike the ground fracturing his jaw.
Employee #1 was hospitalized.
At 2:10 a.m. on August 25, 2021, an employee working for a janitorial service
was working in the vicinity of the Frontmatic Q500 Tender Trim Incline Conveyor
Belt. The conveyor was located at the south end of the Tender Trim line. As the
employee was working, he became entangled in the rotating shaft/scraper blade.
The employee was hospitalized to treat a lacerated right arm with associated
muscle, tendon, nerve and bone damage.
At around 4:20 or 4:36 p.m. on October 21, 2020, an employee was working for a
construction firm. He was a construction laborer. He was working on the second
story of a wood framed building structure. He was walking on the trusses
installing the roof sheathing. He was nailing down a piece of plywood when it
shifted underneath him. The employee slipped and fell about 10 feet (3.0 m) to
the lower wooden level and then an additional 10 feet (3.0 m) to the ground. He
was taken by ambulance to a hospital and admitted for treatment of multiple
spine fractures. The employer did not report the incident on a timely basis.
At approximately 12:00 P.M. on March 3, 2021, two employees, working for an
elevator and escalator contractor, were performing a repack for the hydraulic
piston seal at a new construction three-story building. Employee 2  picked the
car doors and secured the doors open with a device on the door track to stop the
elevator car from moving. The hazardous energy control procedure was not
implemented and Employee 2 accessed the pit to spread absorbent sand over leaked
hydraulic fluid on the floor of the elevator pit. Employee 1 was positioned at
the landing, observed dust exiting the pit due to the placing of the absorbent
material, and removed the device holding the elevator doors open. Employee 1
then entered the hoist way onto a ladder without notifying Employee 2 in the
pit. The door closed and the elevator began lowering to level one and struck
Employee 1 as he was climbing down the ladder into the pit. Employee 1 fell from
the ladder.  Employee 1 was hospitalized and treated for head and leg injuries.
At 9:50 p.m. on August 25, 2021, an employee was attempting to access a roof
where a coworker was pressure washing the hood vent for a kitchen grill on a
restaurant.  The coworker heard a voice and saw the employee rising up from the
ladder over the edge of the roof however, it was dark and the coworker lost
sight of the employee. The coworker exited the roof and returned to the ground
where he found the employee injured. The employee had fallen approximately
20-feet when he attempted to get onto the roof from the ladder. The employee was
killed and suffered fatal blunt force trauma to the body.
At approximately 11:00 a.m. on August 26, 2021, an employee was working at the
yard as a wood-yard crew leader.  The employee was exposed to COVID-19 while
working in the facility and died from complications from the virus.
At 3:00 a.m. on May 20, 2021, an employee working for plastics film manufacturer
was winding plastic on a winding machine. The machine cycled and pulled the
employee's arm into the moving parts. The employee was hospitalized to treat a
broken forearm.
At 8:15 a.m. on August 26, 2021, an employee working as a press operator was
operating Federal #7 Mechanical Power Press. The employee followed standard
procedures. He put a part into the press, hit the two-hand control, went to
remove the part, and the press cycled on its own. The employee's right arm was
caught between the die cut plates as a result. The employee was hospitalized to
treat a crushed arm.
At 12:00 p.m. on August 18, 2021, an employee working for a warehouse facility
was operating a stand-up forklift in MBUSA Plant 1. The employee was backing up
the forklift while staging bumper racks for production. He got off the forklift
as the vehicle rolled to a stop at which time he caught his left ankle in
between a rack and the rear of the forklift. The employee was hospitalized to
treat a fractured ankle.
At 9:49 p.m. on August 11, 2021, Employee #1, a security guard, attempted to
extinguish a fire that ignited at the employer's facility. During the incident,
he sustained minor burns and smoke inhalation. The employee was hospitalized for
treatment.
At 8:00 a.m. on August 28, 2021, an employee worked to replace roofing panels.
While working, a panel collapsed, and the employee fell approximately

At 1:30 p.m. on June 21, 2021, Employee #1 was assisting with the removal of an
8-inch pipe inside a water storage tank when an electric arc welder ignited
methane gas. This caused an explosion, resulting in water rushing out and
pinning the employee against a cyclone fence. The employee sustained lacerations
and contusions and was hospitalized for treatment.
At 10:40 a.m. on October 8, 2021, an employee, conducting maintenance and repair
in the fabrication department, was using a pressure airline attached to a
molasses line (sugar mill), using compressed air to clean out the line.  The
line over-pressurized.  The employee was looking into the site glass when the

The employee was killed due to face, eye and chest injuries.
An employee was working at a general medical or surgical hospital. It was a
medical center for veterans. She was in an administrative support position. She
was a claims assistant in the community service department of the medical
center. She worked in the reception area with four coworkers in a 518 sq ft (48
sq m) area. Ventilation in the area was sometimes inadequate, in that there were
periods of time with no air circulation. The workers wore facemasks while
working. Four of the five workers in the area developed COVID-19. The employee,
who was partially vaccinated, was hospitalized with symptoms ten days after
testing positive. She died in the hospital about two weeks after she was
admitted on October 9, 2021. From the timeline of the outbreak, it was thought
that she contracted COVID-19 from one of her coworkers or from a walk-in client.
At 12:15 p.m. on June 2, 2021, Employee #1 was part of a crew tasked with
removing a eucalyptus tree at a residential property. After gradually cutting
down the tree with assistance from the foreman, the employee positioned himself
on his knees to flatten the stump using a Husqvarna 372 XP chainsaw. The stump
had co-dominant stems, and as he cut through the center, a portion of the stump
dropped onto the chain bar, causing the chainsaw to kick back between his legs.
The chainsaw struck the employee's inner thighs, resulting in lacerations. The
foreman, who was retrieving equipment from the other side of the house at the
time, did not witness the incident and had not instructed the employee to cut
the stump. The employee was not wearing protective chaps while operating the
chainsaw. The employee was hospitalized for treatment.
At 7:40 a.m. on April 12, 2021, an employee working as an equipment operator for
a logistics company was driving a forklift. The employee was unable to get the
forklift to stop causing her to have a collision. The employee was hospitalized
to treat a broken leg.
At 10:30 p.m. on October 7, 2021, an employee was troubleshooting and repairing
a metering pump at a produce wholesaler facility. The metering pump was used to
feed Oxysan 1510 Antimicrobial chemical solution which is a peracetic acid based
antimicrobial product.  While working on the pump, the employee was sprayed in
the face and left eye with Oxysan 1510. The employee experienced eye irritation
and blurred vision in the left eye and was hospitalized.
At 7:45 p.m. on September 29, 2021, an employee was troubleshooting an
electrical unit on a production line when the multimeter he was using made
contact with an electrical components. The employee was electrocuted and died.
At 2:36 p.m. on September 22, 2021, an employee was adding gas pipe to a new
HVAC system. The employee leaned forward in front of an open panel and contacted
a live electrical wire. The employee was killed due to electrocution.
At approximately 12:21 p.m. on September 10, 2021, an employee was standing on

At 11:15 a.m. on April 9, 2022, an employee was discarding stale bread products

An employee was working as a delivery driver for a pharmacy when he was

At 4:00 p.m. on September 8, 2021, an employee was sweeping the sidewalk. After

down.  He was found unresponsive.

At 3:30 p.m. on July 26, 2021, an employee at the California Department of State

At 03:00 p.m. on July 06, 2021, an employee was climbing a stack of pallets to
put a band around them. The employee lost his balance and fell, pulling the

injuries brought by the fall and falling pallets.
On April 16, 2021, an employee was working for a firm that provided sanitation
services for meat packers nationwide. In this incident, the employee was

other than the employer. The employer did comply with reporting requirements.

hit his back. By a second account, related by a coworker, the incident happened

work-related. A cause was not determined.

with a sodium hydroxide and hot water when a chemical reaction occurred. The

At 2:50 a.m. on October 26, 2021, an employee was cleaning a Thermwood CNC

At 2:30 a.m. on June 23, 2021, an employee was working as a sanitation worker

At 2:45 p.m. on May 13, 2021, an employee working as an order clerk for a

At 2:05 p.m. on October 14, 2021, an employee was standing on a foot platform

At 10:30 a.m. on October 25, 2021, an employee working on a large box truck was

hospital. The employee was hospitalized. The course owned two Reelmaster 3100-D
tee mower. Both had inoperable seat safety switches. A functioning switch would

he thought, to the poor condition of the seats, which allowed the switches to
activate erroneously. The switches had been inoperable for at least four years,
since 2017. The seats had severely degraded outer linings, exposing the seat's
internal foam to the elements. Water was able to penetrate the foam and seep
into the inner material of the seat. The water reached the seat safety switches
and caused erroneous activation., The seat safety switches were bypassed so that
the equipment could be operated. Starting in 2017, the site supervisor had been
submitting purchase order requests for the repair and replacement of the
equipment. All purchase order funding requests had either been denied or were
still pending. The mowers, operating at 3,500 hours, were well past their
expected lifespan of 2,500 hours.
At 2:15 p.m. on September 23, 2021, an employee was training a coworker on how

At approximately 10:15 a.m. on October 6, 2021, an employee cut starboard
material with a  Ryobi 10 inch Portable Table Saw.  The table saw was not

reached near the table saw's blade to pull away one of the cut pieces of
starboard material and her left index finger was cut.  The employee was

At 11:20 a.m. on March 20, 2022, an employee was cutting a tree limb. The pole
saw touched the overhead power line, and the employee was electrocuted. The
employee was killed.
At 5:30 p.m. on April 2, 2021, Employee #1 was struck by forklift and was

At 12:00 p.m. on March 21, 2022, Employee #1, a groundskeeper, was riding as a

and Employee #1 fell out of the moving vehicle. Employee #1 was transported to
the hospital with a head injury.  On March 25, 2022, Employee #1 died from a
brain bleed at Christ Medical Center in Oak Lawn, IL.
At 8:15 a.m. on January 31, 2022, Employees #1 and #2 were installing sheet
metal roofing and vents on a 25 -foot high roof. They needed to retrieve more

scissors lift that was positioned 40 feet from the work area.  Employee #1
picked up the sheet metal and placed it on his head to carry over to the work
action of the upper vice grip, which came down on the employee's finger. The
employee's finger was held for about two seconds. The employee suffered an
amputation to the tip of their right index finger. The employee was hospitalized
to treat these injuries.
At 4:22 p.m. on April 21, 2022, an employee was working for a contractor hired
to install siding at a home. While working from the roof of the residence, he
fell onto the driveway and was killed.  Fire Department Medics reported that the
employee was found unresponsive on the ground next to a ladder.
An employee was working as a wildland fire fighter when he tested positive for

An employee was working for an automotive parts supplier when he contracted

At 2:00 p.m. on August 19, 2021, an employee who worked in administration for an

An employee was working as an office assistant in a state prison when she was

At 11:00 a.m. on May 17, 2021, an employee working as a construction laborer for

rental property managed  by a property management company. The employee's
company was contracted by the tenant. The employee was cleaning the east side of
a 2nd story window approximately 10 to 15 feet high. The employee was using a
ladder to perform his work. The ladder slipped out from under and the employee
causing him to fall approximately 10 feet to the concrete below.  The employee
sustained a head injury and was unconscious. Emergency medical responders were
called to the scene and transported the employee to the hospital. The Division
was unable to interview the employee and gather any additional details as to
what occurred. The employee did not respond to inquiries, and the employer did
not provide any requested documents. The employee was hospitalized to treat head
injuries from the fall.
An employee was working as a patient care specialist at a freestanding
ambulatory surgical and emergency center. Her main job duties involved front
desk and administrative tasks. Typical job duties entailed greeting patient as
they came into the clinic, obtaining information from patients so that they
could be registered, gathering insurance filing and copayment information, and
facilitating the check-in and check-out process. All the firm's urgent care
clinics performed onsite COVID testing. This clinic was no exception; it tested
patients for COVID-19 and treated those who were positive. All the employees
were required to comply with OSHA guidelines about wearing masks and staying
protected. For some reason, the employee contracted COVID-19 and became ill. She
was admitted to the hospital for treatment on August 26, 2021. On Friday,
September 3, 2021, she died. The employer was informed of the fatality that same
day. A representative of the employer emailed a state CSHO at 1:04 p.m. on
September 6, 2021, to report the fatality. TOSHA determined this fatality to be
work related. The employee's next of kin (NOK) was contacted and interviewed.
The next of kin explained that he or she was unaware of any exposure to COVID-19
in the home or in the employee's daily activities, other than while the employee
was at work. The employer's regional director of operations and clinic
coordinator explained that the employee had contact with patients who came into
the facility to receive a COVID-19 test and may have been symptomatic for
COVID-19 when they arrived. The employer was aware of the employee's close
contact exposure to patients with COVID-19. In multiple instances, the employer
failed to prevent the employee from being exposed to COVID-19. Around the time
of this incident, another of the firm's employees, who also worked as a nurse,
tested positive for COVID-19.
At 3:30 p.m. on September 3, 2021, an employee and a coworker had a short
coordination meeting in the loading area of the facility by the driver's side of
the truck. After receiving transportation instructions from the employee, the
coworker got in his truck to back up to a flat-bed trailer loaded with cargo.
The employee walked around the front of  the truck on the passenger side. The
coworker began to back up to the trailer when he felt a "bump" and saw the
employee lying on the ground in front of the truck. The coworker had struck and
backed over the employee. The employee suffered a fatal head trauma.
An employee was working as a registered nurse for a general medical or surgical
hospital. He worked in the urgent aid department. He triaged and cared for
patients in the urgent aid department. On August 22, 2021, he worked a full
shift, triaging and caring for patients with indications and symptoms of
COVID-19 in the urgent aid department. By the end of his work shift, he had
developed fever and body aches. On that day, he tested for COVID-19. He tested

At 3:00 p.m. on April 4, 2020, an employee who worked as a Registered Nurse for

hospital and confirmed to have COVID-19. From April 11, 2020 to April 16, 2020,
the employee was hospitalized before being sent home.  On May 12, 2020, the
employer learned that employee had been hospitalized due to COVID-19. The
employer was unaware if the employee notified anyone else at the company prior
to that date. The date, time and other details leading up to exposure are not
indicated in the narrative. The employer did not have Adequate Aerosol
Transmissible Diseases policies and procedures in place.
At 9:30 a.m. on August 27, 2021, an employee working for a sawmill was
attempting to see if there was a log on the conveyor system. The employee was
climbing down from the side of the conveyor when his left foot slipped and got
caught in the driving wheel of the conveyor. The employee was hospitalized to
treat an amputation below the knee.
At 8:34 a.m. on March 30, 2021, an employee was weeding a large area on a steep
hill. The employee was using a gas-powered trimmer/weeder on a steep hill when
he slipped, fell and rolled down the hill, bumping his head.  The employee lost
consciousness and suffered a concussion.  The employee was hospitalized.
At 11:15 a.m. on May 14, 2021, an employee working as a merchandise handler for
a hardware distribution center warehouse had placed a small box next to the
steering wheel of a Raymond lift truck #114 (powered industrial vehicle/PIV).
The employee then drove toward the aerosols room in the V section area to
deliver a pallet. When the employee placed the pallet down, he noticed the small
box was missing and had fallen off the pallet. The employee backtracked and
found the box so he put it back next to the steering wheel and drove back
towards the V section from T section. When turning into the aerosol room
(distance from T section to V section is about 18 feet), the box slid and caught
in the steering wheel locking it. The PIV could not be controlled with a locked
steering wheel and the employee drove it into the metal rack. The employee's
left foot fell out of the operating compartment and was pinned between the PIV
and the rack. The employee crushed his big toe and fractured the pinky toe
requiring medical treatment without hospitalization. Later, the employee's bit
toe developed gangrene and required partial amputation.
At 11:30 a.m. on March 20, 2021, an employee had created a homemade warming
device (a fire bucket) that consisted of a metal bucket filled with lumber that
was ignited with denatured alcohol. The employee unknowingly spilled some of the
denatured alcohol on his pant legs. The vapors from the alcohol were ignited by
the open flames from the fire bucket, which set the employee's pants on fire.
The employee was hospitalized to treat second and third degree burns to both
legs, from the calf to the knee areas.
Employees were working for an overhead door manufacturer when a COVID-19
outbreak occurred in the facility. Three employees contracted COVID-19 but none
required hospitalization for treatment of their infections.
On August 6, 2021, an employee who had worked as a Nurses Aide in a Health
Center Intensive Care Unit (ICU) and Emergency Room died from COVID-19. The
employee had been providing care to COVID-19 positive patients prior to
contracting COVID-19. The employer did not have an effective COVID-19 Prevention
Program in place.
At 2:40 p.m. on April 22, 2021, an employee was preparing to unload two Magliner
hand trucks from the truck he drove that day. While positioning one hand truck
with a long handle on the lift gate, the employee entered the truck to grab the
secondhand truck with the short handle. A 20-mph gust of wind suddenly pushed
both the employee and the hand truck to the ground, causing a fall from a height
neck. Emergency services transported the employee for medical treatment. The
employee was hospitalized.
At 4:05 p.m. on July 20, 2021, Employee #1 was operating a spot welder when the
machine was activated with his left-hand index finger positioned between the
electrodes. Employee #1 sustained an amputation of the left-hand index finger
and was hospitalized for treatment.
At 11:00 a.m. on July 20, 2021, Employee #1 was piercing metal parts on a Bliss
60-ton partial revolution press when he was resetting the press at the control
panel. After removing his right-hand restraint and switching the press to inch
mode, he did not reapply the restraint and placed his right hand into the point
of operation while setting a part in place. His foot accidentally actuated the
pedal, cycling the press. Employee #1 sustained a complete amputation of his
right middle finger, a partial amputation of his right index finger to the
second knuckle, and his right ring finger was crushed and pierced, requiring
surgery. Factors that may have contributed include lack of engineering controls,
supervision, and training. He was hospitalized for treatment.

At 3:00 p.m. on August 25, 2021, an employee worked to paint a ceiling while

force trauma injuries to the head, and was killed.
At 8:00 a.m. on February 18, 2021, Employee #1 was servicing an elevator. While

free and fell, striking the employee in the head. The employee sustained a
laceration to the head and swelling from the impact. Emergency services were

At 3:00 p.m. on July 21, 2021, an employee working for a wooden pallet
manufacturer was operating a miter saw. The employer stated that the employee

contacted the sawblade with his right hand as a result. The employee was

At 3:00 p.m. on July 30, 2021, Employee #1 was operating a forklift without a

At approximately 12:05 p.m. on August 10, 2021, Employee #1, a 15-year veteran

Employee #1 on the shoulders, back, and head. He was initially taken to a clinic

At 8:30 a.m. on August 23, 2021, an employee was hooking up a KALMAR Ottawa

At 8:30 a.m. on August 17, 2021, an employee, a farm laborer, was working in a

At 11:50 a.m. on March 1, 2021, Employee #1, an employee of Younger Mfg. Co.,
DBA Younger Optics, was working on a JLG scissor lift in the IOTP Department to
install a differential air pressure switch on a metal beam near the ceiling.
While drilling into the beam with a DeWalt cordless drill, an arc flash occurred
because the beam was a bus bar carrying 420V 3-phase electricity. The arc flash
ignited Employee #1's clothing and PPE. Employee #1 attempted to extinguish the
fire by removing his clothing while on the lift. Coworkers tried to assist but
were unable to use a fire extinguisher or lower the lift using external controls
due to an activated emergency stop. Employee #1 ultimately lowered the lift and
was assisted to the ground. He sustained second- and third-degree burns on 25%
of his body and was hospitalized for 44 days at Torrance Memorial Medical
Center.  The incident caused a power outage across the facility and resulted in
serious injuries due to contact with the bus bar and lack of effective safety
measures.
At 1:50 a.m. on April 11, 2021, an employee working as a millwright for a

foot. The employee was hospitalized to treat a crushed foot.
At 9:00 a.m. on November 18, 2020, Employee #1 was decommissioning an electrical

broken fingertip.
Two employees were working for a medical group, one employee was a registered

At 5:25 a.m. on September 1, 2021, an employee working for a grocery store was

At 4:00 p.m. on September 8, 2021, an employee worked to hoist a broken

At 9:00 p.m. on September 7, 2021, she died.
At 9:15 a.m. on September 2, 2021, Employee #1 was standing on the rear step

Employee #1 fell from the driver's side rear step of the trash truck while it

At 9:00 a.m. on August 29, 2021, an employee working as a machine maintenance

At 12:00 p.m. on April 9, 2021, an employee was pushing casting and molding
equipment from one location to another when one of the wheels on the casting
cart rolled over his right smallest toe. The employee did not immediately report
the incident to the employer. The employee's toe became infected and eventually

At 10:00 a.m. on October 1, 2021, an employee working in production for a

circular cutter. The employee cut her hand when the sawblade sliced through her
metal mesh glove. The employee amputated her left index fingertip and required

On October 1, 2021, a security guard was working behind the front desk at a
client location when he was shot and killed by a tenant wielding a zip gun.
At 9:00 a.m. on October 4, 2021, an employee acted as a spotter for two dump

struck and ran over the employee, who received blunt force crushing injuries,

At 7:15 a.m. on October 19, 2021, an employee was beginning to unload frost

At 5:15 p.m. on May 6, 2021, Employee #1 was retrieving or processing saw

On or about October 7, 2021, The employee was working as a caregiver at an

An employee was working as a highway maintenance worker for a state division of
public transportation when he contracted COVID-19. The employee had worn all PPE

or out in the field performing maintenance road work. On January 5, 2021, the

At 8:00 p.m. on October 16, 2021, an employee was installing a lock pin on the
bottom of a shipping container being lowered by a crane.  As the crane was
lifting the container, the front pins were stuck so that only the back of the

hand, resulting in a partial amputation. The employee was hospitalized.
At 11:00 p.m. on October 16, 2021, an employee was clearing jammed up equipment
while working at a veneer and plywood manufacturing facility.  While clearing

a pulley. The employee amputated his fingertip and was hospitalized.
At 5:45 p.m. on May 31, 2025, a coworker, a material equipment operator, was

reverse toward the staging area. While turning a corner around two rows of
82-inch-high double-stacked gaylords, the coworker failed to slow down and did
not sound the horn. As a result, the forklift ran over the feet of Employee #1.
Employee #1 sustained two broken toes on the right foot and four toe amputations
on the left foot. Employee #1 was hospitalized for treatment.
At 7:30 a.m. on July 16, 2021, an employee was replacing a sugar retention tote

rotary valve. The incident resulted in an amputation injury to the tip of his
right middle finger.  The employee was hospitalized.
At 7:45 p.m. on October 16, 2021, an employee was removing rocks from a conveyor
belt system at a fruit and vegetable canning facility. When the employee reached
into the conveyor, his arm became caught in the roller of the conveyor system.
The employee sustained a broken arm and was hospitalized.
At 11:20 a.m. on October 11, 2021, an employee was raising the rear frame of a
2011 Phaeton motorhome using a 20-ton hydraulic bottle jack in order to remove a
broken leveling jack cylinder behind the passenger side rear tire.  Due to the
motorhome's airbag suspension system, the wheels did not lift off of the ground.
With his upper body underneath the motorhome, the employee used his right arm to
pump up the bottle jack in order to try to work out the cylinder.  While pumping
up the jack, the employee heard a "ping" and the jack slipped off the brace, and
the motorhome's frame dropped onto the employee. The employee was caught between
the outside baggage compartment door and the concrete floor, resulting in a
collapsed lung, fractured clavicle, and seven fractured ribs.  The employee was
hospitalized for treatment.
At 10:45 a.m. on October 15, 2021, an employee was changing out hosing and
brackets for steam piping on a dip tank at a furniture manufacturing facility.
The employee who was a maintenance worker had been asked by a plating technician
to look at a leaking steam hose. While conducting this maintenance activity, the
overhead hoist was not deactivated or locked out.  The hoist is used to grab
racks of material that will complete a circuit of the dip tanks to clean and
plate the material.  Typically, the employee would have conducted the steam
hosing change from below the open edge of the dip tanks and below a metal drip
pan.  However, the employee climbed between two dip tanks and attempted to pry
the steam hoses out of the dip tank using a 2 in by 4 in wooden board of
unspecified length. While the employee was prying the hose, he was at mid-chest
level with a tank metal drip pan when the hoist was returning to its home
position across the dip tank.  The hoist struck the employee in the back between
the shoulders and pinned him between the hoist and the tank's drip pan. The
employee was hospitalized to treat multiple crushing injuries to the back, neck,
chest and head, leading to loss of brain function.
At 4:40 p.m. on September 19, 2021, an employee working as a cook for a grocery
store chain was performing her end of the shift tasks in the deli department.
Her tasks included draining oil from the fryer and washing dishes. The employee
was draining oil from the deep fryer. This required that the lower doors of the
fryer remain open so the level of oil could be watched so as to not overflow.
While the oil was draining, the employee was doing dishes. During this time, a
customer came to the deli counter.  As the employee turned to assist the
customer, she tripped over the open fryer doors landing on the tile floor on her
left shoulder. The employee was transported via ambulance to the local hospital,
where she was treated for a fractured left shoulder and released the same day.
At 9:40 a.m. on May 6, 2021, Employee #1, a testing foreman at a shipyard, was
assisting a coworker with rigging weight blocks to test a monorail system. The
monorail was approximately 3 to 4 feet above the ground, creating limited space
to rig the weights. Two weight blocks of different sizes were used to reach 125%
of the monorail's half-ton rated capacity due to the unavailability of a single
correct weight. Employee #1 was attempting to position the smaller weight to
shackle the two weights together. After unsuccessfully using a come-along to
move the smaller weight due to space constraints, Employee #1 and the coworker
tried to move a 500-pound weight by hand. As the 500-pound weight cleared the
top of the 800-pound weight, it shifted and crushed Employee #1's finger,
resulting in amputation. The employer reported the injury to the San Diego
District Office the same day. Employee #1 was hospitalized overnight and
released the following day. Lack of proper rigger training and supervision were
identified as contributing factors.
At 9:10 a.m. on October 13, 2021, an employee was operating a Leifeld machine.
The employee's thumb on his left hand was smashed between a block and a metal
part. His left thumb was amputated, resulting in hospitalization.
At 10:00 a.m. on September 1, 2021, an employee working for a telecommunications
carrier was climbing into an attic from a ladder, The employee stepped on
plywood that was not secured to the framing and fell through the ceiling drywall

unguarded table saw when his hand was caught by the blade.  The employee

poultry processing plant.  The employee was retrieving cut chicken strips from
the conveyor system's plastic chain belting by hand.  Her finger wedged between

hospitalization.

when he reached inside the Flory 1400 Conveyor Cart with his arm. The employee's

At 12:30 p.m. on April 15, 2021, an employee was working for a state
governmental agency that managed facilities for the state's government. The
employee was on a construction project at a one of the facilities that the
agency managed. He was installing plumbing and lighting fixtures at one of the

folded stepladder, the scaffold overturned. The employee fell to the ground

At 4:00 p.m. on April 1, 2021, Employee #1, while delivering tires, was closing
the rear roll-up door of a truck by pulling the strap. As he went to place his
foot on the step, which was missing, he slipped. The truck's roll-up door came

treated without hospitalization.
At 5:00 a.m. on May 6, 2021, Employee #1, a sanitation technician at a food
manufacturing plant, was cleaning and sanitizing the Line 2 Sheeter Head Machine

removed for cleaning. Employee #1 initially sprayed water on the rollers to
remove dough but, when that was ineffective, used a fibrous hand sponge. The
rollers pulled in the sponge and caught Employee #1's right hand. The employee
was able to turn off the rollers himself. The machine had not been locked out or
tagged out during cleaning, nor were extension tools or other protective methods
used to prevent injury. Employee #1 sustained crushed, fractured, degloved, and
amputated tips on the right thumb, index, middle, and ring fingers. He was
hospitalized overnight for treatment. The incident was reported to DOSH San
Diego District Office.
At 7:42 p.m. on September 15, 2021, an employee working as a laborer for a farm
laborer contractor was working on a harvester during night harvesting of grapes
in a vineyard. The employee started to feel ill and received medical treatment
without hospitalization for low blood pressure (personal illness).
At 2:00 p.m. on October 8, 2021, an employee was performing valve cleaning and
inspection operations at a ship building and repair facility. The employee was
working at the site through an employment placement organization.  The employee
and his coworkers were using a chain hoist attached to an A-frame gantry crane
to access the valve for cleaning and inspection.  The A-frame gantry crane was
on an improved ground surface and began sliding when the employee and his
coworkers were turning the valve. The crane movement caused the weight of the
valve to also slide and swing with the hoist sideways from the crane. The
momentum and weight of the swinging valve caused the entire gantry crane to fall
forward and land on the employee causing him to fall backwards onto metallic
disks. The employee sustained contusions to his head, back and arms and
fractures in his leg due to the direct impact to his body from being struck by
the gantry crane and heavy valve and from landing on the metallic disks on the
ground surface. The employee was hospitalized for treatment.

ventilator. During the removal, Employee #1 fell through the 30 inch hole
created by the removal of the roof ventilator. Employee #1 was not using any
fall protection and fell 32 feet to the concrete floor below. The employee was
killed.
At 1:15 p.m. on April 20, 2021, an employee was working as a yard helper for a
metal fabricator. The employee is a full-time employee of the employer. The
employee and Coworker #1 were working in the yard loading 24-gauge 4-foot by
8-foot steel sheets onto a customer's truck. Moving the metal sheets required
removing them from shelving that was approximately 6 feet off the ground. The
employee and Coworker #1 were both wearing gloves with a cuff slightly above
their wrists while moving the sheets one at a time. As they pulled the fourth
sheet off the shelf, the edge struck the employee on his unprotected right
forearm. Upon noticing the cut, Coworker #1 assisted the employee with
controlling the bleeding and notified Coworker #2, their supervisor. Coworker #2
drove the employee to the company's clinic. The clinic transferred the employee
to the medical center, where he was hospitalized and underwent surgery for his
lacerated arm.
An employee was working for a firm that manufactured fluid milk. The firm
manufactured, marketed, distributed, and sold, among many products, branded
coffee creamers and premium dairy products. He was exposed to COVID-19. He was
hospitalized, and he died on October 7, 2021.
At 11:15 a.m. on October 6, 2021, an employee conducted steel erection
operations to install stairs in new construction site. The employee fell
approximately fifty feet, received skull fracture, and was killed
At 9:30 a.m. on October 9, 2021, Employee #1 was installing electrical circuits

killed.
An employee had been working as a Security Agent for a University Hospital. As
part the employee's duties he had potential direct contact with COVID-19
positive patients while responding to disturbance calls, screening patients and

contracted it at the workplace, but the employer did not have Adequate Aerosol
Transmissible Diseases policies and procedures in place.
At 11:14 p.m. on May 20, 2021, an employee working for a children's hospital was
performing a one-one-one with a patient. The patient became agitated and struck
the employee with their fist after their behavior escalated. The employee was
hospitalized to treat head trauma including a concussion, bruising and
contusions.

to cut thin cardboard material. The hinged guard on the shear had been
unknowingly propped up. While adjusting the cardboard material on the shear

actuated the foot treadle. The shear blade descended and amputated the
employee's right hand. The employee was hospitalized for treatment.
On November 16, 2020, an employee who had been working for a manufacturer of
specialty industrial-grade striking, digging and cutting tools tested positive

fractures of three spinous transverse process and a concussion.
At approximately 9:57 a.m. on June 30, 2021, Employee #1 was working from the

60-foot oak tree. While attempting to break free a 10-foot long, 16-inch
diameter trunk section, the trunk fell backward and struck the boom/bucket.
Employee #1, who was not wearing fall protection, was ejected approximately 20
feet to the ground. The tree trunk then landed on him. Employee #1 sustained
head injuries, including a traumatic brain injury, and was hospitalized.
At 1:30 p.m. on July 3, 2021, an employee working as a retail clerk for a

The employee began to feel ill and was hospitalized to treat a heat-related

An employee was monitoring ECG monitors for patients with coworkers. The

At 12:08 p.m. on February 17, 2021, Employee #1 and Employee #2, temporary

The employee tested positive for COVID-19 on September 19th, 2021, and was

An employee, a customs and border protection officer, last worked on August 26,

At 12:00 a.m. on October 6, 2021, an employee worked as a tile setter and took a

While the employee was using a scrubbing pad to clean near an unguarded conveyor
telecommunications line installer and repair technician. He had tested positive

An employee was working as a pipefitter at a general medical or surgical
