At 10:30 a.m. on August 11, 2021, Employee #1 was manually loading a part into a
hydraulic press brake to bend it. While reaching in to better seat the part, he
inadvertently stepped on the pedal with his hand in the point of operation. The
machine partially cycled, and his left middle finger was caught and crushed
between the metal part and the die, resulting in a fingertip amputation. The
employee was hospitalized for treatment.
At 12:00 p.m. on August 19, 2021, an employee working as a quality assurance
inspector for an iron foundry was exiting through a set of rollup doors to a
storage area. As she exited the building through a railing to the storage area,
a forklift that was backing up struck the employee. The employee was
hospitalized to treat cuts to her legs from contact with the ground and the
forklift.
At 11:00 a.m. on August 13, 2021, an employee, on his first day of work, was
operating a press brake to bend inner support parts. While using an electronic
foot pedal to control the press brake, the employee positioned his hand below
the light curtain to adjust a part. Activating the foot pedal caused the press
to lower, trapping his four fingers in the press ram. The employee, despite
wearing cut-proof gloves, sustained severe injuries, including four broken
fingers, three of which required pins. Approximately one week later, the tip of
the employee's left middle finger was surgically removed down to the first
knuckle. Contributing factors may have included improperly adjusted light
curtains, inoperable two-hand controls, working position, and lack of
experience. The employee was hospitalized for treatment.
At 11:00 a.m. on July 29, 2021, an employee working for a new car dealership was
getting into a vehicle carrying a scan tool. The employee inadvertently hit the
drive button causing the vehicle to lurch forward. The employee was pinned by
the door of the vehicle. He fractured his pelvis and was hospitalized.
At 9:45 a.m. on July 16, 2021, Employee #1, a coworker, and a Foreman were
removing a burned block from a preheater lid to replace refractory insulation.
The preheater lid weighed approximately 2,500 pounds and measured roughly 12 by
14 feet. The Foreman  attached the burner block to an overhead double-girder
bridge crane via a nylon sling. While the foreman was pulling the burner block
with the crane, Employee #1 walked around the cover using a pry bar to loosen
the block. Unaware that the lid had lifted off the floor, Employee #1's foot was
positioned under the edge when the cover fell, fracturing the first, second, and
third metatarsals of his left foot. Employee #1 was hospitalized.
An employee had been working as a Travelling Nurse. Prior to being hospitalized,
the employee had been caring for a psychiatric patient who was not compliant
with mask use. The patient's spouse was allowed to be present during his
treatment to keep him calm. The spouse had unknowingly contracted COVID-19 prior
to exposing the employee. The patient also became positive for COVID-19 and was
asymptomatic while being cared for by the employee. The employee was using a
face covering (level 1 face mask) to care for the patient. The employee
developed COVID-19 symptoms and tested positive for COVID-19. At 1:00 p.m. on
down. The employee was found, conscious, on the ground near the passenger side
of his tractor trailer. He was hospitalized with broken ribs and a fractured
skull. He appeared to be making a recovery, when he passed away at the hospital
on September 24th. An autopsy was not performed. From information provided by
the hospital, the coroner determined the cause of death was acute hypoxic
respiratory failure due to blunt force injury, with chronic COPD as a
contributing factor. The manner of death was an on-the-job injury.
At 3:15 p.m. on July 14, 2021, Employee #1 was testing transformers when he
received an electrical shock from VVS transformer leads. Emergency services
transported Employee #1 to the hospital, where he was admitted and treated for
electrical shock.
At 8:30 a.m. on May 7, 2021, Employee #1 was guiding ribbon through a blocking
machine when her hand, wearing a glove, became caught in the spinning guide. The
hand was pulled between two wheels of the machine, resulting in lacerations.
The employee was hospitalized for treatment.
An employee was working at a naval shipyard. He worked as a plumber, pipefitter,
and steamfitter apprentice. He arrived at work one day exhibiting symptoms
related to an infection by COVID-19. He was tested and placed in quarantine. The
test came back positive, and his quarantine continued.  He was eventually
hospitalized. At 7:15 a.m. on September 22, 2021, he died, due to complications
of COVID-19. The employee had been performing standard work practices prior to
his COVID-19 test.
At 2:00 p.m. on July 23, 2021, Employee #1 was welding a bung onto a damaged
hydraulic tank when a flash occurred. The employee sustained burns to the neck
and arms and was hospitalized.
At 10:00 a.m. on September 21, 2021, an employee was in a "Guard Truck"
providing a "Safety Work Zone" for a grass-cutting crew. The employee was found
unresponsive in the vehicle by their supervisor, who contacted 911 and tried to
provide aid. The employee was taken to a medical center and was pronounced dead.
The cause of death is unknown and was possibly a heart attack.
An employee was working at a patient's house, who later tested positive for
COVID-19. The employee tested positive for COVID-19 on April 11, 2021 and was
hospitalized on April 17, 2021. The employee subsequently recovered from the
disease.
At 10:00 a.m. on June 23, 2021, an employee working as a machine operator for an
appliance manufacturer was working in his department. The employee was walking
with a part in his hand intending to bring the part to a different location. He
was walking with his head down and looking at the part and not looking at the
direct path in front of him. A coworker operating a forklift was driving in
reverse in the same area where the employee was walking. The employee did not
see the forklift and the coworker did not see him walking off to the side. The
forklift struck the employee of his left side. The employee was hospitalized to
treat a broken left leg.
At 1:00 p.m. on October 7, 2021, an employee worked to replace slate shingles on
a conical section of roof. While working, the employee fell approximately forty
feet, received head and spinal injuries, and was killed.
At 8:00 a.m. on July 20, 2021, an employee working as a construction laborer for
a provider of decorative and barrier coating for fabricated metal products was
working alone in the facility. The employee was standing was on a six foot high
rolling platform ladder hanging 10-foot metal hooks on a chain. The employee was
hanging a hook when one of the ends of the hook got caught in the hand rail of
the rolling platform ladder. This caused the ladder to tip over causing the
employee to fall to the concrete floor below. The employee was hospitalized to
treat contusions to the side of his body.
At 9:30 a.m. on July 1, 2021, Employee #1, a temporary agency worker serving as
lead packer at a produce handling facility, was working at sorting table #1
attached to a Giro machine in Room #5. On the first day of the season, while
removing a moldy mandarin, the employee's right pinky finger was caught and
amputated in the space between the roller and sheet metal at the end of the
sorting table. A nearby coworker witnessed the incident, and the operations
supervisor was present onsite in his office.  The employee was hospitalized for
treatment.  Cal/OSHA investigated the incident starting July 20, 2021, and
identified multiple causal factors, including unguarded rollers. Serious
citations were issued.
At 12:20 p.m. on October 1, 2021, an employee worked as part of a drilling rig
crew. The employee worked on the drilling rig floor to place the breakout tongs
on a section of pipe. The pin securing the safety line to the tongs was not
fully seated and when the coworker engaged the rotary table to unthread the
section, the pin flew out, the breakout tongs rotated, and struck the employee
on the chest. The employee received a laceration to the upper chest and was
killed.
At approximately 10:00 a.m. on October 2, 2021, an employee was cleaning out a
rendering area. The employee did not lock out the auger and tried to clean the
area by the auger.  The auger caught the bar and spun it to where the employee's
finger was pinned against the guard.  The employee's finger was amputated.  The
employee was hospitalized to treat these injuries.
An employee had been working as a High School Band Teacher for a public school
system. The employee was potentially exposed to a student who had been
experiencing what they thought were allergy symptoms. The student developed
symptoms consistent with COVID-19 infection and 6 days later and tested
positive.  The employee was hospitalized for 10 days before being transferred to
a regional health center for an additional 15 days where he died from COVID-19
on September 9, 2021. Information regarding engineering, administrative and
personal protective equipment controls for COVID-19 are not included in the
narrative.
At 12:00 a.m. on September 16, 2021, an employee worked on a floor truss. At
some point, the employee fell approximately eight feet and was killed due to
head injuries.
At 5:55 a.m. on May 17, 2021, an employee working for a transportation company
was washing a tanker trailer containing Ethyleneamine. The employee was sprayed
with the chemical while washing the tanker. The employee was hospitalized to
treat chemical burns.
An employee was working for an automobile parts manufacturer when he contracted
COVID-19 and subsequently died due to COVID-19-related cardiovascular and
respiratory system failure on September 27, 2021.
At approximately 2:15 p.m. on July 11, 2018, an employee was feeding the
friction mill machine with raw rubber strips.  The employee became entangled
with the rubber strips which pulled his right leg between two (2) rolls of the
machine, crushing his foot and deskinning the leg up to the knee.  The employee
was hospitalized for these injuries.
At 5:45 a.m. on September 22, 2020, Employee #1 was cutting a piece of sheet
metal using a mechanical shear. While the employee's hands were in the danger

index). Emergency services transported the employee to the hospital, where he
was admitted for treatment.
At 12:50 p.m. on December 1, 2020, an employee working as a machine operator for
a window and door manufacturer was feeding a board into a bead chopper saw. He

Employee #1 was found deceased in his camp trailer that was parked near the

September 2, and he was last seen alive by other coworkers on September 3.
Employee #1 died of natural causes.
At 2:14 a.m. on September 23, 2021, an employee was working as a truck driver
for a specialized, long-distance, freight trucking firm. He was driving a

At 1:52 p.m. on September 3, 2021, an employee worked on a roof. At some point,
the employee fell approximately twenty-eight feet and was killed.
At approximately 5:30 p.m. on August 17, 2018, an employee was traveling
southbound in a motor vehicle.  The employee appeared to have a seizure and

bee stings. The employee was hospitalized for these injuries.

At 12:20 p.m. on July 23, 2021, an employee was operating a Kawakami automatic

At 1:00 p.m. on May 4, 2021, an employee working as a laborer for an
entertainment company was working inside a commercial building that had
previously been used as a cabinet shop. The employer is a party equipment rental
company that had leased the building to use as a storage facility. The employee
and two coworkers were tasked with cleaning out excessive amounts of sawdust,
equipment and other materials that had been left behind from the previous
tenant. Although the employee had helped clean up the employer's main facility
in the past, this job was outside of his regular duties and he had never worked
with this amount of dust in the past. The crew was using leaf blowers, shop
vacs, boards and brooms to clean the dust. They also used the pre-existing
vacuum system that was engineered into the building.  A crew had started the
cleaning process the day prior. The employee was working on top of a bathroom
mezzanine cleaning the dust. A different coworker who identified as an
independent contractor was using the bathroom at the time. There was an electric
water heater on the mezzanine and according to those in the crew who was
interviewed, the independent contractor may have been using the sink in the
bathroom at the same time the dust ignited. There were other potential ignition
sources in the area as well such as multiple 120-volt live junction boxes and
lighting fixtures and wiring to the bathroom. There was also a low voltage alarm
system on the exterior bathroom wall underneath the water heater. The sawdust
had accumulated to the point that a combustible dust explosion occurred.
Coworkers witnessed the explosion and noted that the employee was seriously
injured when the airborne sawdust ignited. The employee was hospitalized for
multiple days to treat burns on 30 to 39 percent of his body and an acute kidney
injury.
On September 25, 2021, an employee was working for a soft drink bottling firm.
He was a merchandising employee, driving to a store. He was operating a company
car and traveling on a state highway.  A single person in another vehicle
traveling eastbound on the highway swerved off the road and overcorrected.  Upon
driving back onto the roadway, the other vehicle collided head on with the
vehicle that the employee was driving.  The employee died from the injuries he
received in the collision.
An employee was working in housekeeping in a skilled nursing facility and was

protocol. The following evening, the employee learned that he tested positive

At 11:35 p.m. on July 28, 2021, an employee working as a stock handler for a
wood cabinet and countertop manufacturer was servicing a Lantech material
wrapping machine. The employee was attempting to reposition the transfer chain

employee received medical treatment without hospitalization for an amputated
finger.
An employee worked as a Trade Delivery Driver for an automotive dealership. On
August 12, 2021, the employee and a coworker (Trade Delivery Driver) rode
together for approximately 3 hours. The coworker was notified on August 13,
2021, that the employee was positive for COVID-19 and he had been potentially
exposed. The employee began to experience COVID-19 related symptoms on August
14, 2021, and tested positive on August 21, 2021. On August 24, 2021, the
employee was hospitalized and died. There was no known contact between the
employee and coworkers at the store. Trade Delivery Drivers work part-time and
on call as needed. The potentially exposed coworker's COVID-19 status in not
indicated in the narrative. Information regarding engineering, administrative
and personal protective equipment controls for COVID-19 are also not included in
the narrative.
An employee was caring for the pediatric patient at a patient's home who
contracted COVID-19.  The employee died from complications from COVID-19 at

An employee was working on the filler line.  The employee tested positive for

At 1:00 p.m. on March 9, 2021, an employee was polishing a part with an
industrial metal polishing machine.  The employee's hand was caught between the
buffing wheel and the part being polished. The employee was hospitalized to
treat an amputated hand.

At 11:30 p.m. on March 30, 2021, an employee was moving a wheeled collapsible

An employee worked as a CNA.  The employee contracted COVID-19 and was not

Cart to a diesel island area, stopped the cart and exited preparing to cleanout

After the fire was out, steam lances were continuously directed on the flange

approximately five feet. The employee was taken to the hospital and admitted to
treat a compound fracture to the right tibia (lower leg).
At 3:00 p.m. on December 16, 2021, an employee was operating a Dension
Multipress 2-ton hydraulic bushing press equipped with two hand controls. While
operating the press, the employee's left hand index finger came into contact
with the press ram causing a partial amputation. The employee was transported by
ambulance to a local hospital, where he was hospitalized for treatment.
An employee was working in a hospital when she was exposed to patients and
coworkers infected with COVID-19. The employee contracted COVID-19 and tested
positive on December 8, 2021.  The employee was hospitalized on December 14,
2021 and subsequently died from COVID-19-related pneumonia on December 27, 2021.
Two employees were working for a car dealership when they contracted COVID-19.
Employee 1# worked as a part-time driver, was hospitalized with COVID-19, and

department, contracted COVID-19 and subsequently died on January 7, 2022. The

An employee worked as a Senior Compliance Officer for a Financail Services
Company.  During the pandemic, the employee's work permitted her to split her
time between working in the facility and telecommuting from home up until her
last day at work. The employee's last day in office was November 29, 2021. After
developing symptoms on December 1, 2021, the employee took a COVID-19 test and
received a positive result on December 2, 2021. On or about December 6, 2021,
the employee was hospitalized and later transferred to the intensive care unit
on December 19, 2021. On December 25, 2021, the employee died in the hospital

At 10:00 a.m. on July 2, 2020, an employee dug soil in the yard of residential
home. At some point, a Bobcat S70 Skid-Steer Loader operated in reverse struck
the employee. The employee was hospitalized for eight days to treat a dislocated
shoulder, de-gloving injury to the left ankle, and other unspecified injuries to
the lower legs. Five days after being discharged from the hospital, the employee
suffered a cardiac arrest at home and died.
At approximately 9:30 a.m. on November 8, 2021, an employee assessed and
inspected a motor pulley belt.  The employee reached around the guard to check
the tension of the belt while running.  The employee amputated a finger and was
treated without hospitalization.
At 6:30 a.m. on November 5, 2020, Employee #1, employed by Champion Construction
Consultants (dba Trio Construction Services), was working at an oil lease site
controlled by Crimson Resource Management Corp. The employee's supervisor was
operating a JLG G1055A telehandler to place long sections of heavy metal piping
into a trench across a road. The metal piping, which included two 2" x 60'
sections inside a larger 6" x 50' pipe, fell off the forks of the telehandler,
striking Employee #1 on the right ankle. The employee suffered a severe fracture
to the ankle. After initial treatment at Kaiser, the employee was transferred to
Adventist Health Bakersfield Hospital for admission and further care. The
incident was not reported immediately as a serious injury, and the employer
failed to comply with reporting requirements. The Division proposes one
violation related to the failure to secure the load on the telehandler properly
to prevent tipping or falling.
An employee had been working as a Corrections Officer at a City Correctional
Facility. The employee's last day worked was December 7, 2021. The employee felt
ill, did not report to work, and was tested for COVID-19, receiving a positive
test result on December 8, 2021. The employee was hospitalized on December 14,
2021, but died from renal and respiratory failure on January 2, 2022. Between
December 1, 2021, and December 8, 2021, eight coworkers at the same facility had
tested positive for COVID-19.
At 4:00 p.m. on December 26, 2021, an employee was working for a firm that
manufactured rolled steel shapes. He and a coworker were replacing a leaking
hydraulic hose on the product finishing line (PFL). The coworker left to get the
replacement hose. The employee was seen on security footage walking onto the
chamfering table and into a confined space next to the transferring mechanism to
fix the hose. The chamfering table had not been locked out by the employee or
the coworker. The chamfering table transferring mechanism cycled, and the
employee was crushed between the transferring mechanism and the rest if the
machine. Two other coworkers entered the space and lifted the employee out to
wait for the arrival of emergency services. The employee suffered a crushed
pelvis. He was hospitalized.
At 1:30 p.m. on December 6, 2021, an employee was working on an oil drilling rig
along with two coworkers. The employees worked for a well services provider
hired as a drilling contractor to drill a new oil well. A rental company was
contracted to provide Farr Canada LW 9625 9-5/8" Lightweight Casing Tongs for
running casing down into the well, as well as providing Coworker #1 who was the
equipment operator. The employee had been employed with well services provider
for approximately 4 months and his direct supervisor, Coworker #2, was present
at the site during the time. The employee was positioned towards the front of
the tongs near two open safety doors used to prevent pinch point injuries while
the equipment is in use. Coworker #1 was standing to the rear of the tongs where
the controls for operating the equipment are located. Both the employee and
Coworker #1 were engaged in handling the equipment when the employee was pulling
the tongs onto a new string of casing. The employee noticed that the jaw dies
were misaligned and so he shouted out to Coworker #1 and proceeded to push the
tongs back off the pipe. The employee was pushing with his hands on the safety
door handles. Coworker #1 actuated the lever for the tongs as the employee was
pushing back. The tongs engaged the casing causing the employee's right hand to
be jolted forward and drawn in into the pinch point on the outside of rotary
between the rungs when the ladder section broke free and fell onto the
employee's arm. The employee was taken to the hospital and admitted to treat an
arm fracture.
At 12:00 a.m. on December 1, 2021, an employee operated a compactor (Cat, Inc
CP-323C) at the edge of a dirt pile around a farm shed. At some point, the
compactor rolled over, and the employee was killed by crush injuries received by
the rollover protection system (ROPS).
At 8:00 a.m. on December 8, 2021, an employee was ripping a block of wood using
a Grizzly G1023ZX table saw when he moved the block of wood along the blade to
make the rip cut, his finger contacted the unguarded blade. The employee was
hospitalized to treat an amputation of his right index finger at the second
knuckle.
At 6:43 a.m. on December 31, 2021, an employee was loading pallets of collapsed
product boxes (Gaylords) onto a trailer of a semi truck using a ride-on pallet
jack. As the employee maneuvered a pallet into the trailer, the top corner of
one may have struck the dock seal between the trailer and the warehouse
dislodging the top box and causing it to fall. The falling box struck the
employee on the top of the head causing him to collapse to the ground. The
employee was transported to the hospital and kept overnight due to a head
injury.
At 5:30 p.m. on December 28, 2021, an employee was clearing a jam from a
Tiro-mat machine when he placed his right thumb into the machine and came into
contact with the serrated blade.  The employee partially amputated his thumb,
requiring hospitalization.
At 10:15 a.m. on November 17, 2021, an employee was bending metal pipe stock on
an Alpine pipe bending machine when he placed his hand on a pipe and began
bending it without removing his hand. The employee's finger was caught between
the machine's die and clamp and he suffered a finger amputation.  The employee
was treated without hospitalization.
An employee was working in a physician's office when she was exposed to patients
who potentially were infected with COVID-19. The employee tested positive for
COVID-19 and subsequently died on October 17, 2021.
On December 25, 2021, an employee who worked as a Trimmer Laborer for a meat
processing company died from COVID-19. The employee last worked on December 4,
2021, at which time he had not experienced any symptoms. On December 6, 2021,
the employee tested positive for COVID-19 and on December 7, 2021,  the employee
was hospitalized. The date, time and other details leading up to exposure are
not indicated in the narrative. Information regarding engineering,
administrative and personal protective equipment controls for COVID-19 are also
not included in the narrative.
At 4:30 p.m. on December 29, 2021, an employee was using a Toyokoki Model
APB-286u Press Brake to bend 1.761 inch by 11.375 inch parts the short way. The
employee was holding a part as it was being bent when he caught his left hand
ring and middle fingertips in between the die and the punch. The employee
amputated his fingertips to the bottom of the nail requiring medical treatment
without hospitalization.
On December 27, 2021, an employee who worked as an Assistant Manager at a pizza
restaurant died from complications due to COVID-19. The employee performed the
duties of a delivery driver when needed. During his shift on December 10, 2021,
while working as a delivery driver, the employee began to experience COVID-19
related symptoms. On December 11, 2021, the employee tested positive for
COVID-19. The employer did not have an effective COVID-19 Prevention Program in
place.
At 2:00 p.m. on January 4, 2022, an employee checked for leaks in a steam
boiler. As the employee attempted to exit, he was burned by the steam.   The
employee was taken to the hospital and admitted for treatment.
At 5:00 p.m. on December 20, 2021, and employee was cutting soft wood to use for
installation of new siding on an existing building, while standing on a ladder.
While holding a circular saw with his left hand, the employee cut a finger on
his right hand. The employee was hospitalized to treat a deep laceration of the
finger that required surgical amputation.
At 10:45 a.m. on October 18, 2021, an employee was cleaning chrome rollers on a
plastic extrusion machine. The employee's forearm became pinned between to
chrome rollers that were in motion. The employee suffered a crushing injury to
the forearm and was hospitalized.
At 9:25 a.m. on May 10, 2021, an employee was cleaning the rotors of a
dough-making machine at a food manufacturing facility. The employee, directed by
a supervisor to clean the machine while it was still running, used a rag and
wore gloves during the task. As the employee cleaned near the moving rotors, the
right hand was pulled between the unguarded rotors, resulting in the amputation
of the right index finger. The employee was hospitalized for one day.  The
employee was placed at the site through a staffing agency. The employer had not
provided training on lockout/tagout procedures, and the machine's moving parts
were not properly guarded. DOSH cited the employer for serious violations of
�3314(c) and �3314(l) for failure to deenergize equipment during cleaning and
for lack of employee training on hazardous energy control procedures.
At 3:30 p.m. on November 30, 2021, an employee was cleaning up a face cut on a
piece of wood. The gas powered saw kicked back, made contact with, and cut the
employee's arm. The employee was admitted and treated at the hospital for
lacerations to the right arm.
At 3:30 p.m. on January 5, 2022, an employee was installing solar panels on a
roof. The employee fell off the roof to the concrete surface below, and was
killed. The employee suffered fractures to the upper body and face.
At 8:30 a.m. on January 5, 2022, an employee was engaged in performing well
servicing operations and was exposed to fall hazards in excess of four feet
after being hoisted to the derrick board and conducting operations on or around
the pump jack head. The employee fell to the ground from a height of
approximately 30 - 40 feet and was killed.
At 7:00 a.m. on December 7, 2021, an employee was removing a manhole cover with
a coworker when the manhole cover hook slipped from the cover causing it to fall
back down. The employee's finger was caught between the cover and the manhole.
The employee was hospitalized to treat a partial amputation of his right middle
finger.
At 11:45 p.m. on Jyly 20, 2021, a an employee working as a cement pump operator
for an oil and gas well drilling contractor was operating a cement mud pump
unit. The employee was part of a crew performing a well abandonment. The
employee started running water through the pumping unit when he noticed that
water was leaking from all three of the plungers in the triplex unit. While the
plunger was still energized, the employee used an 18-inch-long rod to tighten
the packing nut on the farthest plunger. The rod slipped out of the hole in the
nut and his right hand fell in the pinch point created by the moving plunger and
the packing nut closest to him. The employee received medical treatment without
hospitalization for an amputated middle fingertip.
At 4:15 p.m. on January 4, 2022, an employee was performing a home visit to
investigate the report of a child in danger. The employee, a child protection
specialist, entered the home to perform her duties and investigate the
allegations of a child in danger, when she was attacked by an adult male with a
knife. The employee sustained multiple sharp force injuries and blunt force
trauma and was killed.
An employee had worked as a Firefighter for a City Fire Department. The employee
had been performing basic and standard firefighter duties prior to contracting
COVID-19.  On November 27, 2021, the employee tested positive for for COVID-19
and on December 21, 2021, the employee died due to complications from the
disease.
At 4:30 p.m. on January 3, 2022, an employee was preparing a mixer machine, so
he removed the pressure line hose from the interlock and blower. The employee
stood up, lost his balance, and began to fall. While reaching out to catch
himself, his left-hand middle finger slipped into a hole in the interlock guard.
The employee was hospitalized for treatment of an amputated middle fingertip.
At approximately 4:30 a.m. on November 28, 2021, an employee was cleaning the
bay of the sweeper truck into the dumpster. The employee slipped and fell onto
the right side of his ribs. He slipped more than once (twice) and continued to
work until slipped again for the third time. The employee was hospitalized to
treat these injuries.
At 10:45 a.m. on January 4, 2022, an employee attempted to access a vault. While
on a platform, the employee fell and fractured his ribs and sternum. The
employee was hospitalized for treatment.
At 8:17 a.m. on June 21, 2021, an employee was clearing a clog in a vertical
packaging machine that feeds corn chips from a hopper to individual bags when he
stopped and appeared frozen. He collapsed in front of the machine and was caught
by a coworker (the Plant Manager) who lowered him to the ground. The employee
was transported to a hospital where he later died of a fentanyl overdose.
At 2:00 p.m. on November 11, 2021, an employee was working for a firm that made
manufactured homes, or mobile homes. He was a welder or cutter. He was cutting a
12-inch (300-mm) I-beam. He was using an approved cutting torch. The operation
created sparks. The employer believed that a spark landed on the FRC
(flame-resistant clothing) jacket the employee was wearing. The jacket caught on
fire, and the employee received burns. He was hospitalized. The employer did not
and was transported to the hospital, where he was admitted to treat his
injuries.
At approximately 10:00 a.m. on February 10, 2022, an employee assisted at the
automated rebar bender, stacking the pieces as they came from the machine.  The
pieces being made were a large square pieces raised approximately 15-20 feet
from the ground. As one was finishing the bend, it caught in the machine before
falling towards the employee and striking him in the side of the face. The
employee was hospitalized to treat the injury.
At approximately 10:30 a.m. on February 8, 2022, an employee took juice samples
on top of a tanker. She was in a cage hoisted by a forklift. When the employee
got off the tanker, the cage was caught on the metal on top of the tanker truck,
and it loosened, and the cage fell to the ground and landed on the employee.
The employee sustained injuries to the left jaw, bulging right eye,
collar/shoulder broken bone, broken left arm, and wrists. The employee was
hospitalized to treat these injuries.
At 10:15 a.m. on February 7, 2022, an employee was operating a Loadmac 825
Forklift, loaded with lumber, on blacktop asphalt driveway with a 15-degree
incline. The employee was operating the forklift using the multi-directional
steer option, when the building lumber material slipped from the forks of the
forklift. The forklift lost traction and slid off the driveway onto the grass
hill, tipping the forklift.  The employee was hospitalized for treatment of a
fractured right foot.
At 2:00 p.m. on January 8, 2022, an employee, an extrusion manager, noticed that
a hopper was clogged. The employee removed a cover plate on the hopper as it was
running and placed his hand inside in an attempt manually to clear the jam when
his thumb was pinched by the auger mixing blade. The employee suffered a partial
amputation of his left thumb and was treated without hospitalization.
At 9:50 p.m. on December 22, 2021, an employee was moving a PHX Handler to the
clean room by passing through the shipping room when his right foot was got
caught underneath the caster wheel and crushed. The employee suffered a toe
fracture which got infected and resulted in hospitalization and amputation.
At approximately 10:00 a.m. on February 2, 2022, an employee assisted his
supervisor in clearing a product from a malfunctioning hopper. The employee
noticed a large rock at the bottom of the hopper and reached in, contacting the
blade.  The employee suffered a partial amputation of the left thumb and a
laceration to the left palm.  The employee was treated without hospitalization.
At 1:30 p.m. on February 8, 2022, an employee who worked as an Assistant Dietary
Manager for a Skilled Nursing Facility was hospitalized with complications of
the COVID-19. On January 23, 2022, the employee left work and began quarantining
at home that same day. The date, time and other details leading up to exposure
are not indicated in the narrative. Information regarding engineering,
administrative and personal protective equipment controls for COVID-19 are also
not included in the narrative.
At 10:45 a.m. on January 24, 2022, an employee was working for a company that
does printing and assembly to make posters, stickers, and cut-outs by printing
on cardboard or foam board.  The employee worked at the facility for 4 months
and was operating the VUTEk LX3 Pro wide format printer to print on cardboard.
Coworker #1 was about 10 feet away operating an additional printer. The employee
noticed deterioration in print quality, indicating that the material edge guides
(MEGs) that hold the cardboard in place needed cleaning. In order to clean the
MEGs, the employee must access the printer point of operation. According to
Coworker #2 (Manager) and Coworker #3 (Owner) when the MEGS needed cleaning, the
plastic cover over the printer carriage has an interlock that would shut down
the printer. The employee said he was not aware there was an interlock and it
did not work because he would often operate the printer with the cover open.
Coworker #1 said he had never seen the employee operate the printer with the
cover open. The employee said he had been told not to use the red emergency stop
button because it would require starting the print job again costing too much
time. Coworker #2 said she trained employees to hit "Pause" button when cleaning
the MEGs, allowing the job to resume after cleaning. The employee and Coworker
#1 said they had not received safety training apart from how to operate the
printer. Coworker #1 confirmed that the interlocks on the printers didn't work.
The employee stated as he was cleaning the MEGs and Coworker #1 distracted him
by tapping him on the shoulder and he failed to remove his hand from the printer
before the cartridge struck his right arm. Coworker #1 denied tapping the
employee on the shoulder. The employee's right forearm was dragged by the
carriage and the impact removed the skin and muscle. The employee admitted to
the hospital for one week before being transferred to another hospital for a
month, where he underwent surgery.
At 9:00 a.m. on February 14, 2022, an employee was installing a stick cylinder
to the boom arm of an excavator. The stick cylinder was hoisted by a 5-ton crane
and the employee was installing the eye end of the stick on the bracket of the
boom arm. The employee on the floor level, was installing the pin when the crane
started to lift up and tilt the boom arm towards the employee. The employee
tried to get away but hit a utility cart the boom arm struck him in both shins.
The employee was hospitalized to treat fractures to both legs.
At 12:00 noon on January 28, 2022, an employee was operating a Hydrogen
Induction Bracing machine when an explosion occurred. The employee was
hospitalized for treatment of burns.
At 12:00 p.m. on February 5, 2022, an employee and a coworker were attempting to
lower the wings of the spring tooth they had just moved to another ranch. While
trying to lower the first wing, the employee got onto the spring tooth to try
and assist with slightly lifting the wing as the coworker was pulling the pin.
The employee tried lifting the wing instead of actuating the hydraulics for
raising the wing. As the coworker removed the pin, the wing unexpectedly shifted
down and the rope attached to the wing became taunt. At the time, the employee
had one of his hands resting on a metal bar when the taunt rope pinched his
fingers against the metal bar. A couple of the employee's left hand fingers were
amputated.  The employee was hospitalized.
At 8:30 a.m. on February 8, 2022, an employee was working at a motor vehicle
dealership. The firm sold trucks. He worked as a mechanic or automotive
technician. He was removing an exhaust assembly from a Kenworth T6-80 diesel
truck. An exhaust clamp came into contact with a damaged fitting and dislodged
the fitting. The employee was sprayed in the mouth with Roadforce Heavy Duty
extended life antifreeze/coolant. He ingested some of the coolant. He became
nauseous, and he began vomiting. He was hospitalized.
At approximately 6:30 a.m. on February 12, 2022, an employee was loading a part
into CNC SL75 (mach # 808) The employee's thumb was caught in a nip point
created when the auto clamping chuck jaws prematurely activated (closed) through

sustained a partial amputation of the right thumb and was hospitalized to treat

The employee was hospitalized.
At 1:00 a.m. on September 4, 2021, an employee working as a machinist for a
commercial bakery was cleaning the Line 3 kettle pump. The employee had his left
hand inside the energized pump when it was struck by a moving part. The employee
was hospitalized to treat an amputated middle fingertip.
At 1:33 p.m. on October 27, 2021, an employee was operating a John Deere Model
5115ML tractor to remove and haul almond trees and limbs that had blown over on
a farm.  The task consisted of chaining the tree or limbs to the tractor and
dragging them to the shop and yard area to pile them up. The employee had
performed this task for approximately two weeks.  The employee had placed the
tractor into neutral before descending from it, but he inadvertently pressed
down on the lever under the steering wheel which allows the tractor to be placed
into neutral, forward or reverse without having to engage the clutch. When the
employee pushed the level down, it caused the tractor to go into reverse,
catching his leg by the front left tire and pulling him under the tractor.  A
coworker nearby did not directly witness the incident but did observe the
employee crawling out from the tractor which was in reverse and had come to rest
against a metal post.  The employee sustained fractures of the thoracic and
lumbar vertebras, liver laceration, right knee pain, fractured ribs and a
fractured left clavicle. The employee was taken to the regional medical center,
where he was hospitalized and later released on October 31, 2021.
An employee had worked as the Director of Maintenance for a Metropolitan
Transportation Authority. The employee performed his job duties inside his
office via zoom, phone and computer. The employee socially distanced from
everyone and had minimal contact with coworkers at the facility. The employee's
last day at the work was February 4, 2022. The employee developed COVID-19
related symptoms on February 7, 2022. On February 8, 2022, the employee was
tested and admitted to the hospital. There were no known exposures to COVID-19
On October 24, 2021, an employee who worked in an unspecified job for a cancer c
enter was hospitalized for treatement of COVID-19. On the same day, the employee

rk was October 22, 2021. The facility only offers outpatient services and does n

At 3:00 p.m. on February 4, 2022, an employee worked to install an HVAC system
and was running conduit in a room. At the end of the shift, coworkers went to
look for the employee who was found unresponsive and lying on the floor. The
coworkers-initiated CPR and called for emergency response. The employee was
killed by possible, unspecified natural cause.
At 10:36 a.m. on February 3, 2022, Employee #1 responded to a help call from an
inmate in the housing area. The inmate was allowed to exit the housing area and
struggled with Employee #1. A coworker assisted Employee #1 with the inmate,
when the inmate ran back into the housing area. Employee #1 and the coworker
pursued the inmate and a help call was placed for other correctional officers.
The inmate was sprayed with pepper spray, which also contacted Employee #1 on
the arm. Shortly thereafter, Employee #1 went to her sergeant's office, and said
she needed to catch her breath. A medical call for a correctional officer was

experience a rapid heart rate and difficulty breathing. EMS was called, and
Employee #1 was transported to the hospital, where she died shortly after
arrival.
On September 29, 2021, Employee #1 died from illness due to COVID-19 infection.
At 5:22 a.m. on November 19, 2021, an employee was walking in a parking lot when
a twenty-six foot box truck struck her and ran her over. The employee was
walking in the rear parking lot of the facility. A coworker was driving the box
truck across the parking lot from a bay and drove past two parked box trucks.
The coworker also drove outside the lanes of traffic and across marked parking
spaces while looking into the right mirror of the truck. He did not see the
employee before striking her with the truck and running her over and killing
her.
At 12:30 p.m. on January 21, 2022, Employee #1 and two coworkers were trying to
realign a bale of recycled plastic bottles that was turned wrong, causing the
declumper (blades) to jam on the Debaler machine (Serial  Number 1533.10.0603,
Model Number BBU .90). The bale was approximately 64 inches in length, height
was 30 inches, and width was 47.48 inches. The bale's weight was approximately
1000 to 1400 pounds.  As Employee #1 and another coworker were trying to turn
the bale, the conveyor belt and blades were still moving. A half of a blade
diameter was approximately eight and a half inches, and five inches in width.
The piece of the blade that stuck out and actually dug into the bales to sort
plastic bottles into pieces was approximately an inch and a fourth of an inch.
After approximately 15 - 20 minutes of trying to clear the jam, Employee #1 and
another coworker started to turn the bale. Employee #1 was on the side of the
bale that was closest to the blades (declumper). Employee #1 contacted the
blades (declumper). Employee #1's clothing was loose and the blades (declumper)
caught the clothing, and Employee #1's foot was caught in the blades

four rows of blades at the declumper, and Employee #1 was caught within the
first two. A coworker ran to the emergency stop button on the Debaler operator's
control panel and hit the E-Stop button and also pulled the Emergency Cord near
the declumper.  Employee #1 was killed at the scene due to crushing and chopping
injuries to the lower extremities.
At 3:30 p.m. on December 20, 2021, an employee was melting icicles with a heat
gun, when he became unresponsive and set on fire.  He was pronounced dead on
December 21, 2021.
At 12:45 a.m. on February 5, 2022, an employee was waiting for his coworker to

was later found to be unresponsive. The employee had diabetes and was believed
to be suffering from low blood sugar levels at the time the incident occurred.
At 8:30 a.m. on December 14, 2021, an employee worked on a roof cutting
insulation board. The employee maintained a foot on the board while cutting that
section, the heater fell, struck the ladder the employee was on, and caused both
to fall. The employee struck his head on the floor and was hospitalized to treat
multiple brain contusions, and a severe traumatic brain injury from blunt force
trauma to the head. The employee died five days later from their injuries.
At 2:34 p.m. on January 19, 2022, an employee was working in the engine
compartment of a concrete truck servicing the transmission and working with

At 5:00 a.m. on January 19, 2022, an employee was walking when he slipped on ice
and struck the ground. The employee tore his rotator cuff, requiring medical
treatment without hospitalization.
At approximately 8:45 p.m. on February 11, 2022, an employee was trying to get a
chain loose and the chain became tight.  Then,  it amputated the fingers at the
pinch point.  The employee was hospitalized to treat these injuries.
At 10:00 a.m. on February 8, 2022, an employee was informed that a conveyor belt
was not working properly, he proceeded to inspect the machine to identify the
issue.  The employee went inside the machine's drive motor and drive belt
section when the machine started moving, amputating his right pinky finger. The
employee was hospitalized for treatment.
At 1:00 p.m. on February 16, 2022, an employee was operating a stand-up
forklift. The employee, not looking in the direction of travel, struck a
guardrail and overcorrected, striking the end of another guardrail. The employee
suffered a severe laceration of his lower leg when it struck against the

employee.  He walked up multiple flights of stairs to access a coker unit

brackets. The employee slipped due to damp conditions of the morning and fell

to hook to a truck. The employee was caught between the trailer (Drake Trailer)

At 12:30 p.m. on January 19, 2022, an employee attempted to descend an extension
ladder, when the ladder's feet gave way and the employee fell approximately six

both ankles.
At 10:00 a.m. on February 24, 2022, an employee was working for a firm that
manufactured wood containers and pallets. He was operating a West Plains Resaw

With his hands, he was moving sawdust into the vacuum collection system located
in the collector box. His finger came into contact with the sawblade, which was
located above the collector box. He suffered the amputation of a portion of his
hand. He was hospitalized. There were no machine-specific procedures for locking
out the slab edger.
At 8:25 a.m. on November 10, 2021, an employee was working as an associate at a
big box retailer of hardware and lumber. She was attempting to operate a riding

authorized to operate the lift equipment. The manager was not around. The
employee hit the throttle too quickly. She tried to slow or stop the pallet jack
by stepping off the machine while it was in operation. Her right foot was pinned
between the pallet jack and some cantilever racking. She suffered fractures of
her metatarsal bones. She was hospitalized.

them with new cyclones. Employees were cutting the old cyclones into smaller
pieces and pushing them off of a platform approximately 40 feet 10 inches above
the floor. Employee #1 was working as the spotter and was struck by a fallen
piece of metal and died due to generalized blunt force trauma.  Employee #1 was
killed.

a fire at a chicken ranch farm. An employee, a firefighter, was advancing the
hose line, when an explosion occurred. The other firefighters immediately gave
CPR until the employee was life-flighted to OHSU, where shortly thereafter he
was pronounced dead.

Employee #1 to the hospital, where Employee #1 was pronounced dead.

panels. The employee fell through the roof insulation.  The employee was killed

ground.

left middle finger tip just below the first knuckle. The employee was
hospitalized.
At approximately 6:00 a.m. on February 14, 2022, an employee worked an
instrument and an electronic technician was burnt by gushing high-temperature
steam from a faulty flow control valve (FCV), which he was approaching.
Maintenance personnel and operation specialists were trying to check  and
repair/replace a flow control valve attached to a reboiler used in a chemical
process facility. The pressurized valve operation was monitored and operated
remotely by a control room specialist while a coworker was observing the actual
operation of the valve standing close to it. The communication between these
employees was done through radios.  The radio communication did not work
properly, and the computer in the control room did not indicate the correct
pressure build-up inside the FCV that was being monitored. A sudden stream from
the FCV relief directed to a shallow ditch reflected back on the employee
walking toward the valve. It was noted that the proper lockout tagout procedures
had not been followed.  The employee  was hospitalized for over 24 hours to
treat burn blisters in the right calf.

firm that made pressure treated lumber products. He was working with a stacker

hospitalized.

machine energized while the employee was reaching inside to clear the jam and
caught the employee's hand and finger. The employee suffered a fracture,
degloving of a finger and was hospitalized.

At 5:20 p.m. on August 3, 2021, an employee at a pallet construction site was

position. While reaching into the saw with his right hand, the saw blade

An employee worked for a City public transportation agency performing Parking
Enforcement Officer related duties. The employee's last day at work was July 16,

COVID-19. The employee worked as a Parking Enforcement Officer which entailed

she rarely interacted with the public.  The Employer provides face masks, face

The employee did not attend the wedding. The Employer provided tools to protect

At 11:30 a.m. on August 6, 2021, an employee working as a food batchmaker for a
manufacturer of tomato products was retrieving an item from a racking system.
The employee fell and landed on his arm. The employee was hospitalized to treat
a broken wrist.
At 8:00 a.m. on August 5, 2021, an employee was working as a mill operator for a
custom metal fabrication shop was milling a custom aluminum part in the
production area. The employee had worked for the employer for over 6 years. The
employee was operating a HAAS CNC Model VF-0 Vertical Mill (Serial 23309). When
he reached into the mill to adjust a part, the employee contacted the rotating
spindle. The employee was hospitalized to treat a partially amputated right
index finger.
At 1:15 p.m. on August 3, 2021, an employee was measuring a piece of stone while
standing in the "fall shadow" of the stone at a work site. The stone was
unsecured and tipped over, landing on the employee's leg and causing a fracture.
The employee was hospitalized for the treatment of this injury.
At 6:00 a.m. on August 9, 2021, an employee was responding to a chlorine leak
when he accidentally walked into a chlorine gas cloud. This exposure resulted in
pulmonary edema. The employee was hospitalized for treatment of the condition.
An employee was working in an outpatient medical clinic when she was infected
with COVID-19 which required hospitalization for treatment on July 28, 2021. The
employee successfully recovered from her infection.
At 11:30 a.m. on March 22, 2021, an employee was working on the Nothum breader.
The employee either tapped the Nothum breader with a screwdriver or with his
hand to unclog the breading while the machine was running. The employee was
wearing a cotton glove that got caught in the chain. The employee suffered a
partial amputation to the left middle finger and was treated without
hospitalization.
Two employees were working as assemblers for a firm that made batteries. They
worked in a battery assembly area. They contracted COVID-19, and they died at
1:30 p.m. on August 8, 2021.
At 12:30 p.m. on August 9, 2021, an employee was operating and monitoring a
swager machine when two pieces of rebar were fed into the gripper vise
simultaneously, which is designed to hold only one piece at a time. As the
employee reached to remove the second piece of rebar, his left ring and middle
fingers were caught in the gripper vise, resulting in fingertip amputations. The
employee was hospitalized for treatment.
At 1:00 p.m. on August 5, 2021, an employee working as an assembler for a farm
and garden machinery and equipment manufacturer was putting stiffeners on the
side of a dryer she was assembling. The employee was standing on a 6-foot ladder
when she noticed a nut missing from one of the stiffeners. The employee was was
attempting to replace the bolt when she fell from the ladder to the concrete
floor below. The employee was hospitalized to treat a broken leg from impact
with the concrete floor.
At 9:30 a.m. on August 8, 2021, an employee used a ladder to access an elevated
area to attempt to level a new overhead screw conveyor. At some point, the
employee fell approximately twelve feet, received a severe head injury, and was
killed.
At 12:15 p.m. on July 15, 2021, Employee #1 was climbing a ladder to hang a
metal string for a tarp when the ladder slipped. The employee fell onto the
concrete floor, sustaining a broken right leg. Emergency services transported
Employee #1 to the hospital, where he was admitted and treated.
At 10:30 a.m. on August 10, 2021, an employee was getting out of his work truck
when two trucks were in a accident on the roadway. One of the trucks in the
accident got pushed into the employee pinning him between it and his truck. The
employee suffered multiple fractures and internal injuries and subsequently
died.
At 7:15 a.m. on June 15, 2021, an employee working for a metal pipe and tube
manufacturer was utilizing a horizontal bandsaw to cut iron pipe. The employee
had already cut a few pieces and had stacked them on the table attached to the
At 12:00 a.m. on June 28, 2021, an employee conducted a roofing inspection to
identify a potential leak from a condensate line. The employee became ill
shortly after coming down off the roof and collapsed. The employee was taken to
the hospital to treat a heat illness and later died.
At approximately 10:00 a.m. on June 24, 2021, an employee was driving a John
Deere Turf Gator across Shumway Road to the employer's dump site when struck by
a vehicle traveling on Shumway Road. The employee was ejected from the turf
vehicle and sustained multiple head injuries, including fractures and
hemorrhaging. The employee was admitted to intensive care for treatment.
At 2:00 p.m. on Jul 28, 2021, an employee was on his second day on the job when
he said he felt dizzy and asked for a break. The employee walked to a nearby
sidewalk and collapsed. A coworker waiting to pull his truck into the facility
say the employee collapse and called for help. The employee died of possible
presexisting health conditions with possible exacerbation from the high heat
index that day.
At 6:50 p.m. on February 7, 2021, an employee working as an extrusion operator
for a food packaging product manufacturer was working in the extrusion building.
In this building, styrene is forced through an extrusion die, a laminate is
applied, and then the product is rolled into large segments for transportation
to a holding area. There were two temporary labor agencies on site which were
not involved in the incident. The employee was performing the string up process
on the line 507 laminator. During this process, the employee feeds sheets of
styrene and laminate from large rolls into the laminator machine. The employer's
procedure for the laminator instructs the operator to place the heat roller in
the elevated position during the string up process. The employee was feeding the
material through the laminating heat roller with the roller in the down
position. The employee's gloved hand was pulled into the nip point between two
rollers. The employee stated that he initially thought the heat roller was in
the elevated position but didn't realize it was down until it was too late. The
employee had received crushing injuries to his right hand middle and ring
fingers. The employee was hospitalized and released the next morning after being
referred to a hand specialist.
At 12:00 noon on July 20, 2021, an employee was performing one-on-one monitoring
duties of a youth client when he was attacked by the client. Medical staff at
the facility began providing aid to the employee while coworkers called for
emergency services. Paramedics arrived and transported the employee to a local
medical center for treatment. The employee subsequently died from his injuries.
At approximately 8:00 a.m. on April 27, 2021, an employee was in the process of
emptying a commercial dumpster. While positioning the dumpster for disposal, the
employee placed his hand between the dumpster and the truck. As a result, the
employee's right finger was caught and amputated. The employee was hospitalized
for treatment.
An employee was working as an engineer in an aerospace engineering facility when
he was exposed to COVID-19 by a coworker. The employee developed symptoms of
COVID-19 and was hospitalized on June 13, 2021 for 10 days until his discharge.
At 1:45 p.m. on July 23, 2021, an employee worked from a ladder to install a
glass panel during the construction of a glass wall. At some point, the employee
experienced a possible cardiac event, fell approximately three feet from the
ladder, and was killed.
At 12:30 p.m. on July 29, 2021, an employee was using a Hyster forklift with
clamp attachment to unload a semi trailer of recycled baled cardboard. The
employee was attempting to reinstall the mast chain pin back into the cylinder
when the elevated mast fell and crushed him. The employee incurred multiple
broken bones and head injuries and was killed.
At 5:15 p.m. on July 13, 2021, Employee #1 was loading a tube into a CNC lathe
machine when the magnetic lifting attachment released. The tube fell and pinched
the employee's left index finger between the tube and the tail stock cone,
resulting in amputation of the fingertip. Emergency services transported the
employee to the hospital for admission and treatment.
At 1:15 p.m. on July 29, 2021, an employee working as a welder for a petroleum
refinery was taking measurements for a 3-inch pipe repair on a pressurized acid
line. The pressurized acid line consisted of a 3/4-inch threadolet, a 3/4-inch
bleeder pipe and a 3/4-inch valve. Sulfuric acid was leaking from a 3/4-inch
Threadolet fitting. The line gave way spraying acid onto the employee. The
employee was hospitalized to treat acid burns to his torso from the waist down
including his legs and both hands.
At 11:30 a.m. on May 30, 2021, an employee working as a buyer for a furniture
store was exiting the women's restroom as a coworker, the assistant store
manager, was entering. The door opened inwards and knocked the employee to the
floor. The employee backed up to avoid being struck with the door and fell. The
employee was hospitalized to treat a fractured hip.
At 10:43 a.m. on February 11, 2021, an employee was polishing parts on a Burr
King three-wheel grinder while deburring. During this process, a fire started
from the hose connected to the grinder's dust collector spark arrestor. The fire
caused burns to the employee's shoulder and ear. The employee was treated
without hospitalization. The incident highlights the importance of ensuring
proper maintenance and safety checks on dust collection systems to prevent fire
hazards during grinding operations.
At 6:48 a.m. on June 2, 2021, Employee #1, a facilities maintenance mechanic at
a golf equipment manufacturing warehouse, was working with a team to install LED
lighting between industrial racks. While descending in an order picker (Crown
#30SP36TT), Employee #1 placed his left hand on a horizontal steel lighting bar.
As the order picker lowered, his hand was caught between the overhead protection
cage and the steel bar, fracturing his left middle and ring fingers. Employee #1
was admitted to the hospital and treated for distal fractures, contusions, and
bruises to the fingers. The incident was witnessed by two coworkers.
Six employees worked for a facility that houses individuals with developmental
and intellectual disabilities.  All six contracted COVID-19 and died.  Employee
#1 who worked in an unspecified capacity for the facility died on March 29,
2020. Employee #2, who worked as a Direct Care Assistant died on April 3 or
April 4, 2020. Employee #3 who worked in an unspecified capacity for the
facility died on April 11, 2020. Employee #4 who worked as a Developmental
Assistant 3 died on April 18, 2020. Employee #5 who worked in an unspecified
capacity for the facility died on April 20, 2020. And Employee #6 who worked as
a Nurse died on June 21, 2020. The employer did not have an adequate Respiratory
Protection Program in place.
At 12:45 a.m. on July 29, 2021, an employee was removing bracing from a load of
granite slabs when the slabs began to shift and pinned him underneath them. The
employee died of asphyxiation before slabs could be lifted off of him.
At 8:30 a.m. on May 5, 2021, Employee #1, a machine operator, completed a cycle
on a molding machine and reached into the point of operation to retrieve the
drilling for the connection of two underground vaults. An employer adjacent to
the construction site was testing the fire alarm system for a spray booth.
During the testing, the CO2 fire suppression system unexpectedly released.  The
roll-up door was partially opened, and during the discharge the CO2 fumes which
allowed them to escape the building.  The CO2 then entered the underground vault
where Employee #1 was working and engulfed the working area.  Employee #1 was
removed from the vault and hospitalized.
An employee was working for a performing arts company. He worked as an
attraction attendant at a laser tag maze. He was exposed to SARS-CoV-2 while at
work, and he contracted COVID-19. At 11:45 p.m. on August 9, 2021, he died.

responsibilities was verifying maintenance work on a freezer bar machine. While
feeling the alignment of an air-driven stamper component that stamps the time

stamper and a fixed part of the machine after an assistant mechanic adjusted an
air valve. The employee sustained an amputation of the tip of the middle finger
on the right hand. The injury required hospitalization.
An employee was working at a general medical or surgical hospital. She worked as
a patient sitter. She had allegedly been exposed to a COVID-positive patient on

returned to work. She called in to quit on July 22nd. The employer had not been
aware that the employee had contracted COVID, that she had symptoms of COVID, or
if or when she was hospitalized. She died on or about August 1, 2021. Her
employer learned of her death when the health department notified the hospital
on August 11, 2021.
At 9:49 a.m. on July 30, 2021, an employee was pruning trees when he fell 4 feet
from a ladder. A coworker called 911 and provided CPR until paramedics arrived.
Paramedics provided CPR for about 30 minutes before the employee was pronounced
dead due to a heart attack.
At 1:00 a.m. on July 17, 2021, an employee was found laying on the ground by his

At 9:15 a.m. on September 11, 2021, an employee was closing a 20-yard roll-off

The employee fell to the poured concrete basement floor and suffered injuries to

that was in operation. Emergency services transported Employee #1 to the
hospital, where he was admitted and treated for a right shoulder injury.
At 2:30 p.m. on May 5, 2021, Employee #1, assisting with the unloading of a
1,300-pound crated HVAC unit, was hand signaling to guide the forklift operator.
The forklift operator failed to position the forklift forks deep enough into the
load, causing it to become unbalanced as it was moved off the trailer. As the
load began to tip, the employee rushed to the left side of the load in an
attempt to balance it with his hands. However, the load ultimately fell on the
employee, causing fractures to his left arm and left leg. Emergency services
were called, and the employee was transported to the hospital for admission and
treatment.

At 12:00 p.m. on August 28, 2021, an employee working as a firefighter and

At 12:45 p.m. on September 23, 2021, an employee was working for a firm that

left, fast lane of the highway. The driver was late in making his exit from the
freeway, and he cut across two lanes of traffic. He drove across the "gore
area," striking the employee. The employee was killed.
At 2:45 p.m. on September 8, 2021, Employee #1 was performing electrical work at
an airport facility. He was troubleshooting a 4,400-volt transformer for an
airfield sign. He radioed to the tower to cut electrical power to the sign. He

untangle it. Employee #1 was electrocuted and killed when he came into contact

hospitalized to treat a fractured and bruised leg and bruising.

in the hospital at 11:00 p.m. on September 24, 2021, due to respiratory issues
related to COVID-19.

had used a lifter to set down a load of 2-in. by 64-in. (51-mm by 1.63-m) plates
onto an existing 6 in.-high (153-mm-high) stack of 2-in. by 60-in. (51-mm by
1.52-m) plates. The UPA said that the employee was unhooking the steel stack
from the lifter to have the plates picked up by a suction lifter when the top
plate shifted and fell. The sheet slid down and struck the supervisor's left
foot, fracturing the metatarsal bones in the employee's foot. The employee was
taken to a nearby hospital and admitted for treatment and surgery. The narrative
said that the employee removed the crane hook from the lifting device and
operated the crane toward the south. When the lifting device was removed, it was
not properly set on its base. When the crane was moved, the lifting device
tipped toward the employee, causing the fracture. This movement was in part due
to the different dimensions of the plates. In any event, the employee was
hospitalized.

prevent kickback when he contacted the blade with his left hand. The employee
was hospitalized to treat amputations to his middle and index fingers and a
laceration to his thumb.
An employee was working in Enclosure #4.  A coworker tested positive for
COVID-19 and the employee was exposed to SARS CoV-2 by an infected coworker.
The employee died from complications from the virus at approximately 2:00 a.m.
on September 12, 2021.

experiencing symptoms of COVID-19 on July 28, 2021. The employee went to the

quarantined at home until his symptoms worsened, and he was hospitalized on

company name on the product and presses a rubber seal into place. The machine

brake press at a manufacturing facility. He was feeding sheet metal into the

amputation of his right index finger and possible crushed knuckles on both
hands. The employee was hospitalized for treatment.

The employee was near the west end of the south pre-weld area in the small parts
cleaning and finishing department when struck by a powered industrial vehicle
(PIV). A coworker operating the PIV had driven forward, executed a U-turn at the

coworker failed to maintain a clear view of the travel path and did not see the
employee, who was facing away from the vehicle. The employee entered the PIV's
path approximately three feet behind it and was struck on the left leg. The
employee sustained an avulsion injury and was hospitalized.

performing rigging down during well servicing. The employee heard a loud sound
of the clevis striking an item in the derrick causing him to leave his current
position to investigate. For unknown reasons, the employee slipped on the rig
floor and fell into the drum area. Nothing was found to have struck the employee
from above or from the rig floor and their was no height involved in the fall.
But the employee was killed due to blunt force trauma.

At 3:45 p.m. on September 3, 2021, an employee working as a mixing and blending

hands away from the splitter wedge. After the employee turned the equipment on

his fingertip between the wedge and the wood. It takes approximately 5 seconds
for the wedge to reach the wood. The wedge travels slowly before eventually
splitting the wood with downward force. Due to the slow motion of the wedge, the
employee was not sure why he did not pull his finger out of the way before the
wedge reached his finger. The employee stated the reason his finger was severed

split apart. He held the tree trunk at its back side which was close to the
splitting wedge path. Placing his hand in a different location might have
prevented the injury. In addition, push sticks, push blocks or other extension
tools were not available for use. Warning signs were posted on the apparatus not
to put any part of the body in the way of the splitting wedge path. The employee
was hospitalized to treat an amputated fingertip.
